stb-2Dstacking.help:
usage: stb-2Dstacking [-h] -l1 LAYER1 -l2 LAYER2 [-a MAX_AREA] [-s MAX_STRAIN]
                      [-i | -id MATCH_ID] [--batch_sym]
                      [-g GAP | --gap_range START END STEPS] [--vacuum VACUUM]
                      [-t TWIST] [-tx SHIFT_X] [-ty SHIFT_Y] [-sm {top,bottom,sym}]
                      [-o OUTPUT] [-sp SYMPREC] [--save-report] [--view] [--ml-relax]
                      [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                      [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-v] [--no-intro]

STB Monolayer Stacking Tool with Geometric Control & Symmetry Analysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l1 LAYER1, --layer1 LAYER1
                        Path to the bottom monolayer .fdf file
  -l2 LAYER2, --layer2 LAYER2
                        Path to the top monolayer .fdf file
  -a MAX_AREA, --max_area MAX_AREA
                        Maximum supercell area (default: 150.0)
  -s MAX_STRAIN, --max_strain MAX_STRAIN
                        Maximum allowed strain fraction (default: 0.05)
  -i, --interactive     Interactive mode: shows table to select match ID
  -id MATCH_ID, --match_id MATCH_ID
                        Directly select a specific match ID (default: 0)
  --batch_sym           Generate all high-symmetry stackings automatically
  -g GAP, --gap GAP     Van der Waals gap in Angstroms (default: 3.2)
  --gap_range START END STEPS
                        Range for energy curve. Ex: 2.5 4.5 11
  --vacuum VACUUM       Target vacuum space in Angstroms. Inherits L1 by default.
  -t TWIST, --twist TWIST
                        Twist angle of layer 2 in degrees (default: 0.0)
  -tx SHIFT_X, --shift_x SHIFT_X
                        Fractional shift of layer 2 in X (default: 0.0)
  -ty SHIFT_Y, --shift_y SHIFT_Y
                        Fractional shift of layer 2 in Y (default: 0.0)
  -sm {top,bottom,sym}, --strain_mode {top,bottom,sym}
                        Strain distribution mode (default: top)
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf base file name
  -sp SYMPREC, --symprec SYMPREC
                        Symmetry tolerance in Angstroms (default: 0.01)
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_2dstacking_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view of the final heterostructure(s) (via ASE) after writing the output file(s). Needs a display. Off by default.
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax each generated heterostructure with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) before writing it out -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the in-plane cell -- the vacuum axis (c) always stays exactly fixed. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb_stacking -l1 bottom.fdf -l2 top.fdf -i
  stb_stacking -l1 bottom.fdf -l2 top.fdf --batch_sym -g 3.2

stb-adsorb.help:
usage: stb-adsorb [-h] [-s STRUCTURE] [-c CALC] [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                  [--adsorbate ADSORBATE] [--list]
                  [--site-type {ontop,bridge,hollow,all}] [--site-index SITE_INDEX]
                  [--all-sites] [--position X Y] [--positions-file PATH]
                  [--height HEIGHT] [--height-sweep MIN MAX STEP] [--both-sides]
                  [--symprec SYMPREC] [--force-spin] [--no-force-spin]
                  [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX] [--ml-prerelax]
                  [--ml-rank] [--ml-model {small,medium,large}]
                  [--ml-custom-model PATH] [--ml-device {cpu,cuda}]
                  [--ml-fmax ML_FMAX] [--ml-steps ML_STEPS] [--top-k TOP_K]
                  [--n-orientations-polar N_ORIENTATIONS_POLAR]
                  [--n-orientations-azimuthal N_ORIENTATIONS_AZIMUTHAL]
                  [--orientation-top-k ORIENTATION_TOP_K]
                  [--orientation-rmsd-tol ORIENTATION_RMSD_TOL] [-O OUTPUT_DIR]
                  [--save-report] [--view] [--view-plots] [-v] [--no-intro]

Prepares SIESTA folders for an adsorption-energy study: a clean slab/2D material, an isolated adsorbate, and one folder per candidate adsorption site.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input slab/2D structure.fdf (vacuum along c). Default: structure.fdf.
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template already configured for the slab (kgrid, basis, XC, %include structure.fdf, etc.) -- copied as-is into 'clean_slab/' and every 'sites/site_*/' folder (same lattice, so the same k-grid applies to all of them); a Gamma-only, spin-polarized derivative goes into 'adsorbate/'. A config_extra.fdf sidecar is %included on top, forcing MD.VariableCell false (see [1]/[4] in the report). Default: calc.fdf.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank or a folder path.
  --adsorbate ADSORBATE
                        Element symbol (single atom) or ASE G2 molecule name (e.g. H2O, CO2, CH4). Comma-separated for more than one (e.g. 'O,N,C') -- the same site search runs once per adsorbate, useful for comparing binding affinity across species at the same site(s).
  --list                List the available G2 molecule names and exit.
  --site-type {ontop,bridge,hollow,all}
                        Which family of adsorption sites to search (default: ontop).
  --site-index SITE_INDEX
                        Which symmetrically distinct site of --site-type to use, 0-based (default: 0). Ignored with --all-sites or --position.
  --all-sites           Write one folder per symmetrically distinct site of --site-type, instead of just --site-index.
  --position X Y        Manual Cartesian (X, Y) position in Ang, overriding automatic site-finding entirely (--site-type/--site-index/--all-sites are ignored when this is given).
  --positions-file PATH
                        '.dat' file with one or more adsorption site positions, as in-plane fractional (a, b) coordinates relative to the file's own LATTICE_A/LATTICE_B/LATTICE_C lines ('number type frac_a frac_b' per site line; '#' comments and blank lines ignored) -- used INSTEAD of automatic site-finding (--site-type/--symprec are ignored). --all-sites/--site-index then select among the file's positions exactly as they would among auto-found ones. stb-adsorb always writes 'sites/site_positions.dat' with the lattice and positions actually used this run (auto-found or manual alike), in the same format, so it can be inspected, hand-edited, and fed back here for a future run. Mutually exclusive with --position and --both-sides.
  --height HEIGHT       Adsorption distance in Ang above the surface (default: 2.0). Ignored if --height-sweep is given.
  --height-sweep MIN MAX STEP
                        Generate one site per height in this range (inclusive), instead of a single fixed --height -- an approach-curve scan. stb-adsorbAnalysis will report E_ads vs. height for it. Same min/max/step convention as stb-convergence. Incompatible with --both-sides.
  --both-sides          Adsorb on both exposed faces (for a free-standing 2D material with vacuum on both sides of the c-axis). Requires a concrete --site-type (not 'all'); incompatible with --position, --ml-rank and --height-sweep.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-reduction tolerance for site-finding (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default).
  --force-spin          Force Spin polarized (via config_extra.fdf, overriding --calc's own Spin tag if any) in every 'sites/site_*/' folder too, not just the isolated-adsorbate reference (default: ON) -- a single adsorbate atom (or a molecule containing one) bonded to a slab commonly leaves the combined system with a net magnetic moment (most simply, an odd total valence-electron count, which a spin-restricted calculation cannot represent at all). Costs nothing for a genuinely closed-shell site (converges to zero moment). Does not affect 'clean_slab/' (no adsorbate present).
  --no-force-spin       Leave --calc's own Spin tag untouched in 'sites/site_*/' (the isolated-adsorbate reference is still always forced polarized).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum-axis detection threshold in Ang, used to validate the input's vacuum axis is c (default: 10.0), same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-slab.
  --vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX
                        Cubic box side (Ang) for the isolated-adsorbate reference calculation (default: 20.0).
  --ml-prerelax         Relax the isolated adsorbate's geometry (positions only) with MACE-MP-0 before writing its reference folder -- same idea as stb-phononsCreate --ml-prerelax. Mainly useful for adsorbates whose starting geometry isn't already at equilibrium (e.g. a hand-built one rather than an ASE G2 entry, which already is). Needs the optional 'ml' extra.
  --ml-rank             Pre-screen candidate sites with a MACE-MP-0 relax (substrate fixed, only the adsorbate moves) before writing SIESTA folders, ranking by relaxed energy -- a fast pre-screen for which site(s) to prioritize for real DFT, not a replacement for stb-adsorbAnalysis. Needs the optional 'ml' extra. Only valid with --all-sites.
  --ml-model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size for --ml-prerelax/--ml-rank: speed/accuracy tradeoff (default: medium). Ignored if --ml-custom-model is given.
  --ml-custom-model PATH
                        Use a custom MACE model file for --ml-prerelax/--ml-rank instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --ml-model.
  --ml-device {cpu,cuda}
  --ml-fmax ML_FMAX
  --ml-steps ML_STEPS   Max MACE-MP-0 optimizer steps per relax, for both --ml-prerelax and --ml-rank (default: 200). Raise it if a candidate is reported as not converged; lower it to speed up screening a large number of sites/orientations at the cost of less-relaxed rankings.
  --top-k TOP_K         With --ml-rank: only write SIESTA folders for the N best-ranked sites, instead of all of them. Counts SITES, not orientations -- if orientation sampling is also on, every already --orientation-top-k-kept orientation of each of the N selected sites is written, so the number of folders can exceed N.
  --n-orientations-polar N_ORIENTATIONS_POLAR
                        With --ml-rank and a multi-atom --adsorbate: systematically sample this many initial molecule orientations PER SITE before relaxing -- which part of the molecule ends up facing the surface (e.g. O-down vs. H-down for H2O) is otherwise fixed by the molecule's default G2 geometry alone. Default 1 = current behavior, no sampling. Combined with --n-orientations-azimuthal below (total orientations per site = polar x azimuthal); a modest 4x2=8 is a reasonable starting point -- cost scales linearly with this product (one full MACE relax per orientation per site). Works with a single --site-index too, not just --all-sites -- every sampled orientation of the SAME site is then what gets ranked. Every relaxed orientation (not just the kept/unique ones) is saved to sites/orientation_trajectory.xyz as a multi-frame trajectory (viewable in VMD/OVITO).
  --n-orientations-azimuthal N_ORIENTATIONS_AZIMUTHAL
                        With --ml-rank: this many evenly-spaced in-plane rotations sampled per polar direction (see --n-orientations-polar). Default 1.
  --orientation-top-k ORIENTATION_TOP_K
                        With --ml-rank and orientation sampling: keep only the N best unique (post-deduplication) orientations per site, instead of all surviving ones. Unset (default) keeps every unique orientation found.
  --orientation-rmsd-tol ORIENTATION_RMSD_TOL
                        With --ml-rank and orientation sampling: two relaxed orientations at the same site are treated as duplicates (only the better-energy one kept) when their adsorbate-atom RMSD is below this (Ang) AND their energy differs by less than 0.01 eV. Default 0.3.
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory (default: adsorption_run) for 'clean_slab', 'adsorbate' and 'sites' -- everything this study needs lives under one folder, same convention as stb-hubbardu's hubbardu_runs.
  --save-report         Also persist the full report narrative to adsorption_prep_report.txt (under --output-dir). Off by default. 'sites/adsorption_sites.txt' (the SITE_TABLE stb-adsorbAnalysis reads) is always written regardless.
  --view                Open every generated structure (clean_slab, isolated adsorbate(s), and every written site) in ASE's interactive 3D viewer as a multi-frame browser, after everything else has finished. Needs a display.
  --view-plots          Also show the matplotlib plot(s) this run generates -- the candidate-site layout, and the ML pre-screen ranking chart if --ml-rank is used -- on screen (one blocking window per plot), instead of only saving them as PNGs. Off by default. A separate flag from --view since that one already means the ASE structure viewer here.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-adsorb -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf --adsorbate O --site-type ontop
  stb-adsorb -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf --adsorbate H2O --all-sites --site-type all
  stb-adsorb -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf --adsorbate H --all-sites --ml-rank --top-k 3
  stb-adsorb -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf --adsorbate O,N,C --site-type ontop
  stb-adsorb -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf --adsorbate O --height-sweep 1.5 3.0 0.5

stb-adsorbAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-adsorbAnalysis [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE] [-o OUTPUT]
                          [--apply STRUCTURE_FDF] [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE]
                          [--save-report] [--view] [--view-plots] [--compute-gibbs]
                          [--zpe-mode {local,full}] [--displacement DISPLACEMENT]
                          [--gibbs-supercell GIBBS_SUPERCELL GIBBS_SUPERCELL GIBBS_SUPERCELL]
                          [-v] [--no-intro]

Computes adsorption energies from an stb-adsorb sweep: E_ads = E_site - E_clean_slab - E_adsorbate.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Root directory containing 'clean_slab/', 'adsorbate*/' and 'sites/' (default: adsorption_run -- stb-adsorb's own default --output-dir, so this stage runs against that one's output with no extra flag in the common case).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each folder (default: calc.out).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output data file name (default: adsorption_curve.dat).
  --apply STRUCTURE_FDF
                        Copy the most stable site's structure.fdf (BSSE-corrected ranking when available for every site, else the uncorrected ranking) to this path.
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05, same as stb-cohesiveAnalysis) above which a site's calc.out is flagged as possibly not relaxed -- E_ads would then reflect a strained/off-equilibrium geometry rather than the true adsorption minimum. Advisory only, never blocks the result.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to adsorption_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open clean_slab, every adsorbate reference and every site (preferring each folder's own <label>.XV -- the actual relaxed geometry, if SIESTA has been run there -- falling back to its input structure.fdf otherwise) in ASE's interactive 3D viewer as a multi-frame browser, after everything else has finished. Needs a display.
  --view-plots          Also show the matplotlib adsorption-ranking plot on screen (one blocking window), instead of only saving it as a PNG. Off by default.
  --compute-gibbs       Also write the vibrational-Hessian displacement folders (under '<dir>/gibbs/') stb-adsorbGibbs (Stage 4) needs to compute a Gibbs free energy of adsorption, for the winning site (BSSE-ranked if complete, else uncorrected) and its isolated-adsorbate reference. Off by default -- this is the one exception in this tool to 'analysis never generates new folders', by explicit design (see CLAUDE.md): the alternative would be a whole extra prep-only stage duplicating everything [0]-[4] already do.
  --zpe-mode {local,full}
                        Vibrational Hessian mode for the SITE side, when --compute-gibbs (default: local). 'local': partial Hessian, only the adsorbate's own atoms displaced (substrate frozen) -- fast, a decoupled-oscillator approximation, no Phonopy involved. 'full': a real Phonopy phonon calculation of the ENTIRE site structure, minus the clean slab's own (also full-structure) phonon calculation -- rigorous, but far more SIESTA jobs. The isolated-adsorbate reference ALWAYS uses the 'local' (full-Hessian-of-the-whole-molecule) method regardless of this flag -- there's no periodic substrate phonon to subtract for an isolated molecule in a vacuum box, so Phonopy's supercell machinery buys nothing there.
  --displacement DISPLACEMENT
                        Finite-difference displacement in Ang for the Hessian/Phonopy displacements (default: 0.015, same as stb-herRefs/stb-oerRefs).
  --gibbs-supercell GIBBS_SUPERCELL GIBBS_SUPERCELL GIBBS_SUPERCELL
                        Supercell dimensions for --zpe-mode full's site+clean-slab phonon calculations (default: 1 1 1 -- appropriate when the slab's own in-plane supercell is already large enough).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-adsorbAnalysis
  stb-adsorbAnalysis --dir adsorption_run --file calc.out
  stb-adsorbAnalysis --apply best_structure.fdf

stb-adsorbBsse.help:
usage: stb-adsorbBsse [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE]
                      [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE] [--save-report] [-v]
                      [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of the Adsorption workflow: generates the BSSE (counterpoise) ghost-fragment folders at each site's RELAXED geometry, once stb-adsorb's own sites/site_*/ have finished running in SIESTA.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Root directory containing 'clean_slab/' and 'sites/' (default: adsorption_run -- stb-adsorb's own default --output-dir).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each site folder (default: calc.out).
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05) above which a site's relaxation is flagged as possibly incomplete -- advisory only, never blocks BSSE folder generation.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to adsorption_bsse_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-adsorbBsse
  stb-adsorbBsse --dir adsorption_run --file calc.out

stb-adsorbGibbs.help:
usage: stb-adsorbGibbs [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE] [--tmin TMIN] [--tmax TMAX]
                       [--tstep TSTEP] [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE]
                       [--save-report] [--view-plots] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 4 of the Adsorption workflow: combines the vibrational Hessian/phonon folders stb-adsorbAnalysis --compute-gibbs (Stage 3) wrote into a Gibbs free energy of adsorption, DG = E_ads(BSSE if available) + DZPE - T*DS.
DZPE/DS = [ZPE/S(site) - ZPE/S(isolated adsorbate reference)], both computed with the SAME method
(local partial-Hessian, or full Phonopy for the site side when Stage 3 used --zpe-mode full) --
the isolated reference always uses the local, full-molecule Hessian (there's no periodic substrate
phonon to subtract for a molecule in a vacuum box, so Phonopy's supercell machinery buys nothing
there; for a single-atom adsorbate this correctly gives ZPE=S=0, since a free atom has no
vibrational modes at all once its 3 translational modes are excluded).

KNOWN LIMITATION, always printed in the report: the isolated-reference term above is
VIBRATIONAL/HARMONIC ONLY -- it does NOT include the translational/rotational entropy a real gas
molecule has from being free to move/rotate in 3D (an ideal-gas partition-function term this tool
does not compute). For a single-atom adsorbate this is exact (no rotation/translation to begin
with beyond the excluded trivial modes); for a polyatomic adsorbate it is an approximation, in the
same spirit as (though computed differently from) stb-herRefs/stb-oerRefs' own use of a FIXED
literature entropy for their H2/H2O gas-phase references -- generalized here since there is no
literature table for an arbitrary adsorbate.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Root directory containing 'gibbs/', 'sites/', 'clean_slab/' etc. (default: adsorption_run -- stb-adsorb's own default --output-dir).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each folder (default: calc.out).
  --tmin TMIN           Sweep start, Kelvin (default: 200).
  --tmax TMAX           Sweep end, Kelvin (default: 400).
  --tstep TSTEP         Sweep step, Kelvin (default: 25).
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05) above which a folder is flagged as possibly not converged/relaxed. Advisory only.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to adsorption_gibbs_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view-plots          Also show the DG-vs-T plot on screen, instead of only saving it as a PNG. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-adsorbGibbs --dir adsorption_run --tmin 100 --tmax 500

stb-aimdAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-aimdAnalysis [-h] [-l LABEL] [--geometry-file PATH] [--trajectory PATH]
                        [--dt FS] [--stride STRIDE] [--skip SKIP] [--pair A-B]
                        [--r-max R_MAX] [--n-bins N_BINS] [--fit-start FS]
                        [--fit-end FS] [--track-atom N] [--track-pair I-J]
                        [--list-atoms] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report]
                        [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [--no-intro] [-v]

Physical post-processing of an AIMD/MD trajectory -- a SIESTA AIMD run (<label>.ANI) or a generic ASE-readable trajectory (e.g. one written by stb-mlmd): radial distribution function g(r), mean-squared displacement (MSD) and diffusion coefficient, a VACF-derived vibrational density of state (VDOS), single-atom displacement tracking, and atom-pair relative distance tracking. Complements stb-ani2traj, which only converts a SIESTA trajectory's format for external viewers.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SIESTA SystemLabel -- reads '<label>.ANI'. Mutually exclusive with --trajectory.
  --geometry-file PATH  Explicit path to the real SIESTA .fdf input file (--label mode only). MD.InitialTimeStep/MD.LengthTimeStep (the real MD timestep) and, if '<label>.XV'/'<label>.out' aren't usable, the lattice itself are read from here. Auto-detecting '<label>.fdf' almost never works in practice -- the input file's own name is chosen by the user and is very often NOT <label>.fdf (e.g. SystemLabel 'siesta' with the real input called calc.fdf) -- pass this explicitly instead of relying on that guess.
  --trajectory PATH     Read a generic ASE-readable multi-frame trajectory instead of a SIESTA .ANI -- e.g. one written by stb-mlmd (xsf/pdb/xyz). Mutually exclusive with --label.
  --dt FS               Real time between saved frames in the --trajectory file, in fs (--trajectory mode only). Auto-detected if the file is an extended-xyz with per-frame 'Time' info (e.g. stb-mlmd --out-format xyz); required otherwise (xsf/pdb carry no such data).
  --stride STRIDE       Keep only every Nth frame (default: 1, every frame).
  --skip SKIP           Discard the first N frames (post-stride) as thermal equilibration, before any statistics are computed (default: 0).
  --pair A-B            Restrict the RDF to one species pair, e.g. 'O-H' (default: total RDF over all pairs).
  --r-max R_MAX         RDF cutoff in Angstrom (default: the minimum-image limit of the smallest cell found in the trajectory).
  --n-bins N_BINS       Number of RDF bins (default: 200).
  --fit-start FS        MSD linear-fit window start, in fs (default: half the trajectory length).
  --fit-end FS          MSD linear-fit window end, in fs (default: end of trajectory).
  --track-atom N        0-based atom index whose own Cartesian displacement (from its initial position, PBC-unwrapped -- same convention as the MSD) is tracked and reported over time (optional).
  --track-pair I-J      Two 0-based atom indices, e.g. '0-5', whose relative distance (minimum-image convention, same as the RDF) is tracked and reported over time (optional).
  --list-atoms          Print a table of every atom's 0-based index, species, and Cartesian coordinates (Ang, from the first frame only) to help pick --track-atom/--track-pair indices, then exit immediately -- no RDF/MSD/VDOS/report is computed. Off by default (a large structure can have hundreds of atoms).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write <stem>_*.dat/.gplot (with --save-gnuplot) and stb_aimdAnalysis_report.txt/references.bib into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_aimdAnalysis_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a .dat + .gplot pair for every computed quantity (RDF, MSD, VACF, VDOS, and the atom-displacement/pair-distance series if --track-atom/--track-pair are used). Off by default -- this tool previously wrote matplotlib PNGs unconditionally on every run with no gnuplot output at all.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview before finishing. Off by default -- this tool previously always generated (and saved) the matplotlib plots, with no way to skip it.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-aimdAnalysis --label aimd
  stb-aimdAnalysis -l aimd --pair O-H --skip 50
  stb-aimdAnalysis -l aimd --fit-start 5000 --fit-end 15000
  stb-aimdAnalysis -l aimd --track-atom 0 --track-pair 0-1
  stb-aimdAnalysis -l aimd --save-report --save-gnuplot --view
  stb-aimdAnalysis --trajectory si_bulk_md_traj.xyz --dt 10

stb-amorphize.help:
usage: stb-amorphize [-h] -f FILENAME [--melt-temp MELT_TEMP]
                     [--melt-steps MELT_STEPS] [--quench-temp QUENCH_TEMP]
                     [--quench-steps QUENCH_STEPS] [--timestep TIMESTEP] [--taut TAUT]
                     [--taup TAUP] [--compressibility COMPRESSIBILITY]
                     [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                     [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--seed SEED] [--no-final-relax]
                     [--stride STRIDE] [--save-data] [--save-traj]
                     [--traj-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}] [-sp SYMPREC] [--save-report]
                     [--view] [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Melt-quench amorphous structure generator using the MACE-MP-0 potential.
Heats a crystalline structure above its melting point long enough to erase
crystalline memory, then cools it back down -- a fast heuristic starting
guess for an amorphous/glassy structure, meant to give SIESTA a much better
starting point than an ad-hoc random-displacement structure. NOT a
substitute for a slower, production-quality quench (more steps, slower
cooling) or DFT verification.

Bulk (3D periodic) structures only -- melting a vacuum-padded slab/wire/
molecule is physically meaningless. The input is rejected outright if any
vacuum-padded axis is detected.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input crystalline structure file (.fdf), typically a supercell (e.g. from stb-supercell). Must be bulk (3D periodic, no vacuum-padded axis).
  --melt-temp MELT_TEMP
                        Melt temperature in K (default: 3000.0).
  --melt-steps MELT_STEPS
                        MD steps held at --melt-temp (default: 500).
  --quench-temp QUENCH_TEMP
                        Final target temperature in K (default: 300.0).
  --quench-steps QUENCH_STEPS
                        MD steps for a linear cooling ramp from --melt-temp to --quench-temp (default: 1000).
  --timestep TIMESTEP   MD timestep in fs (default: 1.0).
  --taut TAUT           Berendsen temperature-coupling time constant, fs (default: 50.0).
  --taup TAUP           Berendsen pressure-coupling time constant, fs (default: 200.0).
  --compressibility COMPRESSIBILITY
                        Compressibility in eV/Ang^3 for the Berendsen barostat (default: 4.57e-5, water's value -- a generic placeholder; override with your material's real compressibility if known).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size: speed/accuracy tradeoff (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  --seed SEED           Seed for the initial Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities (default: not reproducible).
  --no-final-relax      Skip the final static (position+cell) relax. On by default: the MD quench alone leaves real residual thermal energy, not a clean local minimum.
  --stride STRIDE       Sample one diagnostics point / trajectory frame every Nth MD step, across both the melt and quench stages (default: 10). Only used if --save-data and/or --save-traj is given.
  --save-data           Write <stem>_md_diagnostics.dat + a companion .gplot (step, temperature, E_pot/E_kin/E_total, volume) for the whole melt-quench process, plottable with gnuplot. Off by default.
  --save-traj           Write a multi-frame trajectory of the melt-quench MD (see --traj-format) for viewing in OVITO/VMD. Off by default.
  --traj-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}
                        Trajectory format for --save-traj (default: xsf). Same 3 choices as stb-ani2traj/stb-mlmd.
  -sp SYMPREC, --symprec SYMPREC
                        Symmetry tolerance in Angstroms for the before/after symmetry analysis (default: 0.01).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_amorphize_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the input crystalline structure and the final amorphized structure (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: amorphous.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-amorphize -f bulk_supercell.fdf
  stb-amorphize -f bulk_supercell.fdf --melt-temp 4000 --quench-steps 2000
  stb-amorphize -f bulk_supercell.fdf --save-report --view
  stb-amorphize -f bulk_supercell.fdf --save-data --save-traj --traj-format xsf

Notes:
  - Bulk (3D periodic) structures only -- see the description above.

stb-ani2traj.help:
usage: stb-ani2traj [-h] -l LABEL [-of {pdb,xsf,xyz}] [-o OUTPUT] [--stride STRIDE]
                    [--unwrap] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Convert a SIESTA AIMD trajectory (<label>.ANI) into a multi-frame trajectory format that also carries the lattice -- for opening in OVITO, VMD, etc. .ANI itself is a bare multi-frame XYZ with no cell information at all; the lattice is read per-frame from <label>.out when available (correct for variable-cell/NPT runs too), or a single static one from <label>.XV/<label>.fdf otherwise.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel (required).
  -of {pdb,xsf,xyz}, --out-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}
                        Output trajectory format (default: xsf):
                          xsf - multi-frame AXSF, read natively by OVITO and VMD's xsf plugin.
                          pdb - multi-model PDB (CRYST1), VMD's own default format, also read by OVITO.
                          xyz - extended XYZ (Lattice tag), OVITO-native; VMD's xyz reader ignores
                                the Lattice tag (positions show, but without periodic boundaries).
                                The only format that also carries per-frame E_KS/Temp_ion/Time.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output filename. Default: <label>_traj.<ext>
  --stride STRIDE       Keep only every Nth frame (default: 1, every frame).
  --unwrap              Remove periodic-boundary 'jumps': each frame's positions are corrected by the minimum-image displacement relative to the previous frame, so atoms that legitimately cross the box edge read as continuous motion in OVITO/VMD instead of teleporting. Off by default (raw .ANI positions, as SIESTA wrote them, mod the cell).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_ani2traj_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-ani2traj --label aimd --out-format xsf
  stb-ani2traj -l siesta -of pdb -o traj.pdb --stride 5
  stb-ani2traj -l siesta -of xyz --unwrap

stb-archive.help:
usage: stb-archive [-h] [--path PATH] [-l LABEL] [--include EXT [EXT ...]]
                   [--exclude EXT [EXT ...]] [-o OUTPUT] [--save-report] [--no-intro]
                   [-v]

Package a finished SIESTA calculation (inputs + essential outputs) into a single
.tar.gz for sharing or reproducibility -- the complement of stb-clean, which deletes
that same class of outputs to prep for a restart instead of preserving them. --path
can be a glob pattern to archive several folders at once (e.g. 'strain_*'), one
archive each.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --path PATH           Directory to archive, or a glob pattern (e.g. 'strain_*')
                        matching several directories (default: current directory).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel override, applied to every matched directory.
                        Auto-detected per directory from its .fdf file(s) if not given
                        (only affects the manifest's run-type/convergence/energy
                        summary, not which files get archived).
  --include EXT [EXT ...]
                        Extra extensions to include, on top of the default set (.fdf
                        .psf .psml .sh .out .XV .STRUCT_OUT .bands .DOS .xml).
  --exclude EXT [EXT ...]
                        Extensions to remove from the default include set.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Archive filename. Default: <foldername>_archive.tar.gz (next
                        to --path). Ignored in batch mode (multiple directories
                        matched --path).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_archive_report.txt. Off by
                        default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

stb-bader.help:
usage: stb-bader [-h] -l LABEL [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--ref REF]
                 [--speed {normal,fast}] [--threads N] [--vacuum-tol TOL] [--no-cube]
                 [--export-volumes] [-v] [--no-intro]

Computes Bader (AIM) atomic charges from a SIESTA charge-density grid.
Reads <label>.RHO (charge density) plus <label>.XV or <label>.fdf (geometry),
converts to a .cube file via sisl, and partitions it into atomic basins with
PyBader. Z_val (valence electron count per species) is parsed automatically
from <label>.out when available (or --ref points at a specific SIESTA
output); species it doesn't mention fall back to a hardcoded periodic-table
guess, per species, with a warning. If the .RHO file is spin-polarized, a
per-atom net spin (magnetic moment) is reported alongside the charge
automatically. Dummy/no-element sites (Z<=0) are excluded to match
PyBader's own handling; SIESTA's own ghost/BSSE atoms are unaffected.
Also reports each atom's Bader volume and minimum surface distance, a
per-species mean/std summary, and cross-checks symmetry-equivalent atoms
against each other -- on top of the per-atom warnings for a suspiciously
low (near-zero) population.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel used in Siesta
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write the .cube file(s)/references.bib into (and stb_bader_report.txt, with --save-report; also any --export-volumes files) (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_bader_report.txt. Off by default.
  --ref REF             Path to a specific .out file to read Z_val from (overrides <label>.out)
  --speed {normal,fast}
                        'fast' uses PyBader's own bundled speed profile (on-grid charge assignment instead of near-grid) -- quicker, less precise basin boundaries (default: normal)
  --threads N           Worker threads for PyBader, >= 1 (default: $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK if set, else every CPU core -- multiprocessing.cpu_count() can overcount under a job scheduler's cgroup limits)
  --vacuum-tol TOL      Charge-density threshold (e/Ang^3) below which a voxel is assigned to a separate 'vacuum' bucket instead of the nearest atom -- useful for slabs/wires/isolated molecules with empty space in the cell (default: disabled, matches PyBader's own default)
  --no-cube             Delete the intermediate .cube file(s) after the calculation (kept by default -- they can be large for dense grids)
  --export-volumes      Also write each atom's individual Bader volume as its own 'Bader-atoms-<N>.cube' file (plus a vacuum one if --vacuum-tol is set) inside --output-dir, for visual inspection in VESTA/VMD -- one file per atom, each as large as the main grid, so this is opt-in (default: off)
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-bader --label siesta
  stb-bader --label siesta --ref relax/siesta.out --save-report
  stb-bader --label siesta --speed fast --threads 8
  stb-bader --label slab --vacuum-tol 1e-3
  stb-bader --label siesta --export-volumes

stb-bands.help:
usage: stb-bands [-h] [--label LABEL] [--file INPUT_FILE] --shift
                 {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual} [--manual-value MANUAL_VALUE]
                 [--gap-tol GAP_TOL] [--eig-file EIG_FILE] [--kp-file KP_FILE]
                 [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Process the band structure data.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label (e.g. 'siesta'). Shorthand for --file <label>.bands, and auto-detects <label>.EIG next to it for the mesh (k-grid) gap comparison -- if that .EIG isn't there, the mesh comparison is skipped rather than treated as an error. Also auto-detects <label>.KP (mesh k-point coordinates) alongside the .EIG, if present. Mutually exclusive with --file/--eig-file/--kp-file.
  --file INPUT_FILE     Path to the input file containing band structure data (e.g., siesta.bands). Alternative to --label when you need an explicit path.
  --shift {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual}
                        Reference energy shift:
                          - 'vbm'    : Valence Band Maximum
                          - 'cbm'    : Conduction Band Minimum
                          - 'fermi'  : Fermi level
                          - 'manual' : Custom shift value (requires --manual-value).
  --manual-value MANUAL_VALUE
                        Custom energy shift value (required if --shift manual is used).
  --gap-tol GAP_TOL     Energy tolerance in eV below which a gap is classified as Metallic (default: 0.01).
  --eig-file EIG_FILE   Optional SIESTA .EIG file (full k-mesh eigenvalues from the SCF run). When given, compares the k-mesh gap against the k-path gap from --file -- the high-symmetry path may not pass through the true VBM/CBM. Requires sisl.
  --kp-file KP_FILE     Optional SIESTA .KP file matching --eig-file's k-mesh (Cartesian kx,ky,kz in 1/Ang). When given, mesh VBM/CBM/direct-gap k-points are reported as (kx, ky, kz) instead of a bare mesh index. Requires --eig-file.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write bands_gnuplot.dat and bands.gplot into (and stb_bands_report.txt/references.bib, with --save-report) (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_bands_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb_bands --label siesta --shift fermi
  stb_bands --file siesta.bands --shift fermi
  stb_bands --file siesta.bands --shift manual --manual-value 0.5
  stb_bands --file siesta.bands --shift fermi --gap-tol 0.05
  stb_bands --file siesta.bands --shift fermi --eig-file siesta.EIG
  stb_bands --file siesta.bands --shift fermi --save-report

stb-chargediffAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-chargediffAnalysis [-h] [--dir DIR] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--3d | --profile]
                              [-a {0,1,2}] [-p POS] [--spin] [--iso-min RHO]
                              [--no-cube] [--vmin VMIN] [--vmax VMAX] [--contour]
                              [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [--no-intro]
                              [-v]

Stage 2 of the Charge Density Difference workflow: given just --dir (the same folder stb-chargediffPrep wrote into), auto-discovers the combined system and every fragment from chargediff_manifest.json, reads each one's own .RHO (once SIESTA has been run in every folder), and computes Delta rho = rho_combined - sum(rho_fragment_i) -- the standard way to visualize charge accumulation/depletion regions.
Produces the same 2D slice / 3D point cloud / planar-averaged 1D profile /
Gaussian cube output as stb-density, so the visualization conventions match
the rest of the suite. --spin computes the spin-density difference instead
(only available if the combined system and every fragment are
spin-polarized).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Directory stb-chargediffPrep wrote into -- must contain 'chargediff_manifest.json' plus the 'combined/' and fragment subfolders it lists, each already run in SIESTA. Default: chargediff_run (stb-chargediffPrep's own default --output-dir).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write the data/gnuplot/cube/report files and references.bib into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --3d                  Export full 3D volume
  --profile             Write the planar average of Delta rho along --axis as a 1D profile (average taken over the other two axes) instead of a 2D/3D map -- useful for bilayers, slabs, and interfaces
  -a {0,1,2}, --axis {0,1,2}
                        For a slice/profile: the axis normal to the cut plane (slice) or the axis the profile varies along (profile) (0=X, 1=Y, 2=Z)
  -p POS, --pos POS     Position (Angstrom) of the 2D cut (ignored in --profile mode)
  --spin                Compute the SPIN density difference instead of the charge density difference -- only available if the combined system AND every fragment are spin-polarized.
  --iso-min RHO         For --3d: only export/preview points with |Delta rho| >= this threshold (e/Ang^3) -- keeps the point cloud a manageable size and visually meaningful instead of dominated by near-zero points
  --no-cube             Skip writing Delta rho's full 3D grid as a Gaussian .cube file -- written by default (needs a '*.XV' or 'structure.fdf' in the combined folder for the geometry), for real 3D isosurface rendering in VESTA/VMD/Avogadro.
  --vmin VMIN           Fix the colorbar/palette lower bound manually (e/Ang^3), e.g. to compare several slices on the same scale.
  --vmax VMAX           Fix the colorbar/palette upper bound manually (e/Ang^3).
  --contour             Overlay contour lines on a 2D slice map/preview (ignored for --3d/--profile)
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to chargediff_analysis_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a .gplot script next to each .dat file this run generates. Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of Delta rho (slice heatmap / profile line / 3D scatter, matching the mode). Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-chargediffAnalysis
  stb-chargediffAnalysis --dir chargediff_run --profile --axis 2
  stb-chargediffAnalysis --dir chargediff_run --view
  stb-chargediffAnalysis --dir chargediff_run --no-cube

stb-chargediffPrep.help:
usage: stb-chargediffPrep [-h] [-s STRUCTURE]
                          (--fragment-manifest PATH | --fragment-sizes N1,N2,...,NK | --fragment-species El_a,El_b;El_c;...)
                          [--calc CALC] [--mesh-cutoff RY] [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                          [--force-spin] [--no-force-spin] [--force-dipole]
                          [--no-force-dipole] [--force-vdw] [--no-force-vdw]
                          [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--view] [--save-report]
                          [--no-intro] [-v]

Stage 1 of the Charge Density Difference workflow: writes a 'combined/' SIESTA input folder (every atom real, no ghosting) plus one fragment folder per fragment of an N-fragment system (bilayer, molecule-on-slab, etc.) -- ALL of them sharing the identical cell/mesh/level of theory, forced by this tool itself. Every fragment folder ALWAYS includes every other fragment as ghost atoms (no opt-out) so every calculation shares the same basis set.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Path to the combined system's own .fdf structure file -- taken directly as the REAL, authoritative geometry to be split into fragments (structure_io.read_fdf, no directory scanning, no automatic preference for a relaxed '*.XV' that might sit alongside it -- point this at whichever file you consider the real geometry, e.g. a fresh structure.fdf written from a converged '*.XV' via stb-translate). Default: 'structure.fdf'.
  --fragment-manifest PATH
                        Reuse an existing fragment_manifest.json (written by stb-adsorb) to recover its slab/adsorbate split -- exactly 2 fragments. Pass an empty value ('') to default to 'fragment_manifest.json' next to --structure itself.
  --fragment-sizes N1,N2,...,NK
                        General split by ATOM COUNT: comma-separated atom counts, in the order fragments appear in the structure file (fragment 1 = first N1 atoms, fragment 2 = next N2, ...). Must sum to the combined structure's total atom count. K >= 2.
  --fragment-species El_a,El_b;El_c;...
                        General split by CHEMICAL SPECIES, independent of atom order: ';'-separated groups, each a comma-separated list of element symbols belonging to that fragment (e.g. 'C;B,N' for a graphene/h-BN heterostructure). Every species present in the structure must appear in exactly one group. LIMITATION: cannot be used when two fragments physically share a species (e.g. MoS2 on WS2, sulfur in both layers) -- use --fragment-sizes or --fragment-manifest instead in that case.
  --calc CALC           SIESTA input template (.fdf) used for every fragment folder -- same basis/SCF/k-grid as the combined system (default: 'calc.fdf').
  --mesh-cutoff RY      Explicit MeshCutoff (Ry) to force in every fragment folder -- the SAME value on all of them, never auto-detected from --calc/the combined system's own calc.fdf (a per-run SIESTA default can silently differ between calculations with different atoms/pseudopotentials, which would corrupt the point-by-point subtraction). Default: 400 Ry -- raise it for a finer grid (recommended for a production CDD map) or type a different value here.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path (same convention as stb-adsorb/stb-her/stb-hubbardu). Default: reuse the directory --structure lives in, which already has every pseudopotential the combined calculation needed.
  --force-spin          Force spin-polarized SCF in every fragment folder (default: inherited from the combined system's own config_extra.fdf, if any).
  --no-force-spin       Force spin-restricted SCF, overriding the combined system's own setting.
  --force-dipole        Force the slab dipole correction (default: inherited from the combined system's own config_extra.fdf, if any).
  --no-force-dipole     Disable the slab dipole correction, overriding the combined system's own setting.
  --force-vdw           Force the DFT-D3 dispersion correction (default: inherited from the combined system's own config_extra.fdf, if any).
  --no-force-vdw        Disable the DFT-D3 dispersion correction, overriding the combined system's own setting.
  --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory to write the fragment folders into (default: chargediff_run).
  --view                After writing them, open ONE ASE interactive 3D viewer window with the combined structure followed by every fragment as navigable movie frames -- ghost atoms render as mostly-hollow circles (see structure_to_view_atoms's docstring). Needs a display. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to chargediff_prep_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Usage examples:
  stb-chargediffPrep --fragment-sizes "12,12"
  stb-chargediffPrep --structure bilayer/structure.fdf --fragment-species "C;B,N" -p dojo
  stb-chargediffPrep --structure adsorption_run/sites/site_1/structure.fdf --fragment-manifest adsorption_run/sites/site_1/fragment_manifest.json

stb-clean.help:
usage: stb-clean [-h] [--path PATH] [--keep KEEP [KEEP ...]] [--recursive]
                 [--no-archive] [--no-confirm] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Clean a SIESTA calc folder to restart a fresh run: removes every file except the
extensions in --keep (pseudopotentials, .fdf input, submission script by default).
This deletes outputs/results too (.out, .XV, .bands, .DOS, ...) -- it's meant to prep
for a re-run, not to archive results. Every removed file is archived (tar.gz) first
unless --no-archive.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --path PATH           Directory to clean, or a glob pattern (e.g. 'strain_*')
                        matching several directories to clean one after another
                        (default: current directory).
  --keep KEEP [KEEP ...]
                        Extensions to keep, i.e. NOT delete (default: .psml .psf .fdf
                        .sh -- pseudopotentials, the SIESTA input, and the submission
                        script). Everything else, including prior run outputs, is
                        removed.
  --recursive           Also clean subdirectories (skips hidden ones, e.g. .git), not
                        just the top level of --path.
  --no-archive          Skip archiving removed files before deleting them. Archiving
                        (tar.gz, next to --path) is the default safety net -- turn it
                        off only if you're sure.
  --no-confirm, -n      Don't ask for confirmation before deleting.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_clean_report.txt (next to
                        --path). Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

stb-cohesive.help:
usage: stb-cohesive [-h] -s STRUCTURE [-p PP_PATH] [-k K_DENSITY] [--spin]
                    [--vacuum VACUUM] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [-O OUTPUT_DIR]
                    [--bsse-correction] [--no-bsse-correction]
                    [--bsse-cutoff BSSE_CUTOFF] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                    [--bsse-multi-site] [--no-bsse-multi-site]
                    [--bsse-convergence-check]
                    [--bsse-convergence-increment BSSE_CONVERGENCE_INCREMENT [BSSE_CONVERGENCE_INCREMENT ...]]
                    [--dispersion] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Prepare folder structure for cohesive energy calculations.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Path to the initial structure.fdf file
  -p PP_PATH, --pp-path PP_PATH
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path.
  -k K_DENSITY, --k-density K_DENSITY
                        K-point density in 1/Angstrom (default: 0.2)
  --spin                Set the full structure calculation to spin polarized
  --vacuum VACUUM       Guaranteed buffer (Ang/2, see below) between the outermost atom of each isolated-atom-type calculation and the edge of its cubic simulation box (default: 20.0). For a plain isolated atom (no neighbors) the box is exactly this value, same as before. For a BSSE ghost cluster (see --bsse-cutoff) or its --bsse-convergence-check counterpart, the box automatically GROWS with the cluster's own radius (box side = 2*cutoff + --vacuum) so the buffer beyond the outermost ghost atom stays exactly --vacuum/2 regardless of how large --bsse-cutoff/--bsse-convergence-increment are -- otherwise a bigger convergence-check cluster would eat into a fixed-size box and risk interacting with its own periodic images, contaminating the very convergence check it's meant to validate. Increase for elements with unusually diffuse basis orbitals.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum gap threshold in Ang used to detect which lattice axes of the FULL structure are periodic vs. vacuum-padded (default: 10.0), same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-strain/stb-elasticInputs. Vacuum-padded axes are forced to a single (Gamma-only) k-grid division regardless of --k-density.
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory (default: cohesive_runs, matching stb-strain's/stb-elasticInputs' own <property>_runs convention) for the 'structure', 'atoms' and 'atoms_bsse' folders -- so stb-cohesiveAnalysis can just 'cd <output-dir>' (or pass --dir) and find everything with no extra flags. Set this to avoid silently overwriting a previous run's setup when preparing more than one structure from the same working directory.
  --bsse-correction     Also generate a BSSE (Basis Set Superposition Error) -corrected reference per species, in 'atoms_bsse/<symbol>/' (default: ON). LCAO cohesive energies are otherwise systematically over-bound: the isolated atom is computed with a smaller effective basis than it has inside the solid (no neighboring atoms' orbitals available). The correction embeds the same real atom in 'ghost' copies (SIESTA convention: negative Z, no valence charge, same basis as the real element) of its actual nearest neighbors from the full structure (see --bsse-cutoff), giving it the same effective basis it has in the solid without changing its physics. Doubles the number of isolated-atom-type DFT calculations needed (one plain + one BSSE-corrected per species).
  --no-bsse-correction  Skip the BSSE-corrected reference (halves the isolated-atom-type calculation count, at the cost of a systematically over-bound cohesive energy).
  --bsse-cutoff BSSE_CUTOFF
                        Radius in Ang (default: 4.0) around each species' anchor atom within which real neighbors become ghost atoms in its BSSE-corrected reference (see --bsse-correction). How many coordination shells this actually reaches depends on the material's bond length -- for short-bonded covalent solids (e.g. graphene, diamond, ~1.4-1.5 Ang bonds) it typically reaches several shells; for longer-bonded ionic/metallic solids it may only reach the 1st. Check the printed ghost-neighbor count per species; the correction is converged once increasing --bsse-cutoff no longer changes the reported BSSE-corrected energy appreciably. Only used when --bsse-correction is on.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default), used to find symmetrically distinct sites per species for --bsse-multi-site. Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance -- a tighter value than the relaxation's own residual numerical noise can misdetect the true space group (see stb-symmetry --scan-symprec to check where a given structure's symmetry call is sensitive).
  --bsse-multi-site     When a species occupies 2+ symmetrically distinct sites (e.g. octahedral vs. tetrahedral Fe), build a separate BSSE ghost-cluster reference PER site (default: ON) -- stb-cohesiveAnalysis then weights each site's BSSE-corrected energy by its multiplicity, instead of using a single (potentially unrepresentative) site for the whole species.
  --no-bsse-multi-site  Use only the first detected site as the BSSE reference for a species with multiple distinct sites (prints a warning naming the sites being skipped), instead of one cluster per site.
  --bsse-convergence-check
                        Also generate one or more extra BSSE references per species/site at a larger cutoff (see --bsse-convergence-increment) -- stb-cohesiveAnalysis then reports how much the BSSE-corrected cohesive energy shifts as the cutoff grows, as a convergence check (default: OFF -- on top of --bsse-correction's own doubling, each extra cutoff adds one more isolated-atom-type calculation per species/site). Requires --bsse-correction.
  --bsse-convergence-increment BSSE_CONVERGENCE_INCREMENT [BSSE_CONVERGENCE_INCREMENT ...]
                        One or more Ang values added to --bsse-cutoff (default: 2.0, a single point). Pass several (e.g. --bsse-convergence-increment 2 4 6) to scan multiple cutoffs in one run and see the correction's full trend instead of a single before/after comparison -- stb-cohesiveAnalysis will report and plot the whole curve. With exactly one increment (the default), the extra reference is written to 'atoms_bsse_check/' as before; with 2+, each is written to its own 'atoms_bsse_check_<cutoff>/' instead.
  --dispersion          Enable Grimme DFT-D3 dispersion correction (SIESTA's own DFTD3 directive, default: OFF) for every calculation (full structure, isolated atoms, and BSSE references alike) -- relevant for layered/molecular materials where van der Waals interactions contribute non-negligibly to the cohesive energy. Safe to apply uniformly: a genuinely isolated atom has no neighbor to form a dispersion pair with, so D3 contributes ~0 there regardless.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/cohesive_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb_cohesive -s structure.fdf -k 0.15
  stb_cohesive -s structure.fdf --spin -p /path/to/pseudos

stb-cohesiveAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-cohesiveAnalysis [-h] -o OUT_FILE [-d DIR_PATH]
                            [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE] [--save-report]
                            [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Process cohesive energy results from SIESTA calculations.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o OUT_FILE, --out OUT_FILE
                        Name of the SIESTA output file (e.g., calc.out)
  -d DIR_PATH, --dir DIR_PATH
                        Path to the folder containing 'structure' and 'atoms' directories (default: cohesive_runs, matching stb-cohesive's own --output-dir default -- no --dir needed in the common case, even run from the parent directory).
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05) above which the full structure's calc.out is flagged as possibly not relaxed -- the cohesive energy would then reflect a strained/off-equilibrium geometry rather than the true minimum. Advisory only, never blocks the result.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <dir>/cohesive_results.dat. Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the BSSE-correction figure (see [4] of the report) before finishing. The figure itself is always saved when BSSE data is available, regardless of this flag. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb_cohesive_analysis -o calc.out
  stb_cohesive_analysis -o calc.out -d /path/to/results

stb-convdos.help:
usage: stb-convdos [-h] (--file INPUT_FILE | --dir INPUT_DIR)
                   (--sigma SIGMA | --fwhm FWHM) [--size SIZE] [--out OUTFILE]
                   [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--no-plot] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Apply Gaussian convolution to broaden a DOS file's columns.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file INPUT_FILE     Input DOS file: whitespace-separated columns, energy first. Requires --out. Alternative to --dir.
  --dir INPUT_DIR       Recursively broaden every *.dat file found under this directory (e.g. a stb-dos output folder: dos_total.dat + dos_per_atom/*.dat + dos_per_species/*.dat) with the same --sigma/--fwhm/--size. Each file is written under --output-dir preserving its relative path and filename -- a broadened mirror of the whole input tree. A file that fails validation is skipped with a warning, not fatal to the rest of the batch. Alternative to --file.
  --sigma SIGMA         Gaussian broadening standard deviation, in meV. Converted internally to grid samples using each input file's own energy spacing, so the same --sigma gives the same physical broadening regardless of how densely a file is sampled. Must be positive. Alternative to --fwhm.
  --fwhm FWHM           Gaussian broadening full width at half maximum, in meV (FWHM = 2.3548 * sigma) -- the width more commonly quoted in spectroscopy/DOS literature. Must be positive. Alternative to --sigma.
  --size SIZE           Gaussian kernel width, in samples. Optional -- by default sized automatically from --sigma/--fwhm to cover about 3 standard deviations on each side. Must be a positive odd number if given explicitly (an even size shifts the filtered curve by half a bin, since it has no single center sample).
  --out OUTFILE         Output file for the filtered data. Required with --file, invalid with --dir.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root of the broadened output tree for --dir (default: '<dir>_filtered', a sibling directory). Invalid with --file (use --out there).
  --no-plot             Skip the before/after plot (all columns are still filtered and written). With --dir, only the first processed file is ever plotted regardless of this flag's default; --no-plot turns that single plot off too.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_convdos_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-convdos --file dos_total.dat --sigma 50 --out dos_filtered.dat
  stb-convdos --file dos_total.dat --fwhm 100 --size 41 --out dos_filtered.dat --no-plot
  stb-convdos --dir dos_output/ --sigma 50 --output-dir dos_output_filtered/

stb-convergence.help:
usage: stb-convergence [-h] [-s STRUCTURE] [-c CALC] [-p PSEUDO_DIR] --parameter
                       PARAMETER [PARAMETER ...] [--meshcutoff-range MIN MAX STEP]
                       [--energyshift-range MIN MAX STEP] [--kgrid-range MIN MAX STEP]
                       [--relax-steps RELAX_STEPS] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                       [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 2: writes one ready-to-run SIESTA folder per swept value of one or more convergence-test parameters, one subfolder per parameter, fully relaxing the structure (positions + cell) at each. Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each folder yourself, then use stb-convergenceAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input structure.fdf, copied as 'structure.fdf' into every generated folder (default: structure.fdf).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template (default: calc.fdf) -- SCF/basis/MD settings, normally %including the structure file above by name. Copied into every generated folder with one line added: '%include config_extra.fdf', prepended at the very top (see [3] of the report) -- this forces full relaxation and the swept parameter's value, regardless of what this template itself contains.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path. If given, the required pseudopotential for every species in the structure is copied into every generated folder, so it's immediately ready for SIESTA.
  --parameter PARAMETER [PARAMETER ...]
                        Which tag(s) to sweep: meshcutoff, energyshift, kgrid, or 'all' for all three (one independent sweep per parameter, each in its own subfolder).
  --meshcutoff-range MIN MAX STEP
                        Custom Mesh.CutOff sweep range (Ry). Omit to use the suggested default (see [2] of the report). Only meaningful if 'meshcutoff' is in --parameter.
  --energyshift-range MIN MAX STEP
                        Custom PAO.EnergyShift sweep range (Ry) (see --meshcutoff-range). Only meaningful if 'energyshift' is in --parameter.
  --kgrid-range MIN MAX STEP
                        Custom k-grid density sweep range (1/Ang) (see --meshcutoff-range). Only meaningful if 'kgrid' is in --parameter.
  --relax-steps RELAX_STEPS
                        Number of relaxation steps (MD.Steps) forced in every generated folder (default: 100). Both atomic positions and the cell relax (MD.VariableCell true).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        --parameter kgrid only: vacuum-axis detection threshold in Angstrom, same meaning as stb-kgrid's --vacuum-gap (default: 10.0).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Top-level directory (default: convergence_runs). Run folders go into its own '<output-dir>/<parameter>/convergence_<parameter>_<value>/' subfolder, one tree per swept parameter.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/convergence_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-convergence -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --parameter all
  stb-convergence -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --parameter all --meshcutoff-range 150 350 50
  stb-convergence -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --parameter kgrid --relax-steps 200 --save-report

stb-convergenceAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-convergenceAnalysis [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE] [--tolerance TOLERANCE]
                               [--volume-tolerance VOLUME_TOLERANCE]
                               [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                               [--apply CALC_FDF] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                               [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v]
                               [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 2: analyzes a stb-convergence sweep and reports where each swept parameter's energy AND relaxed structure converge.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Directory to scan for 'convergence_*' run folders -- either stb-convergence's default nested layout (one <parameter>/ subfolder per swept parameter under here) or a flat layout (pointing directly at one parameter's own subfolder) (default: convergence_runs).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each run folder (default: calc.out).
  --tolerance TOLERANCE
                        Energy convergence tolerance in eV/atom (default: 0.01).
  --volume-tolerance VOLUME_TOLERANCE
                        Relaxed-cell-volume convergence tolerance, as a percent change between consecutive swept values (default: 0.5).
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual-force data-quality flag threshold in eV/Ang (default: 0.05) -- NOT a convergence criterion, just flags a run whose CG relaxation may not have reached a genuine minimum.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write <parameter>_convergence.dat/.gplot into with --save-gnuplot, and the report into with --save-report (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --apply CALC_FDF      Writes every parameter's converged (recommended) value into this calc.fdf in place (same tag substitution stb-convergence itself uses) -- parameters with no converged value found are skipped.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        --apply with a kgrid sweep only: vacuum-axis detection threshold in Angstrom, same meaning as stb-kgrid's --vacuum-gap (default: 10.0).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/convergence_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write, per discovered parameter, curve data + a companion .gplot script (2-panel: energy + relaxed volume). Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview (energy + volume per discovered parameter) before finishing. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-convergenceAnalysis --dir convergence_runs
  stb-convergenceAnalysis --dir convergence_runs --tolerance 0.005 --save-report --save-gnuplot --view
  stb-convergenceAnalysis --dir convergence_runs --apply calc.fdf

stb-coop.help:
usage: stb-coop [-h] [--label LABEL] [--wfsx WFSX] [--hsx-file HSX_FILE] --quantity
                {coop,cohp} [--pair I J] [--pair-species A B] --erange EMIN EMAX
                [--npoints NPOINTS] [--shift {none,fermi,manual}] [--fermi FERMI]
                [--bands-file BANDS_FILE] [--fermi-file FERMI_FILE]
                [--manual-value MANUAL_VALUE] (--sigma SIGMA | --fwhm FWHM)
                [--atol ATOL] [--bond-order] [--dm-file DM_FILE] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Energy-resolved COOP/COHP bonding/antibonding curves for selected atom pairs, from a full-BZ SIESTA .WFSX + .HSX.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Auto-detects <label>.WFSX, falling back to <label>.selected.WFSX then <label>.bands.WFSX, and, unless --hsx-file overrides it, <label>.HSX (mandatory -- no approximate fallback). Mutually exclusive with --wfsx (not --hsx-file -- see its own help).
  --wfsx WFSX           Explicit path to the .WFSX file (alternative to --label).
  --hsx-file HSX_FILE   Explicit .HSX path. Required if --wfsx is used instead of --label; optional (and common) together WITH --label too, since the real file is often not literally named <label>.HSX -- --label still auto-detects the .WFSX in that case, only the Hamiltonian source changes.
  --quantity {coop,cohp}
                        'coop': Crystal Orbital Overlap Population. 'cohp': Crystal Orbital Hamilton Population.
  --pair I J            0-based atom-index pair (repeatable). I == J is allowed (on-site term).
  --pair-species A B    Species-pair (repeatable), e.g. --pair-species Sn O -- aggregates ALL atom-index pairs between the two species into one combined curve. If A == B (e.g. Sn Sn), the aggregate also includes each atom's own on-site term, mixed in with the inter-atomic Sn-Sn terms -- use --pair I J for a purely inter-atomic curve instead.
  --erange EMIN EMAX    Energy window (eV), relative to --shift's reference.
  --npoints NPOINTS     Number of energy samples (default: 300). sisl's COOP/COHP is memory-heavy for many points -- start modest.
  --shift {none,fermi,manual}
                        Energy reference (default: none). No vbm/cbm option -- see the module docstring.
  --fermi FERMI         Fermi energy (eV) for --shift fermi. Highest-priority source if given.
  --bands-file BANDS_FILE
                        Companion .bands file to read the Fermi energy from, for --shift fermi.
  --fermi-file FERMI_FILE
                        Explicit SIESTA .out log to read the Fermi energy from, for --shift fermi -- an alternative to --bands-file for a run with no saved .bands file. Not assumed to be named after --label.
  --manual-value MANUAL_VALUE
                        Custom shift value (eV), required if --shift manual.
  --sigma SIGMA         Gaussian broadening standard deviation, in meV.
  --fwhm FWHM           Gaussian broadening full width at half maximum, in meV.
  --atol ATOL           Per-state energy-window cutoff passed straight to sisl's COOP/COHP (default: 1e-10) -- a performance knob, not a physics tolerance.
  --bond-order          Also compute Hamiltonian.bond_order(method='mulliken', projection='atom') per pair from a REAL density matrix -- a cheap, energy-INTEGRATED complementary sanity check, not a substitute for the curve. Needs --dm-file or an auto-detected <label>.DM (see below).
  --dm-file DM_FILE     Explicit .DM density-matrix path, for --bond-order. Falls back to an auto-detected <label>.DM if omitted. SIESTA's .DM format doesn't store the overlap matrix -- it's spliced in from the already-loaded Hamiltonian, so the .DM must be from the same calculation as the .HSX/--hsx-file.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write coop.dat/cohp.dat (and, with --save-gnuplot/--save-report, the .gplot script/report/references.bib) into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_coop_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a real .gplot script alongside coop.dat/cohp.dat. Off by default -- this tool used to write the .dat file unconditionally but never wrote a .gplot script at all.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview before finishing. Off by default (replaces the old --no-plot, which was on by default).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-coop --label siesta --quantity coop --pair 0 1 --erange -10 5 --sigma 200
  stb-coop --label siesta --quantity cohp --pair-species Sn O --erange -10 5 --fwhm 300
  stb-coop --label siesta --quantity coop --pair 0 1 --erange -10 5 --sigma 200 \
      --bond-order --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-crystalbuilder.help:
usage: stb-crystalbuilder [-h] --spacegroup SPACEGROUP --a A [--b B] [--c C]
                          [--alpha ALPHA] [--beta BETA] [--gamma GAMMA] --site SYMBOL
                          X Y Z [--symprec SYMPREC]
                          [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE]
                          [--reduce {primitive,conventional,refined}] [--ml-relax]
                          [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                          [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report]
                          [--view] [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Builds a structure from a space group and Wyckoff positions.
Give only the symmetrically-distinct sites (e.g. one per Wyckoff letter) --
pymatgen expands the rest via the space group's own symmetry operations.

Bulk (3D) crystals only: the 230 space groups accepted by --spacegroup are
the international crystallographic groups for 3D-periodic crystals -- there
is no 2D/1D analog (layer/rod groups) here. To get a 2D or 1D structure,
build the 3D bulk crystal with this tool first, then cut it down with
stb-slab (a surface slab), stb-nanotube (rolled into a tube/ribbon), or
stb-2Dstacking (an isolated monolayer) -- e.g. build bulk graphite
(space group P6_3/mmc) here, then stb-slab --hkl 0 0 1 it into a graphene
monolayer.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --spacegroup SPACEGROUP
                        Space group as an international symbol (e.g. 'Fm-3m') or number (e.g. '225', must be between 1 and 230).
  --a A                 Lattice constant a (Ang).
  --b B                 Lattice constant b (Ang). Default: same as --a.
  --c C                 Lattice constant c (Ang). Default: same as --a.
  --alpha ALPHA         Lattice angle alpha, degrees (default: 90).
  --beta BETA           Lattice angle beta, degrees (default: 90).
  --gamma GAMMA         Lattice angle gamma, degrees (default: 90).
  --site SYMBOL X Y Z   One symmetrically-distinct Wyckoff site: element symbol and fractional x y z. Repeat --site for each distinct site.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry precision, used both for the post-build symmetry detection and for --reduce (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default, matches stb-symmetry/stb-unitcell).
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry angle tolerance in degrees (default: 5.0, pymatgen's own default).
  --reduce {primitive,conventional,refined}
                        Reduce the space-group-expanded structure to its primitive/conventional/refined cell (via stb-unitcell's own reduction) before writing. Off by default -- the raw space-group-expanded structure is written as-is.
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax the final structure with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) before writing it out -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the cell. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_crystalbuilder_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the raw space-group-expanded structure and the final structure (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: crystal.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
