  stb-crystalbuilder --spacegroup Fm-3m --a 3.52 --site Ni 0 0 0
  stb-crystalbuilder --spacegroup 225 --a 3.52 --site Ni 0 0 0 -o fcc_ni.fdf
  stb-crystalbuilder --spacegroup Fd-3m --a 8.396 \
      --site Fe 0.125 0.125 0.125 --site Fe 0.5 0.5 0.5 \
      --site O 0.2548 0.2548 0.2548
  stb-crystalbuilder --spacegroup Fm-3m --a 3.52 --site Ni 0 0 0 \
      --reduce primitive --ml-relax --save-report --view

Notes:
  - Bulk (3D) crystals only -- see the description above for how to get
    a 2D/1D structure out of this tool's output.

stb-crystalcast.help:
usage: stb-crystalcast [-h] [--substitute OLD:NEW [OLD:NEW ...]] [--subgroup]
                       [--supergroup] [--target-group TARGET_GROUP]
                       [--group-type {t,k,t+k}] [--eps EPS] [--d-tol D_TOL] [-f FILE]
                       [--dim {3,2,1,0}] [--group GROUP] [--molecular]
                       [--list-molecules] [--species SPECIES [SPECIES ...]]
                       [--num-ions NUM_IONS [NUM_IONS ...]]
                       [--volume-factor VOLUME_FACTOR] [--thickness THICKNESS]
                       [--area AREA] [--vacuum VACUUM]
                       [--lattice A B C ALPHA BETA GAMMA] [--sites SITES [SITES ...]]
                       [--max-attempts MAX_ATTEMPTS] [--count COUNT] [--seed SEED]
                       [--ml-rank] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                       [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                       [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE] [--save-report] [--view]
                       [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Casts one or more random structures compatible with a given symmetry group.
Give a symmetry group and a composition (species + how many of each) -- pyxtal
places the atoms on randomly chosen, symmetry-compatible Wyckoff positions
for you. This is the inverse of stb-crystalbuilder: use crystalbuilder when
you already know the exact Wyckoff sites you want, use crystalcast when you
want valid candidate structures generated for you (e.g. as starting guesses
for structure prediction). --molecular packs whole rigid molecules (instead
of bare atoms) into the symmetry group. --ml-rank pre-screens generated
candidates by MACE relaxed energy. --substitute/--subgroup/--supergroup
all instead operate on an existing structure read via -f/--file:
--substitute swaps elements while preserving the symmetry framework,
--subgroup/--supergroup search for related lower/higher-symmetry
structures. (To inspect an existing structure's own symmetry/Wyckoff
decomposition instead of generating or transforming one, use
stb-symmetry or stb-unitcell.)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --substitute OLD:NEW [OLD:NEW ...]
                        Substitute elements in an existing structure (read via -f/--file), preserving its symmetry framework: one or more OLD:NEW pairs, e.g. --substitute Cl:F Na:K. Mutually exclusive with --subgroup/--supergroup and the generation options below.
  --subgroup            Generate lower-symmetry subgroup variant(s) of an existing structure (read via -f/--file) -- a symmetry-breaking distortion. Up to --count candidates are written (numbered like --count > 1 in generation mode). Optionally narrow the search with --target-group/--group-type/--eps. Mutually exclusive with --substitute/--supergroup and the generation options.
  --supergroup          Search for higher-symmetry supergroup structure(s) of an existing structure (read via -f/--file) towards --target-group (required -- the installed pyxtal doesn't support auto-searching all possible supergroups). Mutually exclusive with --substitute/--subgroup and the generation options below.
  --target-group TARGET_GROUP
                        Target space group number. Optional filter for --subgroup (only search towards this specific subgroup); required destination for --supergroup.
  --group-type {t,k,t+k}
                        --subgroup only: 't' (translationengleiche), 'k' (klassengleiche), or 't+k' relation to search (default: t).
  --eps EPS             --subgroup only: perturbation applied to atomic coordinates when breaking symmetry (default: 0.05).
  --d-tol D_TOL         --supergroup only: maximum atomic-displacement tolerance allowed when searching for a higher-symmetry parent (default: 1.0).
  -f FILE, --file FILE  Input .fdf structure file. Required with --substitute/--subgroup/--supergroup, unused otherwise.
  --dim {3,2,1,0}       Structure dimensionality: 3 = bulk (space group, default), 2 = layer (layer group, periodic in a/b with vacuum along c), 1 = rod/wire (rod group, periodic along c with vacuum in a/b), 0 = isolated cluster (point group, no periodicity). --molecular does not support --dim 0 (upstream pyxtal limitation). Generation mode only.
  --group GROUP         Symmetry group identifier, meaning depends on --dim: space group number/symbol (dim 3, e.g. 225 or 'Fm-3m'), layer group number 1-80 (dim 2), rod group number 1-75 (dim 1), or point group number/Schoenflies symbol 1-32 (dim 0, e.g. 20 or 'D3d'). Required in generation mode.
  --molecular           Treat each --species entry as a whole rigid molecule instead of a bare element: a name from pyxtal's bundled collection (see --list-molecules), a path to a .xyz/.gjf/.g03/.json file, or a SMILES string as 'SMILES.smi' (needs the optional 'rdkit' package).
  --list-molecules      Print the molecule names bundled with pyxtal (usable directly as --species with --molecular) and exit.
  --species SPECIES [SPECIES ...]
                        Element symbols (or, with --molecular, molecule identifiers) in the structure, e.g. --species Ni O. Required in generation mode.
  --num-ions NUM_IONS [NUM_IONS ...]
                        Number of atoms (or, with --molecular, molecules) of each --species, same order and count, e.g. --num-ions 4 8. Required in generation mode.
  --volume-factor VOLUME_FACTOR
                        Scales the estimated cell volume before placing atoms; raise it if generation keeps failing to fit atoms without overlap (default: 1.1, pyxtal's own default).
  --thickness THICKNESS
                        Layer thickness in Ang (--dim 2 only; default: chosen automatically by pyxtal).
  --area AREA           Rod cross-sectional area in Ang^2 (--dim 1 only; default: chosen automatically by pyxtal).
  --vacuum VACUUM       Vacuum padding in Ang around the cluster, on every side (--dim 0 only, matches stb-molecule's --vacuum; default: 10.0).
  --lattice A B C ALPHA BETA GAMMA
                        Fix the cell instead of estimating it from --volume-factor, e.g. for matching a known experimental cell: A B C ALPHA BETA GAMMA (Ang/degrees). Not valid with --dim 0 (use --vacuum instead). For --dim 2/1, only the periodic direction(s) are actually honored -- the vacuum direction(s) are still sized by --thickness/--area/pyxtal's own default, same as without --lattice.
  --sites SITES [SITES ...]
                        Pre-assign Wyckoff positions instead of leaving every site random: one entry per --species, each a comma-separated list of Wyckoff labels summing to that species' --num-ions, e.g. --species Na O --num-ions 4 8 --sites 4a 4b,4c. Default: fully random assignment.
  --max-attempts MAX_ATTEMPTS
                        Internal retries pyxtal allows itself per structure to find a non-overlapping placement before giving up on it (default: 10).
  --count COUNT         Number of independent random structures to generate in generation mode, or number of candidates to keep in --subgroup/--supergroup mode (default: 1).
  --seed SEED           Random seed. Same seed + same inputs reproduces the same batch of structures (default: not seeded, different every run). With --molecular, only the lattice is reproduced this way -- molecule orientations are not (an upstream pyxtal limitation). Unused outside generation mode.
  --ml-rank             Generation mode only. After generating --count structures, quickly relaxes each one's positions with a MACE potential, prints them ranked by relaxed energy, and writes each output file with its relaxed geometry. A relative comparison from a fast ML potential, not an absolute DFT formation energy.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-rank (default: medium). Only valid together with --ml-rank.
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-rank, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size. Only valid together with --ml-rank.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry precision: for generation, used to re-detect each --dim 3 candidate's actual space group; for --substitute/--subgroup/--supergroup, the tolerance passed to pyxtal's own symmetry detection (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default, matches stb-symmetry/stb-unitcell).
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Angle tolerance in degrees for symmetry detection (default: 5.0, matches stb-symmetry/stb-unitcell).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_crystalcast_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) of every structure written by this run (for --substitute/--subgroup/--supergroup, the input structure is shown first, as frame 0) -- page through frames in ase-gui. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: crystalcast.fdf). With --count > 1 (generation, --subgroup, or --supergroup), each structure is written as '<output>_<N>.fdf'; the tool refuses to run if any of those numbered names already exist, to avoid silently overwriting unrelated files.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-crystalcast --group 225 --species Ni O --num-ions 4 8
  stb-crystalcast --group Fd-3m --species Fe O --num-ions 8 16 \
      --count 5 --seed 42 -o spinel.fdf
  stb-crystalcast --group 225 --species Ni O --num-ions 4 8 --count 5 \
      --ml-rank --model medium
  stb-crystalcast --group 225 --species Na Cl --num-ions 4 4 \
      --lattice 5.64 5.64 5.64 90 90 90
  stb-crystalcast --group 225 --species Na Cl --num-ions 4 4 --sites 4a 4b
  stb-crystalcast --dim 2 --group 65 --species C --num-ions 6 --thickness 3.4
  stb-crystalcast --dim 0 --group D3d --species C --num-ions 6 --vacuum 12
  stb-crystalcast --molecular --group 19 --species H2O --num-ions 4
  stb-crystalcast --molecular --group 14 --species aspirin --num-ions 4 -o aspirin.fdf
  stb-crystalcast --list-molecules
  stb-crystalcast --substitute Cl:F -f rocksalt.fdf -o rocksalt_f.fdf
  stb-crystalcast --subgroup -f spinel_1.fdf --count 5 -o distorted.fdf
  stb-crystalcast --supergroup --target-group 225 -f distorted_1.fdf -o parent.fdf
  stb-crystalcast --group 225 --species Ni O --num-ions 4 8 --save-report --view

stb-cube.help:
usage: stb-cube [-h] -l LABEL -t {VT,VH,RHO,BADER} [-o OUTPUT]
                [--spin {total,up,down,diff}] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Convert SIESTA Grid files (VT, VH, RHO, BADER) to Gaussian Cube format.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        System Label (required).
  -t {VT,VH,RHO,BADER}, --type {VT,VH,RHO,BADER}
                        File type to convert.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Custom output filename. Default: label_type.cube
  --spin {total,up,down,diff}
                        Which spin channel to convert, for spin-polarized calculations: 'total' (up+down, default), 'up', 'down', or 'diff' (up-down, i.e. the local magnetization/spin density). Auto-identified and cross-checked against <label>.HSX when present: ignored (falls back to 'total') for non-spin-polarized or non-collinear/spin-orbit calculations, where up/down/diff doesn't apply. Verified against a real SIESTA spin-polarized O2 run: 'diff' integrates to exactly the spin moment SIESTA itself reports.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_cube_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb_convert --label graphene --type RHO
  stb_convert -l system -t VT -o potential.cube

stb-defect.help:
usage: stb-defect [-h] -f FILENAME --type {vacancy,substitution,interstitial}
                  [--index INDEX | --nearest X Y Z | --all-inequivalent-sites]
                  [--nearest-format {fractional,cartesian}]
                  [--filter-species FILTER_SPECIES] [--symprec SYMPREC] [--ml-rank]
                  [--new-species NEW_SPECIES] [--position X Y Z]
                  [--position-format {fractional,cartesian}] [--species SPECIES]
                  [--ml-relax] [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                  [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report] [--view]
                  [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Introduces a point defect (vacancy, substitution, interstitial) into a SIESTA FDF structure.
Select the site by raw atom index, by the position closest to a target, or
automatically at every symmetrically distinct site.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input structure file (.fdf).
  --type {vacancy,substitution,interstitial}
                        Defect type to introduce.
  --index INDEX         Comma-separated 1-indexed atom(s) to remove/substitute, e.g. '3,7'.
  --nearest X Y Z       Selects the atom closest to this position (vacancy/substitution).
  --all-inequivalent-sites
                        Generate one output structure per symmetrically distinct site (via spglib), instead of a single combined structure -- e.g. to compare defect formation energies across all inequivalent sites rather than picking one by hand. Writes '<output>_site<N>.fdf' per site instead of a single --output file. Narrow to one species with --filter-species.
  --nearest-format {fractional,cartesian}
                        How to interpret --nearest. Default: fractional.
  --filter-species FILTER_SPECIES
                        Restrict --nearest's or --all-inequivalent-sites' search to atoms of this element.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry precision for --all-inequivalent-sites and the before/after symmetry table (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default, matches stb-symmetry/stb-unitcell).
  --ml-rank             Only valid with --all-inequivalent-sites. Quickly relaxes each candidate site's local geometry (positions only) with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]), then prints them ranked by relaxed energy -- a fast pre-screen for which site is most likely favorable, before spending DFT time on all of them. Overwrites each site's output file with its relaxed geometry. This is a relative comparison from a fast ML potential, not an absolute DFT formation energy. Mutually exclusive with --ml-relax (which already relaxes every output structure, just without the ranking table).
  --new-species NEW_SPECIES
                        Replacement element symbol (required for --type substitution).
  --position X Y Z      Position of the new atom (required for --type interstitial).
  --position-format {fractional,cartesian}
                        How to interpret --position. Default: fractional.
  --species SPECIES     Element symbol of the new atom (required for --type interstitial).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax every output structure with a MACE potential before writing it out (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) -- positions only by default. Off by default. Mutually exclusive with --ml-rank.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the cell -- any vacuum-padded axis always stays exactly fixed. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax/--ml-rank (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax/--ml-rank, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_defect_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the input structure and every output structure (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file(s). Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: defect.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-defect -f structure.fdf --type vacancy --index 5
  stb-defect -f structure.fdf --type substitution --index 5 --new-species Ge
  stb-defect -f structure.fdf --type vacancy --nearest 0.5 0.5 0.5 --filter-species O
  stb-defect -f structure.fdf --type interstitial --position 0.5 0.5 0.5 --species N
  stb-defect -f structure.fdf --type vacancy --all-inequivalent-sites --filter-species O
  stb-defect -f structure.fdf --type vacancy --index 5 --ml-relax --save-report --view

stb-density.help:
usage: stb-density [-h] -l LABEL [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--3d | --profile] [-a {0,1,2}]
                   [-p POS] [--spin] [--rho2 FILE] [--iso-min RHO] [--cube]
                   [--vmin VMIN] [--vmax VMAX] [--contour] [--save-report]
                   [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [--no-intro] [-v]

Converts a SIESTA charge-density grid (.RHO) to 2D maps, 3D point clouds, or planar-averaged 1D profiles.
Plots the total charge density by default. If the .RHO file is
spin-polarized, the spin density (up-down) is now detected and reported
automatically alongside it -- --spin no longer needs to be remembered just
to notice a magnetic calculation; pass --spin to look at ONLY the spin
density (skip the charge section) instead. --rho2 subtracts a second .RHO
file's density from the first (Delta rho = rho1 - rho2), the standard way
to visualize charge transfer/bonding (e.g. adsorbate+substrate vs. isolated
fragments) -- both files must be on the same grid. --iso-min filters low
-|density| points out of a --3d export, since an unfiltered production-size
grid can produce a multi-GB file dominated by near-zero vacuum/interstitial
points. --profile writes the planar average along the chosen axis instead
of a map (useful for slabs/interfaces). --cube additionally writes a
standard Gaussian cube file (needs a <label>.XV or <label>.fdf for the
geometry) for real isosurface rendering in VESTA/VMD/Avogadro. --vmin/
--vmax fix the colorbar range manually for the primary quantity, e.g. to
compare several slices on the same scale.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        System Label (looks for .RHO file)
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write the data/gnuplot/cube/report files and references.bib into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --3d                  Export full 3D volume
  --profile             Write the planar average of the density along --axis as a 1D profile (average taken over the other two axes) instead of a 2D/3D map -- useful for slabs, interfaces, and superlattices
  -a {0,1,2}, --axis {0,1,2}
                        For a slice/profile: the axis normal to the cut plane (slice) or the axis the profile varies along (profile) (0=X, 1=Y, 2=Z)
  -p POS, --pos POS     Position (Angstrom) of the 2D cut (ignored in --profile mode)
  --spin                Process ONLY the spin density (up-down), skipping the charge density section entirely -- only available for spin-polarized .RHO files. Without this flag, spin density is now detected and reported automatically alongside the charge density whenever the .RHO file has it, no flag needed.
  --rho2 FILE           A second .RHO file to subtract from the first (Delta rho = rho1 - rho2), e.g. to visualize charge transfer upon adsorption or defect formation. Must be on the same grid (same shape) as <label>.RHO. If both files are spin-polarized, the spin difference is computed too.
  --iso-min RHO         For --3d: only export/preview points with |density| >= this threshold (e/Ang^3) -- keeps the point cloud a manageable size and visually meaningful instead of dominated by near-zero points
  --cube                Also write the primary quantity's full 3D grid as a Gaussian .cube file (needs <label>.XV or <label>.fdf for the geometry) -- for real 3D isosurface rendering in VESTA/VMD/Avogadro, which handle volumetric data better than a point cloud. Applies to the charge density, or the spin density if --spin was given -- not both at once.
  --vmin VMIN           Fix the colorbar/palette lower bound manually (e/Ang^3) for the primary quantity, e.g. to compare several slices on the same scale. Auto-detected spin density always uses its own zero-symmetric range regardless of this.
  --vmax VMAX           Fix the colorbar/palette upper bound manually (e/Ang^3), for the primary quantity (see --vmin).
  --contour             Overlay contour lines on a 2D slice map/preview (ignored for --3d/--profile)
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_density_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a .gplot script next to each .dat file this run generates. Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of each quantity plotted this run (slice heatmap / profile line / 3D scatter, matching the mode). Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-density --label siesta
  stb-density --label siesta --3d --iso-min 0.01
  stb-density --label siesta --spin
  stb-density --label adsorbed --rho2 isolated.RHO
  stb-density --label siesta --profile --axis 2
  stb-density --label siesta --cube --view

stb-dftu.help:
usage: stb-dftu [-h] [--fdf PATH] [--species SPECIES [SPECIES ...]] [--u U [U ...]]
                [--use-reference] [--j J [J ...]]
                [--shell {3d,4d,4f,5d,5f} [{3d,4d,4f,5d,5f} ...]] [-o OUTPUT]
                [--list-reference] [--suggest ELEMENT] [--save-report] [-v]
                [--no-intro]

Generates a ready-to-use %block LDAU.proj snippet for one or more species.
You supply U (and optionally J) explicitly -- this tool never guesses or
estimates U for you. --list-reference prints a small table of literature GGA+U
values (citation included) as a convenience starting point; --suggest prints
that value for one element with a clear disclaimer. Neither is ever used
automatically -- --u must always be given to produce a block, unless you pass
--use-reference to explicitly opt in to auto-filling U from that same table.
--fdf reads the species list off an existing structure file instead of typing
--species by hand -- combine it with --use-reference to build a block straight
from a structure: only metal species with a tabulated value go into the block,
with a loud warning; non-metals are skipped silently and untabulated metals
are skipped with a warning. For a
first-principles U computed from your own system via the Cococcioni & de
Gironcoli linear-response method, see the Workflow menu's "Hubbard U (Linear
Response)" entry (stb-hubbardu / stb-hubbarduAnalysis) instead.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --fdf PATH            Read the species list off this .fdf structure file instead of typing --species by hand. If --species is also given, it filters down to that subset (each one must be present in the file).
  --species SPECIES [SPECIES ...]
                        Species label(s) to add a DFT+U correction to. Required unless --fdf is given.
  --u U [U ...]         Hubbard U (eV), one per species, in the same order. Required unless --use-reference is given (and every species has a tabulated value).
  --use-reference       For any species without an explicit --u, auto-fill U from the tabulated Materials Project reference table (see --list-reference). A non-metal species (no default correlated shell, e.g. O, Si) is silently skipped -- DFT+U doesn't apply to it. A metal species with no tabulated value is skipped too, but with a warning. The block is built from whatever is left; errors out only if nothing qualifies.
  --j J [J ...]         Exchange J (eV), one per --species (default: 0.0 for each).
  --shell {3d,4d,4f,5d,5f} [{3d,4d,4f,5d,5f} ...]
                        Correlated shell per species (3d/4d/5d/4f/5f). Default: the standard shell for each species (transition metals -> (n)d, lanthanides -> 4f, actinides -> 5f).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Also save the block to this file (in addition to printing it).
  --list-reference      Print the literature GGA+U reference table (with citation) and exit.
  --suggest ELEMENT     Print the literature reference U for one element (with a disclaimer) and exit -- does not generate a block.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_dftu_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-dftu --species Mn --u 3.9
  stb-dftu --species Fe Co --u 5.3 3.32 --shell 3d 3d
  stb-dftu --fdf calc.fdf --use-reference
  stb-dftu --fdf calc.fdf --species Mn --u 3.9
  stb-dftu --list-reference
  stb-dftu --suggest Ni

stb-dos.help:
usage: stb-dos [-h] [--label LABEL]
               [--type {total,atom,species} [{total,atom,species} ...]]
               [--shift SHIFT] [--estimate-from-dos]
               [--dos-threshold-frac DOS_THRESHOLD_FRAC] [--projection {l,ml,none}]
               [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v]
               [--no-intro]
               [filename]

Parse a PDOS.xml file and generate Gnuplot-ready .dat files.

positional arguments:
  filename              The input .PDOS.xml file to process. Give this before --type (see epilog). Optional if --label is given (resolves to '<label>.PDOS.xml').

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA label. Shorthand for filename='<label>.PDOS.xml' if filename isn't given directly, and (with --shift vbm/cbm) used to locate a companion '<label>.bands'/'<label>.EIG' next to it. One of filename or --label is required. If filename is given explicitly without --label, the label is still derived automatically from its own name for --shift vbm/cbm.
  --type {total,atom,species} [{total,atom,species} ...]
                        Type(s) of DOS to output.
                          total:   Sum of all atoms.
                          atom:    One file for each atom.
                          species: One file for each chemical species (e.g., C, N, B).
                        You can select multiple, e.g., --type total species (default: all three)
  --shift SHIFT         Energy shift to apply.
                          'fermi': Automatically shift by the Fermi energy (default).
                          'vbm'/'cbm': Shift by the Valence Band Maximum / Conduction Band
                            Minimum, computed from a companion '<label>.bands' (preferred) or
                            '<label>.EIG' file -- see --label. Falls back to an approximate
                            estimate from the DOS itself only with --estimate-from-dos.
                          '0.0':   Use an absolute energy scale (no shift).
                          '-1.23': Apply a manual shift of -1.23 eV.
  --estimate-from-dos   With --shift vbm/cbm: if no companion '<label>.bands'/'<label>.EIG' is found, fall back to an approximate VBM/CBM estimated directly from the DOS itself (blurred by its own energy broadening -- less precise than a real .bands/.EIG). Off by default: without it, a missing .bands/.EIG is a clear error, not a silent approximation.
  --dos-threshold-frac DOS_THRESHOLD_FRAC
                        Only used by --shift vbm/cbm's --estimate-from-dos fallback: fraction of the peak total DOS above which the curve is considered 'occupied'/'empty' again past the gap region (default: 0.01).
  --projection {l,ml,none}
                        Orbital projection detail level.
                          l:    Aggregate by angular momentum (s, p, d, f). (default)
                          ml:   Project by magnetic quantum number (s, px, py, pz, dxy, etc.).
                          none: No orbital breakdown -- every orbital (including l>3, e.g. g) collapses into a single 'total' column per atom/species/grand-total.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write dos_total.dat, dos_per_atom/, and dos_per_species/ into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_dos_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a .gplot gnuplot script next to every .dat file this run generates (dos_total.dat, each dos_per_atom/*.dat, each dos_per_species/*.dat). Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the total DOS before exiting. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-dos siesta.PDOS.xml --type total species --projection ml
Put the filename first: --type takes one or more values, so anything
written after it (including the filename) is consumed as another type.

stb-effmass.help:
usage: stb-effmass [-h] [--label LABEL] [--wfsx WFSX] [--hsx-file HSX_FILE]
                   [--k-index K_INDEX | --k-point KX KY KZ] [--spin {0,1}] --band BAND
                   [--fermi FERMI] [--bands-file BANDS_FILE] [--fermi-file FERMI_FILE]
                   [--gap-tol GAP_TOL] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report]
                   [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Effective mass tensor (Voigt) and band velocity for one chosen (k, band) eigenstate, from a SIESTA .WFSX + .HSX.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Auto-detects <label>.WFSX, falling back to <label>.selected.WFSX then <label>.bands.WFSX, and, unless --hsx-file overrides it, <label>.HSX (mandatory -- no approximate fallback). Mutually exclusive with --wfsx (not --hsx-file -- see its own help).
  --wfsx WFSX           Explicit path to the .WFSX file (alternative to --label).
  --hsx-file HSX_FILE   Explicit .HSX path. Required if --wfsx is used instead of --label; optional (and common) together WITH --label too, since the real file is often not literally named <label>.HSX.
  --k-index K_INDEX     0-based index into the .WFSX's own k-point order (default: 0 if neither --k-index nor --k-point is given).
  --k-point KX KY KZ    Match by k-point vector instead of index (matched via sisl's read_eigenstate).
  --spin {0,1}          Spin channel (default: 0; must be 0 for a non-polarized calculation).
  --band BAND           Which band at the chosen k: an integer N (1-based), or 'vbm'/'cbm' (requires --fermi, --bands-file, --fermi-file, or an auto-detected .out log -- see below).
  --fermi FERMI         Fermi energy (eV) for --band vbm/cbm. Highest-priority source if given.
  --bands-file BANDS_FILE
                        Companion .bands file to read the Fermi energy from, for --band vbm/cbm.
  --fermi-file FERMI_FILE
                        Explicit SIESTA .out log to read the Fermi energy from, for --band vbm/cbm -- an alternative to --bands-file for a run with no saved .bands file. Not assumed to be named after --label.
  --gap-tol GAP_TOL     Energy tolerance in eV for VBM/CBM classification (default: 0.01). Same meaning as stb-bands/stb-fatbands/stb-wfdensity.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write effmass.dat/velocity.dat (with --save-gnuplot) and stb_effmass_report.txt/references.bib into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_effmass_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write effmass.dat/velocity.dat + a real .gplot bar-chart script. Off by default.
  --view                Show a matplotlib bar-chart preview (effective mass + velocity components) before finishing. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-effmass --label siesta --band vbm --fermi -4.2
  stb-effmass --label siesta --k-index 0 --band 1
  stb-effmass --label siesta --band vbm --fermi-file calc.out \
      --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-elasticAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-elasticAnalysis [-h] [-f FILE] [-d DIR] [--method {stress,energy}]
                           [--dimensionality {auto,3d,2d,1d}]
                           [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--symmetry-method {basic,full}]
                           [--reference-structure REFERENCE_STRUCTURE]
                           [--symprec SYMPREC] [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE]
                           [--eggbox-tolerance EGGBOX_TOLERANCE]
                           [--fit-quality-tolerance FIT_QUALITY_TOLERANCE]
                           [--plot-dir PLOT_DIR] [--save-gnuplot] [--view]
                           [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Siesta Elastic Properties Analyzer (STB Suite)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILE, --file FILE  Siesta log/output filename inside strain folders (default:
                        calc.out)
  -d DIR, --dir DIR     Directory to scan for 'strain_*' run folders and the
                        undeformed reference_structure.fdf (default: elastic_runs,
                        matching stb-elasticInputs' own --output-dir default). Accepts
                        either stb-elasticInputs' own nested output layout -- point
                        this at a single direction's own subfolder (e.g.
                        elastic_runs/xx) for that direction alone, or at the top-level
                        output directory itself to automatically use every direction
                        found under it -- or a flat directory of 'strain_*' folders.
  --method {stress,energy}
                        Which physical quantity to fit (default: stress). 'stress':
                        the existing stress-strain linear fit (sigma = C . epsilon),
                        see --symmetry-method. 'energy': an energy-strain (parabolic)
                        fit (E = E0 + (V0/2) gamma^T C gamma) over the pure+combined
                        patterns written by stb-elasticInputs --method energy -- a
                        physically independent cross-check (total energy vs. the
                        stress tensor), since a code's total energy and stress can
                        have different sources of numerical error. Always uses the
                        general symmetry-allowed-subspace fit (--symmetry-method
                        doesn't apply); requires --reference-structure.
  --dimensionality {auto,3d,2d,1d}
                        Physical dimensionality of the material, controlling report
                        units and which constants are shown (default: auto). 'auto':
                        detected from --reference-structure using the same vacuum-gap
                        convention as stb-elasticInputs/stb-kgrid/stb-strain (see
                        --vacuum-gap) -- 0 vacuum-padded axes -> 3d (GPa), 1 -> 2d
                        (N/m), 2 -> 1d (nN); falls back to 3d with a warning if
                        --reference-structure isn't readable, or if the vacuum sits on
                        an axis other than this workflow's assumed convention (in-
                        plane xy for 2D, wire-along-c for 1D). '3d'/'2d'/'1d': force
                        the mode manually and skip detection entirely.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum gap threshold in Ang (default: 10.0) used only by
                        --dimensionality auto, same convention as stb-
                        elasticInputs/stb-kgrid/stb-strain.
  --symmetry-method {basic,full}
                        How to use detected symmetry (default: basic). 'basic': exact
                        reconstruction/pooling only when a single point-group
                        operation maps one canonical strain direction exactly onto
                        another (misses reductions like hexagonal's C11=C22, which
                        come from the FULL elastic tensor's invariance, not a pairwise
                        direction match). 'full': fits the whole stiffness matrix at
                        once, constrained a priori to the point group's symmetry-
                        allowed subspace -- catches every crystal system's correct
                        independent-constant count uniformly (cubic, hexagonal,
                        trigonal, ...), at the cost of being a global least-squares
                        fit rather than an exact per-column one. Requires --reference-
                        structure to be available.
  --reference-structure REFERENCE_STRUCTURE
                        UNDEFORMED structure file (default: reference_structure.fdf
                        inside --dir, written automatically by stb-elasticInputs next
                        to the strain_*/ folders), used only to detect symmetry for
                        the diagnostic/pooling/reconstruction across equivalent
                        directions. Must be the undeformed structure, not one from
                        inside a strain folder -- a single-axis strain genuinely
                        lowers the symmetry (e.g. cubic strained along x alone is
                        exactly tetragonal, not 'cubic with noise'), so reading
                        symmetry from a strained structure would silently misdetect
                        it. Never required -- falls back to independent per-direction
                        fitting if unavailable.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own
                        default). Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure
                        relaxed with a looser force tolerance -- a tighter value than
                        the relaxation's own residual numerical noise can misdetect
                        the true space group.
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry angle tolerance in degrees (default: 5.0, pymatgen's
                        own default), same use as --symprec.
  --eggbox-tolerance EGGBOX_TOLERANCE
                        Relative difference (%, default: 5.0) above which the
                        mandatory eggbox cross-check (--method stress only, see
                        section [3] of the report) flags a direction. Every diagonal
                        constant actually run is computed two independent ways from
                        the SAME calc.out files -- a stress-linear fit and an energy-
                        parabolic fit -- with no new DFT calculations; a disagreement
                        beyond this tolerance is a hint of eggbox (or other numerical)
                        contamination in the stress data. Needs --reference-structure;
                        skipped with a warning (not an error) if it isn't available.
  --fit-quality-tolerance FIT_QUALITY_TOLERANCE
                        R^2 (default: 0.995) below which the mandatory per-direction
                        stress-vs-strain fit-quality check (--method stress only,
                        section [3] of the report) flags a direction -- a clean linear
                        elastic fit should sit well above this. Also flags a non-
                        negligible residual stress at zero strain (same relative-
                        contribution criterion as the energy method's linear-term
                        check). No new DFT calculations: reuses the same stress-strain
                        fit each direction's column already needed.
  --plot-dir PLOT_DIR   Directory (default: elastic_plots, created only if --save-
                        gnuplot is given) to write the raw fitting data + gnuplot
                        scripts into -- one .dat/.gplot pair per direction (--method
                        stress) or pattern (--method energy), plus a combined
                        overview.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write the raw fitting data + gnuplot scripts into --plot-
                        dir (same data+.gplot convention as the rest of the suite,
                        e.g. stb-strainAnalysis). Off by default -- no new DFT
                        calculations either way, reuses the data/fit already computed
                        for the report.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview (every measured
                        direction/pattern overlaid with its own fit) before finishing.
                        Never saved to disk -- pass --save-gnuplot for that. Off by
                        default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to elastic_stage2.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

stb-elasticInputs.help:
usage: stb-elasticInputs [-h] -s STRUCTURE -c CALC [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                         [--method {stress,energy}] [--dirs DIRS [DIRS ...]]
                         [--symmetry-method {basic,full}] [--max MAX] [--steps STEPS]
                         [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                         [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE] [--save-report] [-v]
                         [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 2: applies one or more canonical Voigt strains to a SIESTA structure and writes one ready-to-run folder (structure + calc.fdf + config_extra.fdf + pseudopotentials) per scanned strain value, forcing a pure single-point SCF at each imposed strain. Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each folder yourself, then use stb-elasticAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input structure.fdf -- lattice + atomic coordinates. Only this file's %block LatticeVectors is rewritten per strain step; everything else is preserved verbatim. Atomic coordinates MUST be fractional (checked in [1] of the report -- Cartesian positions would not scale with the strained cell).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template -- SCF/basis/MD settings, normally %including the structure file above by name. Copied into every generated folder with one line added: '%include config_extra.fdf', prepended at the very top (see [4] of the report for why) -- this forces every generated folder to a pure single-point SCF, regardless of what MD settings this template itself contains.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path. If given, the required pseudopotential for every species in the structure is copied into every generated folder, so it's immediately ready for SIESTA.
  --method {stress,energy}
                        Physical quantity the generated strains are meant to feed (default: stress). 'stress': single-component canonical Voigt strains, for stb-elasticAnalysis's stress-strain fit (--method stress there too). 'energy': a point-group-selected set of pure AND combined (two Voigt components at once, e.g. 'xx+yy') strain patterns for an energy-strain (parabolic) fit -- combined patterns are physically required for off-diagonal constants there, since a pure single-component strain's energy curvature only ever determines its own diagonal constant. Always auto-selects (--dirs must be left at its 'all' default); needs more DFT calculations than --method stress for the same crystal system, since each pattern only yields one number (a curvature) instead of a full stress column.
  --dirs DIRS [DIRS ...]
                        List of directions to generate.
                        Options: [xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz, bi, hydro, all].
                        Example: --dirs xx yy xy
                        'all' auto-reduces to 1 representative direction per symmetry-
                        equivalent group (e.g. just 2 of the 6 for a cubic material) --
                        stb-elasticAnalysis reconstructs the rest by symmetry. Pass every
                        direction explicitly (not 'all') to run all 6 anyway, e.g. to get
                        stb-elasticAnalysis's diagnostic comparison across truly independent
                        DFT calculations instead.
  --symmetry-method {basic,full}
                        How 'all' picks which directions to actually run (default: basic). 'basic': only reduces when a single point-group operation maps one canonical direction exactly onto another (e.g. cubic); misses reductions like hexagonal's C11=C22, which come from the full elastic tensor's symmetry, not a pairwise direction match. 'full': picks the minimal set of directions that fully determines the point group's independent elastic constants (greedy rank selection) -- catches hexagonal/trigonal reductions too. Must match the --symmetry-method passed to stb-elasticAnalysis later.
  --max MAX             Max strain % (default: 2.0)
  --steps STEPS         Steps per direction (default: 4)
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Top-level directory (default: elastic_runs). Run folders go into its own '<output-dir>/<direction>/strain_<direction>_<val>/' subfolder, same convention as stb-strain's own --output-dir -- so stb-elasticAnalysis can just 'cd <output-dir>' and find everything (including reference_structure.fdf) with no extra flags.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum gap threshold in Ang used to detect which lattice axes are periodic vs. vacuum-padded (default: 10.0), same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-strain. Requested directions touching a vacuum-padded axis are skipped with a warning instead of generated.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default), used for the symmetry-based direction reduction and the informational note about triclinic/monoclinic structures. Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance -- a tighter value than the relaxation's own residual numerical noise can misdetect the true space group.
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry angle tolerance in degrees (default: 5.0, pymatgen's own default), same use as --symprec.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/elastic_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-elasticInputs -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --dirs all
  stb-elasticInputs -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf --dirs xx yy xy --max 1.5 --steps 6 --save-report

stb-eosAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-eosAnalysis [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE]
                       [--eos {birchmurnaghan,birch_murnaghan,vinet,murnaghan,sj,all}]
                       [--target-pressure GPA [GPA ...]] [-o OUTPUT] [--save-report]
                       [-v] [--no-intro]

Aggregates a stb-eosInputs 'vol_*' sweep of real SIESTA calculations and fits an equation of state (Birch-Murnaghan by default) to get V0/E0/B0 (bulk modulus)/B0'.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Directory containing the 'vol_*' run folders (default: eos_runs).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each run folder (default: calc.out).
  --eos {birchmurnaghan,birch_murnaghan,vinet,murnaghan,sj,all}
                        Equation-of-state form to fit (default: birchmurnaghan). 'sj' = stabilized jellium (no B0' reported). 'all' fits every form on the same data and reports them side by side (the plotted curve still uses birchmurnaghan); mutually exclusive with --target-pressure.
  --target-pressure GPA [GPA ...]
                        One or more target external pressures (GPa) -- inverts the fitted EOS (P = -dE/dV) to report the predicted equilibrium volume and linear lattice-parameter scale factor at each one. Not available with --eos all (pick one specific form first).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename (no extension) for the .dat/.gplot outputs (default: eos_curve).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_eosAnalysis_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-eosAnalysis --dir eos_runs --file calc.out
  stb-eosAnalysis --dir eos_runs --eos vinet

stb-eosInputs.help:
usage: stb-eosInputs [-h] --file FILE [--n-volumes N_VOLUMES]
                     [--strain-range STRAIN_RANGE] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                     [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [-v] [--no-intro]

Generates a set of isotropically-scaled-volume SIESTA input folders for a real-DFT equation-of-state (E vs V) scan -- run SIESTA in each one (fixed cell, positions may relax), then aggregate with stb-eosAnalysis. The real-SIESTA analog of stb-mleos's MACE-driven in-memory scan.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf). Atomic coordinates must be in fractional (ScaledCartesian/Fractional) format, same requirement as stb-strain.
  --n-volumes N_VOLUMES
                        Number of volumes to scan (default: 9). Needs >= 5 for a robust 4-parameter EOS fit downstream in stb-eosAnalysis.
  --strain-range STRAIN_RANGE
                        Max isotropic volume strain, % (default: 5.0), spanning [-strain-range, +strain-range] -- same meaning as stb-mleos's own --strain-range.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write the 'vol_<pct>' run folders into (default: eos_runs).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes -- bulk-only, rejects any vacuum-padded structure (default: 10.0).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-eosInputs --file structure.fdf
  stb-eosInputs --file structure.fdf --n-volumes 11 --strain-range 8.0 -o eos_runs

stb-fatbands.help:
usage: stb-fatbands [-h] [--label LABEL] [--file INPUT_FILE] [--wfsx WFSX]
                    [--hsx-file HSX_FILE] [--geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE] --shift
                    {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual} [--manual-value MANUAL_VALUE]
                    [--gap-tol GAP_TOL] [--projection {l,ml,atom,species,species_l}]
                    [--category CATEGORY [CATEGORY ...]] [--k-tol K_TOL]
                    [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v]
                    [--no-intro]

Orbital-projected (fatbands) band structure from .bands + .WFSX.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Shorthand for --file <label>.bands, auto-detects <label>.bands.WFSX (falling back to <label>.WFSX with a note), and auto-detects <label>.HSX (optional, upgrades weight accuracy) then <label>.fdf (geometry+basis fallback -- NOT <label>.XV, which has no per-orbital basis information). Mutually exclusive with --file/--wfsx/--hsx-file/--geometry-file.
  --file INPUT_FILE     Explicit path to the .bands file (alternative to --label).
  --wfsx WFSX           Explicit path to the .WFSX file. Required if --file is used instead of --label.
  --hsx-file HSX_FILE   Optional explicit .HSX path (Hamiltonian+overlap) for physically correct overlap-weighted norms. Falls back to --geometry-file / auto-detected .fdf with an accuracy warning if omitted.
  --geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE
                        Optional explicit .fdf geometry path (must have the basis's .ion/.ion.xml files alongside it), used as the fallback parent when no .HSX is available. A bare .XV has no per-orbital basis information and will fail the orbital-count check against the .WFSX -- use --hsx-file or a .fdf instead. Requires sisl.
  --shift {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual}
                        Reference energy shift, same vocabulary as stb-bands:
                          - 'vbm'    : Valence Band Maximum
                          - 'cbm'    : Conduction Band Minimum
                          - 'fermi'  : Fermi level
                          - 'manual' : Custom shift value (requires --manual-value).
  --manual-value MANUAL_VALUE
                        Custom energy shift value (required if --shift manual is used).
  --gap-tol GAP_TOL     Energy tolerance in eV for VBM/CBM classification when --shift is vbm/cbm (default: 0.01). Same meaning as stb-bands.
  --projection {l,ml,atom,species,species_l}
                        Category to color/size markers by (default: species_l):
                          l:         aggregate by angular momentum (s, p, d, f)
                          ml:        detailed orbital (s, px, py, pz, dxy, ...)
                          atom:      per atom index
                          species:   per chemical species
                          species_l: chemical species AND angular momentum combined
                                     (e.g. 'Sn-s', 'Sn-p', 'O-s', 'O-p') -- shows which
                                     orbital character within a species dominates a band,
                                     which plain 'species' or plain 'l' cannot on their own
                        Single choice only -- unlike stb-dos's --type, the plot needs one weight per marker; run again for another projection.
  --category CATEGORY [CATEGORY ...]
                        Restrict output to specific category values (e.g. --projection species --category O Sn, or --projection species_l --category Sn-s O-p). Default: all categories found.
  --k-tol K_TOL         Cross-check tolerance (eV) between WFSX-stored eigenvalues and .bands eigenvalues at sampled k-points (default: 0.001). This is a file-order sanity guard, not a physics tolerance like --gap-tol -- raising it only weakens the check that .bands/.WFSX truly correspond to the same calculation.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write fatbands_<category>.dat/fatbands.gplot (with --save-gnuplot) and stb_fatbands_report.txt/references.bib into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_fatbands_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write fatbands_<category>.dat (one file per category, k_position/energy(eV)/value columns) and fatbands.gplot together. Off by default -- this tool used to write both unconditionally on every run; that's no longer the case.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the fatbands plot before finishing. Off by default -- this tool used to always show it, with no way to skip.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-fatbands --label siesta --shift fermi --projection l
  stb-fatbands --label siesta --shift fermi --projection species --category O Sn
  stb-fatbands --label siesta --shift fermi --projection species_l
  stb-fatbands --file siesta.bands --wfsx siesta.bands.WFSX --hsx-file siesta.HSX \
      --shift fermi --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-fetch.help:
usage: stb-fetch [-h] [--source {materials-project,cod,optimade}]
                 [--material-id MATERIAL_ID | --cod-id COD_ID | --optimade-id OPTIMADE_ID | --formula FORMULA]
                 [--most-stable] [--api-key API_KEY] [--provider PROVIDER]
                 [--list-providers] [--limit LIMIT]
                 [--unitcell {primitive,conventional,refined}] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                 [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE] [-o OUTPUT] [--save-report]
                 [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Fetches a structure from an online database and writes it as .fdf.
Look it up by exact id, or search by formula and pick a candidate.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --source {materials-project,cod,optimade}
                        Database to query. Required unless --list-providers is given.
  --material-id MATERIAL_ID
                        Exact Materials Project id (e.g. 'mp-19306'). materials-project only.
  --cod-id COD_ID       Exact Crystallography Open Database numeric id. cod only.
  --optimade-id OPTIMADE_ID
                        Exact id within the chosen --provider. optimade only.
  --formula FORMULA     Search by chemical formula (e.g. 'Fe3O4'). Works with any source; prints a candidate table if more than one match is found.
  --most-stable         With --formula on materials-project, auto-pick the candidate with the lowest energy above hull instead of requiring an explicit --material-id. Not available for --source cod/optimade (no DFT energy to rank by).
  --api-key API_KEY     Materials Project API key. Default: the PMG_MAPI_KEY environment variable / pymatgen's own settings file.
  --provider PROVIDER   OPTIMADE provider: an alias (see --list-providers for a curated subset; any alias from pymatgen's own OptimadeRester.aliases also works) or a raw OPTIMADE base URL. Required with --source optimade.
  --list-providers      Print a curated list of OPTIMADE providers and exit. Does not require --source or a selection flag.
  --limit LIMIT         Cap on how many --formula candidates to display (default: 20).
  --unitcell {primitive,conventional,refined}
                        Also reduce the fetched structure to its primitive/conventional/refined unit cell (same logic as stb-unitcell) before writing. Default: keep the structure exactly as fetched.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry precision, used for the fetched structure's space group summary and for --unitcell (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default, matches stb-unitcell/stb-symmetry).
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry angle tolerance in degrees, used the same way as --symprec (default: 5.0, pymatgen's own default).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: fetched.fdf).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_fetch_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view of the structure (via ASE) after writing the .fdf. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-fetch --source cod --cod-id 1010369
  stb-fetch --source cod --formula 'Fe3O4'
  stb-fetch --source materials-project --material-id mp-19306
  stb-fetch --source materials-project --formula Fe3O4 --most-stable
  stb-fetch --source optimade --provider twodmatpedia --formula MoS2
  stb-fetch --source optimade --provider twodmatpedia --optimade-id 2dm-2127
  stb-fetch --source cod --cod-id 1010369 --unitcell primitive
  stb-fetch --list-providers

stb-gqca.help:
usage: stb-gqca [-h] -f FILE --sublattice SUBLATTICE --species-b SPECIES_B -c CALC
                [-p PSEUDO_DIR] [--kdensity KDENSITY] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                [-O OUTPUT_DIR] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 2: generates the 3 ordered pair-cluster-representative structures (AA/AB/BB) for a substitutional alloy A(1-x)Bx.
Implements the pair-cluster (N=2) special case of the Generalized Quasi-Chemical Approximation
(GQCA, Sher, van Schilfgaarde, Chen, Chen, Phys. Rev. B 36, 4279, 1987) -- the classic Guggenheim
quasi-chemical approximation, applicable to ANY lattice/dimensionality (2D or 3D alike; verified on
both a 3D zincblende cell and a 2D transition-metal-dichalcogenide cell during this tool's
development). Disorders one existing sublattice (--sublattice) with a second species (--species-b,
typically absent from the input structure) and writes 3 folders: the two pure end-members
(cluster_n0/, cluster_n2/) and the ordered 50:50 compound that most purely realizes an "every
neighbor pair is unlike" (AB) local environment along the shortest sublattice-sublattice bond
(cluster_n1/) -- NOT a random 50:50 mixture, whose bonds would average to a mix of AA/AB/BB.

All 3 folders are written for a REAL relaxation (MD.TypeOfRun CG always; MD.VariableCell T too for
a 3D/bulk input) -- the 3 representative structures generally have different equilibrium lattice
constants (atomic size mismatch between A and B), and single-point evaluation at a fixed lattice
constant would contaminate the mixing energy with spurious strain. [KNOWN LIMITATION] For a 2D
(vacuum-padded) input, cell relaxation is left OFF entirely (positions-only, at the input's own
in-plane lattice constant) rather than risk an unconfirmed SIESTA cell-constraint syntax for
excluding the vacuum axis -- see force_full_relaxation's docstring. Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each
folder yourself, then use stb-gqcaAnalysis.

[WHY ONLY 3 STRUCTURES / ONLY EVER 50:50] The pair cluster (N=2) has exactly 3 possible local
compositions (0, 1, or 2 B atoms per pair) -- there is no "user-chosen x" knob here, and
cluster_n1/ is always built at the cluster-internal 50:50 composition (the ONLY interior point a
2-site cluster has), regardless of the alloy composition you actually care about. Your real target
composition x (e.g. Mo0.7W0.3S2) is swept entirely in Stage 2 (stb-gqcaAnalysis --x-min/--x-max),
which combines these 3 fixed reference energies via the mass-action law to get x_j(x,T) at ANY x in
[0,1] -- these 3 DFT calculations are the complete, sufficient input for the whole x/T thermodynamic
surface, not a coarse sample of it.

options:

  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR

stb-gqcaAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-gqcaAnalysis [-h] [--directory DIRECTORY] [--file FILE] [--x-min X_MIN]
                        [--x-max X_MAX] [--x-points X_POINTS] [--temp TEMP]
                        [--temp-min TEMP_MIN] [--temp-max TEMP_MAX]
                        [--temp-points TEMP_POINTS]
                        [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE] [-o OUTPUT]
                        [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 2: solves the GQCA pair-cluster mass-action equilibrium and reports alloy mixing thermodynamics.
Reads the 3 relaxed cluster_n{0,1,2}/ folders written by stb-gqca (AA/AB/BB pair-cluster
representatives), normalizes each to a per-sublattice-site energy (the 3 folders generally have
different cell sizes -- see read_cluster_energy's own docstring), and solves the mass-action
equilibrium (Sher, van Schilfgaarde, Chen, Chen, Phys. Rev. B 36, 4279, 1987) over a composition x /
temperature T grid to report Delta-H_mix, Delta-S_mix, Delta-G_mix, and a short-range-order (SRO)
parameter.

[UNVERIFIED] The mixing-entropy formula (-kB * Sum_j x_j*ln(x_j/g_j), the standard "gas of
independent clusters" form) and the SRO-parameter normalization could not be pinned to a fully
confirmed closed form from the primary literature during this tool's development -- see
core/gqca_solver.py's own docstrings. The mixing-enthalpy and mass-action-law equations ARE
confirmed against a secondary source that restates the original 1987 formalism. Every report/CSV
column derived from an [UNVERIFIED] quantity is documented as such below.

Also runs a discrete-grid common-tangent (miscibility gap) search on Delta-G_mix(x) at every
sampled T -- kept for completeness, but [STRUCTURAL LIMITATION] Delta-G_mix(x) from this
independent-cluster formalism is PROVABLY CONVEX for any Delta_j (a convex-analysis theorem, not
a numerical coincidence), so a gap is essentially never found here regardless of the input
energies -- this model captures short-range order, not genuine phase separation. See
core/gqca_solver.py::common_tangent_gaps' own docstring for the full argument.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

                        Root directory written by stb-gqca (default: gqca_study).

  --x-max X_MAX         Composition grid maximum (default: 1.0).
  --x-points X_POINTS   Number of composition grid points (default: 21).
  --temp TEMP           Single fixed temperature in K. Mutually exclusive with --temp-min/--temp-max/--temp-points.
  --temp-min TEMP_MIN   Temperature sweep minimum (K).
  --temp-max TEMP_MAX   Temperature sweep maximum (K).
  --temp-points TEMP_POINTS
                        Number of temperature sweep points (default: 5).
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05) above which a cluster folder's calc.out is flagged as possibly not relaxed. Advisory only, never blocks the result.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename (no extension) for the .csv/.dat/.gplot outputs (default: gqca_results).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <directory>/gqca_stage2.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-gqcaAnalysis --directory gqca_study --temp 800
  stb-gqcaAnalysis --directory gqca_study --temp-min 300 --temp-max 1500 --temp-points 5

stb-her.help:
usage: stb-her [-h] -s STRUCTURE -c CALC [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
               [--site-type {ontop,bridge,hollow,all}] [--height HEIGHT]
               [--both-sides] [--symprec SYMPREC] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
               [--position X Y] [--positions-file PATH] [-O OUTPUT_DIR]
               [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 3: finds candidate H-adsorption sites on a slab/2D material and writes one relaxation folder per site.
Part of the HER (Hydrogen Evolution Reaction) workflow -- computes the computational hydrogen
electrode (CHE, Norskov et al.) descriptor Delta-G_H*. Unlike the general-purpose stb-adsorb
(any adsorbate, multi-adsorbate, ML ranking, height sweeps), this tool is deliberately narrower:
the adsorbate is always a single H atom, and EVERY symmetrically distinct site of --site-type is
written (no --site-index/--all-sites choice) -- HER's whole point is finding the GLOBAL most
stable site, so there is no reason to write only some of them. Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each
folder's relaxation yourself, then use stb-herRefs.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input slab/2D structure.fdf (vacuum along one axis).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template for the site relaxations (kgrid, basis, XC, %include structure.fdf, MD.TypeOfRun CG, etc.) -- untouched and copied into every 'sites/site_*/' folder, with a config_extra.fdf sidecar %include'd on top forcing a fixed cell, Slab.DipoleCorrection, Spin polarized and DFTD3 (all mandatory, not opt-in -- see write_site_folder's docstring).
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank or a folder path.
  --site-type {ontop,bridge,hollow,all}
                        Which family/families of adsorption sites to search (default: all -- HER wants the global minimum across site types). Ignored with --position/--positions-file.
  --height HEIGHT       H adsorption distance above the surface, in Ang (default: 1.5). Also used as the offset along the surface normal for --position/--positions-file.
  --both-sides          Adsorb on both exposed faces (for a free-standing 2D material with vacuum on both sides). Needs a symmetry operation mapping top to bottom (same requirement as stb-adsorb --both-sides). Requires a concrete --site-type (not 'all'); mutually exclusive with --position/--positions-file.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-reduction tolerance for site-finding (default: 0.01). Also used for the [1] SLAB SYMMETRY report. Ignored with --position/--positions-file.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum-axis detection threshold in Ang (default: 10.0).
  --position X Y        Manual Cartesian (X, Y) position in Ang for a single H site, overriding automatic site-finding entirely (--site-type/--symprec are ignored when this is given). Mutually exclusive with --positions-file and --both-sides.
  --positions-file PATH
                        '.dat' file with one or more H-adsorption site positions, as in-plane fractional (a, b) coordinates relative to the file's own LATTICE_A/LATTICE_B/LATTICE_C lines ('number type frac_a frac_b' per site line; '#' comments and blank lines ignored) -- used INSTEAD of automatic site-finding (--site-type/--symprec are ignored). EVERY position in the file gets its own site_N/ folder -- unlike stb-adsorb, stb-her has no --site-index/--all-sites choice to make (HER always wants every distinct site). stb-her always writes 'sites/site_positions.dat' with the lattice and positions actually used this run (auto-found or manual alike), in the same format, so it can be inspected, hand-edited, and fed back here for a future run. Mutually exclusive with --position and --both-sides.
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory for the whole HER workflow (default: her_study).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/her_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-her -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --site-type all
  stb-her -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --site-type ontop --both-sides
  stb-her -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --position 1.23 0.71 --height 1.6
  stb-her -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --positions-file sites/site_positions.dat

stb-herAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-herAnalysis [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [--file FILE] [--temp TEMP]
                       [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE] [-o OUTPUT] [--save-report]
                       [--plot] [--no-plot] [--show] [--no-show] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 3 of 3: combines every reference energy from stb-herRefs into the final Delta-G_H* (Gibbs free energy of H adsorption).
Delta-G_H* = Delta-E_H (BSSE-corrected) + Delta-ZPE - T*Delta-S, the computational hydrogen
electrode (CHE, Norskov et al.) descriptor for HER activity -- Delta-G_H* ~= 0 is the Sabatier-
optimal binding strength.

--zpe-mode full's Delta-ZPE/Delta-S computation is NOT simply ZPE(site) - 0.5*ZPE(H2): that
would include the ENTIRE slab's own vibrational zero-point energy (perturbed by H adsorption),
not just H*'s contribution. The physically correct expression subtracts the clean slab's own
(equally full-structure) ZPE/entropy first:
    Delta-ZPE = [ZPE(site) - ZPE(clean_slab)] - 0.5*ZPE(H2)
    Delta-S   = [S(site) - S(clean_slab)] - 0.5*S(H2)
which is why stb-herRefs --zpe-mode full computes TWO full phonon calculations (site AND clean
slab), not one. --zpe-mode local sidesteps this entirely: it never displaces slab atoms in the
first place (a decoupled H*-only oscillator approximation), so there is no slab ZPE/entropy to
subtract.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-her/stb-herRefs (default: her_study).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each folder (default: calc.out).
  --temp TEMP           Temperature in Kelvin, for the local/full ZPE modes' entropy term (default: 298.15). Has no effect on --zpe-mode standard (fixed Norskov offset) or on the H2 gas-phase reference (fixed at its own 298.15 K literature value regardless of --temp -- see the module docstring's H2_ZPE_EV/H2_TS_298K_EV).
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05) above which a folder is flagged as possibly not relaxed/converged. Advisory only.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename (no extension) for the final report (default: HER_report).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <directory>/her_stage3.txt. Off by default.
  --plot                Save a gnuplot .dat/.gplot bar chart of the Delta-G_H* energy breakdown to <directory>/plot/, skipping the interactive prompt this tool otherwise asks at the end. See --no-plot.
  --no-plot             Skip the energy-breakdown plot entirely, skipping the interactive prompt (see --plot). Use this for non-interactive/scripted runs.
  --show                Open a blocking matplotlib window with the same energy-breakdown chart on screen, skipping the interactive prompt this tool otherwise asks. Independent of --plot/--no-plot (the gnuplot files, if any, are still the canonical saved output). Needs a display. See --no-show.
  --no-show             Skip the on-screen matplotlib window entirely, skipping the interactive prompt (see --show). Use this for non-interactive/scripted/headless runs.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-herAnalysis --directory her_study --temp 298.15

stb-herRefs.help:
usage: stb-herRefs [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [--file FILE] [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                   [--zpe-mode {standard,local,full}] [--displacement DISPLACEMENT]
                   [--supercell SUPERCELL SUPERCELL SUPERCELL]
                   [--vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 3: picks the winning H-adsorption site, builds the H2 gas-phase reference, the BSSE ghost triad, and the ZPE/entropy calculation folders.
Scans Stage 1's 'sites/site_*/' for the lowest-FreeEng relaxed site, then writes (all single-point
unless noted): '00_clean_slab/' (pristine slab, same numerical settings as the winning site),
'02_h2_molecule/' (isolated H2 molecule -- RELAXES, since its bond length must reach its own
equilibrium), '03_slab_deformed/' (winning site minus H -- diagnostic only), the BSSE
counterpoise triad ('04_slab_ghost/', '06_h_ghost_slab/', '07_h_isolated/'), and the ZPE
calculation folder(s) for --zpe-mode local/full (nothing for 'standard', which uses the fixed
Norskov offset in Stage 3 instead). Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each folder yourself, then use
stb-herAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-her (default: her_study).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each site folder (default: calc.out).
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (default: reuse whatever the winning site's own folder already has via -- resolved fresh here since the H2/ghost/isolated references need their own pseudo copies).
  --zpe-mode {standard,local,full}
                        ZPE/entropy calculation mode (default: local). 'standard': none generated here, stb-herAnalysis uses the fixed Norskov offset (+0.24 eV). 'local': 6 finite-difference displacements of H only (fast, decoupled-oscillator approximation). 'full': complete Phonopy displacement sets for BOTH the winning site and the clean slab (needed so stb-herAnalysis can subtract the clean slab's own phonon ZPE/entropy -- see stb-herAnalysis --help for why that subtraction is physically necessary).
  --displacement DISPLACEMENT
                        Finite-difference displacement in Ang, for --zpe-mode local's H displacements or --zpe-mode full's Phonopy displacements (default: 0.015).
  --supercell SUPERCELL SUPERCELL SUPERCELL
                        Supercell dimensions for --zpe-mode full's phonon calculation (default: 1 1 1 -- appropriate for a large-enough slab supercell already; increase only if your slab's own lateral repeat is small).
  --vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX
                        Cubic box side (Ang) for the isolated H2 reference (default: 15.0).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-herRefs --directory her_study --zpe-mode local

stb-hirshfeldAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-hirshfeldAnalysis [-h] [-O OUTPUT_DIR] [--tol E-] [--max-iter N]
                             [--ref REF] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Stage 3 of the Hirshfeld-I workflow: reads back every neutral+ion isolated-atom folder, then iterates the Hirshfeld-I reference-density refinement against the combined/production system's real density until convergence.

Overrides auto-detection of combined/'s own '*.out' (which assumes that log was left with a .out extension; use --ref if yours wasn't).

usage: stb-hirshfeldPrep [-h] [-s STRUCTURE] [--calc CALC] [--mesh-cutoff RY]
                         [--vacuum ANG] [-p PSEUDO_DIR] [-O OUTPUT_DIR]
                         [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Stage 1 of the Hirshfeld-I (iterative) charge-partitioning workflow: writes a combined/ folder (the full system, forced to a single-point SaveRho-true evaluation) plus one isolated-atom-in-vacuum-box folder per chemical species -- everything needed before stb-hirshfeldIons (Stage 2) can decide each species' ion sign. Nothing needs to be pre-computed.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Path to the combined/production system's own .fdf structure file (structure_io.read_fdf). Default: 'structure.fdf'.
  --calc CALC           SIESTA input template (.fdf) -- same basis/XC/pseudopotential directives used for combined/ and every isolated-atom folder (default: 'calc.fdf'). Cell, single-point/MD, MeshCutoff and SaveRho are all overridden by this tool's own config_extra.fdf regardless of what's in this template; k-grid/Spin/dipole/vdW are left untouched for combined/, and forced Gamma-only + spin-polarized for every isolated-atom folder.

  --vacuum ANG          Cubic vacuum-box side (Ang) for every isolated atom -- must be large enough that the atom's own density has decayed to ~0 well before the box edge. Default: 20 Ang.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR

  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
