stb-hubbardu.help:
usage: stb-hubbardu [-h] [-s STRUCTURE] [-c CALC] --species SPECIES [--atom-index N]
                    [--shell {3d,4d,4f,5d,5f}] [--j J] [-p DIR] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                    [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 3: generates the 'reference' folder for a Hubbard U linear-response calculation (Cococcioni & de Gironcoli, Phys. Rev. B 71, 035105, 2005).
Workflow: (1) this tool generates 'reference/' -- run SIESTA in it yourself;
(2) once it's converged, run stb-hubbarduAlphas to generate the perturbed
'scf_alpha_*'/'frozen_alpha_*' folders (it copies the reference .DM in for
you); (3) run SIESTA in those, then stb-hubbarduAnalysis to compute U.

If 'reference/' doesn't converge: DFT+U SCF on correlated oxides is often
slow/oscillatory with default settings. Things worth trying in your own
calc.fdf template: a lower DM.MixingWeight (~0.05), a higher DM.NumberPulay
(~6), and a looser SCF.H.Tolerance (~0.01 eV).

If --species appears more than once in --structure, --atom-index is required:
SIESTA's %%block LDAU.proj perturbs an entire species label at once, so with
no --atom-index every atom of that species would be perturbed simultaneously
-- measuring a collective response instead of the single isolated-atom
response the Cococcioni-de Gironcoli supercell method requires. When needed,
the chosen atom is isolated onto its own species label (same Z, own
pseudopotential file) behind the scenes; --species stays the real chemical
species everywhere else (the final recommended %%block LDAU.proj, the
REFERENCE_U sanity check, ...).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input structure.fdf, copied as 'structure.fdf' into every run folder (default: structure.fdf).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  Existing calc.fdf template (default: calc.fdf), with %include structure.fdf and everything else already configured; the DFT+U perturbation lines (and single-point SCF enforcement) are added via a config_extra.fdf %include, not embedded inline.
  --species SPECIES     Species label to apply the Hubbard U correction to (must be present in --structure).
  --atom-index N        1-based index (counting ALL atoms in --structure's coordinate block, in file order -- same convention as stb-defect --index) of the specific atom to perturb. Required only if --species appears more than once in --structure; omit it when --species matches a single atom.
  --shell {3d,4d,4f,5d,5f}
                        Correlated shell (3d/4d/5d/4f/5f). Default: the standard shell for --species (transition metals -> (n)d, lanthanides -> 4f, actinides -> 5f).
  --j J                 Exchange J (eV), fixed across the whole workflow (default: 0.0).
  -p DIR, --pseudo-dir DIR
                        Where to get the pseudopotential files (.psf/.psml) SIESTA needs -- a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path. Only the species actually present in --structure are copied into 'reference/' now, and into every scf_alpha_*/frozen_alpha_* folder later by stb-hubbarduAlphas. If omitted, you must copy them into every run folder yourself.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for the run folders (default: hubbardu_runs).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/hubbardu_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-hubbardu --species Mn
  stb-hubbardu --species Fe --shell 3d --j 0.5
  stb-hubbardu --species Mn --pseudo-dir ./pseudos
  stb-hubbardu --species Mn --pseudo-dir dojo --save-report
  stb-hubbardu --species Mn --atom-index 1  # Mn appears twice in structure.fdf

stb-hubbarduAlphas.help:
usage: stb-hubbarduAlphas [-h] [--dir DIR] [--alphas ALPHAS [ALPHAS ...]]
                          [--frozen-iterations FROZEN_ITERATIONS] [--save-report] [-v]
                          [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 3: generates the perturbed run folders for a Hubbard U linear-response calculation.
Reads the 'reference/' folder and template snapshot written by stb-hubbardu
(stage 1) -- 'reference/' must already be converged, since its .DM is copied
into every generated folder here. Writes one 'scf_alpha_<v>' folder per
perturbation strength (full self-consistent response) and one
'frozen_alpha_<v>' folder per strength INCLUDING v=0 (single-iteration,
frozen-density response) -- the v=0 frozen point is evaluated by the exact
same recipe as the others rather than reusing reference's own fully-converged
value, so every point on the frozen-response line is mutually consistent.
Also copies in any pseudopotentials stb-hubbardu was given via --pseudo-dir.
Doesn't run SIESTA itself -- run each folder's calculation yourself, then use
stb-hubbarduAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Directory containing stage 1's 'reference/' folder and manifest -- defaults to 'hubbardu_runs', stb-hubbardu's own default --output-dir, so stage 2 runs against stage 1's output with no extra flag in the common case.
  --alphas ALPHAS [ALPHAS ...]
                        Perturbation strengths in eV (default: [-0.1, -0.05, 0.05, 0.1]).
  --frozen-iterations FROZEN_ITERATIONS
                        MaxSCFIterations for the frozen-density runs (default: 1; raise this only if stb-hubbarduAnalysis finds nothing to parse in those folders).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <dir>/hubbardu_stage2.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-hubbarduAlphas --dir hubbardu_runs
  stb-hubbarduAlphas --dir hubbardu_runs --alphas -0.2 -0.1 0.1 0.2
  stb-hubbarduAlphas --dir hubbardu_runs --save-report

stb-hubbarduAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-hubbarduAnalysis [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE]
                            [--r2-tolerance R2_TOLERANCE] [-o OUTPUT] [--save-gnuplot]
                            [--view] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 3 of 3: analyzes a stb-hubbardu linear-response sweep and computes the Hubbard U.
Fits the self-consistent (screened) and frozen-density (bare) occupation
responses to the perturbation strength, then applies the standard
Cococcioni & de Gironcoli formula: U = 1/chi0 - 1/chi (Phys. Rev. B 71,
035105, 2005). Reports a convergence summary, both fits' R^2 and intercepts
(flagging a fit whose zero point drifted from what was actually measured
there), and warns if chi/chi0 have opposite signs or U comes out negative --
all signs of a bad fit rather than a real result. Writes a ready-to-use
%%block LDAU.proj snippet with the computed U, plus (opt-in) a gnuplot
data+script pair and/or a live matplotlib preview to inspect the fit
visually instead of trusting R^2 alone.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Directory containing the run folders and run_manifest.json written by stb-hubbardu/stb-hubbarduAlphas (stages 1/2) -- defaults to 'hubbardu_runs', their own default --output-dir/--dir, so stage 3 runs against their output with no extra flag in the common case.
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each run folder (default: calc.out).
  --r2-tolerance R2_TOLERANCE
                        Warn if either fit's R^2 falls below this (default: 0.98) -- a poor linear fit means the perturbation range is probably too wide.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf snippet filename (default: <species>_LDAU.fdf).
  --save-gnuplot        Also write the response curve as a gnuplot data+script pair (<species>_hubbardu_response.dat/.gplot), under a 'plot/' subfolder inside --dir. Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the response curve (both branches + fitted lines) before finishing. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <dir>/hubbardu_stage3.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-hubbarduAnalysis --dir hubbardu_runs --file calc.out
  stb-hubbarduAnalysis --dir hubbardu_runs --save-gnuplot --view --save-report

stb-ipr.help:
usage: stb-ipr [-h] [--label LABEL] [--file INPUT_FILE] [--wfsx WFSX]
               [--hsx-file HSX_FILE] [--geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE] --shift
               {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual} [--manual-value MANUAL_VALUE]
               [--gap-tol GAP_TOL] [--q Q] [--k-tol K_TOL] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
               [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR) scattered onto a band structure, from .bands + .WFSX.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Shorthand for --file <label>.bands, auto-detects <label>.bands.WFSX (falling back to <label>.WFSX then <label>.selected.WFSX, with a note), and, unless --hsx-file/--geometry-file override it, auto-detects <label>.HSX (optional, upgrades weight accuracy) then <label>.fdf (geometry+basis fallback). Mutually exclusive with --file/--wfsx (not --hsx-file/--geometry-file -- see their own help).
  --file INPUT_FILE     Explicit path to the .bands file (alternative to --label).
  --wfsx WFSX           Explicit path to the .WFSX file. Required if --file is used instead of --label.
  --hsx-file HSX_FILE   Optional explicit .HSX path for physically correct overlap-weighted IPR. Falls back to --geometry-file / auto-detected .fdf with an accuracy warning if omitted. Optional (and common) together WITH --label too, since the real file is often not literally named <label>.HSX.
  --geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE
                        Optional explicit .fdf geometry path, used as the fallback parent when no .HSX is available. Requires sisl.
  --shift {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual}
                        Reference energy shift, same vocabulary as stb-bands/stb-fatbands.
  --manual-value MANUAL_VALUE
                        Custom energy shift value (required if --shift manual is used).
  --gap-tol GAP_TOL     Energy tolerance in eV for VBM/CBM classification when --shift is vbm/cbm (default: 0.01).
  --q Q                 IPR order parameter (default: 2, the standard choice). Passed straight to sisl's EigenstateElectron.ipr(q=...), which requires q >= 2. Higher q emphasizes localization more strongly.
  --k-tol K_TOL         Cross-check tolerance (eV) between WFSX-stored eigenvalues and .bands eigenvalues at sampled k-points (default: 0.001). Same file-order sanity guard as stb-fatbands.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write ipr.dat/ipr.gplot (with --save-gnuplot) and stb_ipr_report.txt/references.bib into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_ipr_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write ipr.dat (or ipr_up.dat/ipr_down.dat for a spin-polarized run) + ipr.gplot. Off by default -- this tool used to write both unconditionally on every run.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview before finishing. Off by default -- this tool previously always showed it, with no way to skip.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-ipr --label siesta --shift fermi
  stb-ipr --label siesta --shift fermi --q 4
  stb-ipr --label siesta --shift fermi --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-ir.help:
usage: stb-ir [-h] [-s STRUCTURE] [-c CALC] [-p PSEUDO_DIR] [-dim DIM DIM DIM]
              [-d DISTANCE] [--kgrid KGRID KGRID KGRID]
              [--kgrid-density KGRID_DENSITY] [--symprec SYMPREC]
              [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [-O OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [-v]
              [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 3: generates the phonon-displacement folders for an IR spectrum workflow.
Workflow: (1) this tool generates 'ir_study/phonon_disp/disp-*/' -- run
SIESTA in every folder yourself; (2) once they're done, run stb-irModes to
build FORCE_SETS from them, identify the Gamma-point vibrational modes, and
generate whichever follow-up SIESTA folder(s) the dipole-derivative
calculation needs (auto-selected by structure dimensionality -- +/-delta
dipole-moment displacements for a molecule/wire/slab, or a single
equilibrium Born-effective-charge run for a 3D bulk crystal); (3) run SIESTA
in those, then stb-irAnalysis to get the IR-active frequencies/intensities
and spectrum. This whole workflow computes its own phonons -- it does NOT
need item 4's stb-phononsCreate/stb-phononsPos run first, nor stb-raman's
own Stage 1 (though the underlying Phonopy machinery is shared, via
core/phonon_workflow.py -- each workflow keeps its own independent
phonon_disp/ tree).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input structure file containing the unit cell (default: structure.fdf)
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  Input calculation parameters file (default: calc.fdf)
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path (default: current directory).
  -dim DIM DIM DIM      Supercell dimensions for the phonon force-constant calculation (default: 2 2 2).
  -d DISTANCE, --distance DISTANCE
                        Phonon displacement distance in Angstroms (default: 0.02).
  --kgrid KGRID KGRID KGRID
                        Explicit Monkhorst-Pack grid for the supercell's forced single-point SCF (e.g. --kgrid 2 2 2). Overrides the automatic --kgrid-density suggestion. Written into config_extra.fdf (see [2]).
  --kgrid-density KGRID_DENSITY
                        Target k-point density (1/Ang), used to auto-suggest the supercell k-grid when --kgrid isn't given (default: 0.2, same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-strain/stb-phononsCreate/stb-raman).
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (Ang) Phonopy uses internally to reduce how many displacements are actually needed (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default -- matches the rest of the suite, and deliberately NOT Phonopy's own raw default of 1e-5, which is far too tight for a real DFT-relaxed structure and can misdetect the true point group -- see stb-irModes' own --symprec, which is what actually drives the IR-active/inactive classification. Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum gap (Ang) along an axis to consider it vacuum-padded, for the supercell-dimension advisory and the Stage 2 dipole-path preview (default: 10.0)
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory for the whole IR workflow (default: ir_study) -- phonon displacements are written under <output-dir>/phonon_disp/. Independent from stb-raman's raman_study/ -- each WORKFLOW_TOOLS entry is self-contained, even though the phonon step itself duplicates the same Phonopy work if you run both.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/ir_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-ir -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo
  stb-ir -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p ~/pseudos -dim 2 2 2 -d 0.02
  stb-ir -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo -dim 3 3 1 --symprec 0.02
  stb-ir -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo -dim 3 3 1 --kgrid-density 0.05

Notes:
  - --symprec (default 0.01 Ang) controls how many displacement folders Phonopy
    actually needs to write here, and its real, more important effect is
    downstream, in stb-irModes: that tool reloads these same force constants with
    its OWN --symprec and uses whichever point group IT detects to decide which
    modes are IR-active/forbidden and which ones are truly degenerate
    (--use-symmetry/--skip-degenerate). Phonopy's own raw default (1e-5) is far
    tighter than any real DFT relaxation's residual noise (e.g. a cell angle of
    119.999 deg instead of an exact 120 deg is normal CG-relaxation noise, not a
    real symmetry breaking) and can silently DETECT A LOWER SYMMETRY than the
    crystal actually has -- this is why 0.01 (pymatgen's own default) is used here
    instead. Pass THE SAME --symprec to both stages, or the mode
    numbering/classification stb-irModes reports may not match what this stage
    assumed when it wrote (or skipped) a displacement here. If the space/point
    group stb-irModes reports doesn't match what you expect for this crystal,
    rerun both stages with a looser --symprec (e.g. 0.02-0.1).
  - --kgrid-density (default 0.2 1/Ang, same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-strain/
    stb-phononsCreate/stb-raman) is unrelated to symmetry -- it sets how finely the
    ELECTRONIC structure is sampled for the SUPERCELL force calculation done here,
    which is what the phonon frequencies computed by stb-irModes are actually built
    from. A coarse density under-samples the electronic structure and can leave the
    reported frequencies far from experiment -- most dramatically for a
    metal/semimetal with a Kohn anomaly (verified on stb-raman's own graphene
    G-band case: >100 cm^-1 shift from doubling the k-density alone, after
    supercell size (-dim) had stopped mattering). If a computed frequency looks far
    from the literature/experimental value, suspect --kgrid-density before -dim.
  - This flag only tunes the k-grid HERE, for [4]'s big supercell SCF. Stage 2's
    own single-point dipole/Born-charge runs are small, unit-cell-sized
    calculations that reuse whatever kgrid.MonkhorstPack is already inside the
    --calc file YOU pass to stb-irModes -- there is no equivalent --kgrid-density
    flag on that stage. To keep the whole workflow at a consistent, converged
    k-density end to end, edit that block by hand in the calc.fdf you give
    stb-irModes (it can be a different file from this one).

stb-irAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-irAnalysis [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [-l LABEL] [--file FILE]
                      [--linewidth LINEWIDTH] [--temperature K] [-o OUTPUT]
                      [--experimental FILE] [--peak-prominence FRACTION]
                      [--degenerate-tol THZ] [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view]
                      [--view-modes] [--animation-frames ANIMATION_FRAMES]
                      [--symprec SYMPREC] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 3 of 3: analyzes a stb-irModes displacement sweep and computes the IR spectrum.
Auto-detects, per mode, which path Stage 2 used (from the MODE_TABLE's own
`path` column, never inferred from which files happen to exist):

  - NONBULK: reads the total dipole moment (SIESTA's own "Electric dipole
    (a.u.)" line) from each mode's +/-delta dipole_disp/mode_*/ folder,
    central-differences to get dmu/dQ directly as a 3-vector.

  - BULK: reads the Born effective charge tensors (SystemLabel.BC) from the
    single shared born_charge_disp/equilibrium/ folder, combines with each
    mode's own eigendisplacement (a JSON sidecar Stage 2 already wrote) via
    dmu_beta/dQ = sum_atom sum_tau Z*[atom,tau,beta] * e[atom,tau].

  - HYBRID (2D slab): both of the above at once -- the in-plane dmu/dQ
    components come from the same Born-charge x eigendisplacement formula as
    BULK (computed with a vacuum-aware PolarizationGrids that only covers
    the two periodic axes), the vacuum-axis component comes from the same
    dipole-difference formula as NONBULK. A naive dipole is only valid along
    a non-periodic direction, and Born-effective-charge/Berry-phase is only
    valid along a periodic one -- neither method alone covers all 3 axes of
    a slab correctly, so this combines one component from each.

Either way, IR intensity is |dmu/dQ|^2 -- same formula, only the derivation
differs. Builds a Lorentzian-summed spectrum and always lists its detected
peaks; the gnuplot .dat/.gplot pair itself is opt-in (--save-gnuplot, under
<directory>/plot/) and an on-screen matplotlib preview is available too
(--view). Also always reloads Stage 1's force constants to write an
extended-XYZ vibration animation per analyzed mode under
<directory>/mode_animations/ (skipped gracefully if phonon_disp/ is gone),
optionally opened one at a time in ASE's interactive viewer (--view-modes).
Near-degenerate mode groups get a combined, basis-independent intensity
alongside their individual (basis-dependent) values.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-ir/stb-irModes (default: ir_study).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel used in Stage 2's calc.fdf (default: auto-detected).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each displacement folder (default: calc.out).
  --linewidth LINEWIDTH
                        Lorentzian linewidth (cm^-1) for the summed spectrum (default: 10.0).
  --temperature K       Weight each mode's spectrum contribution by the Stokes Bose-Einstein thermal population factor (n+1) at this temperature (Kelvin). Default: no weighting (every mode contributes by its raw intensity alone, as before this option existed).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename (no extension) for the spectrum .dat/.gplot pair (default: ir_spectrum).
  --experimental FILE   Overlay a measured IR spectrum (2-column text file: frequency cm^-1, intensity) on the simulated one, and report a nearest-neighbor peak match (simulated vs. experimental peak positions, one row per experimental peak). Plotted on a separate y-axis (simulated intensity and real intensity aren't on the same scale).
  --peak-prominence FRACTION
                        Minimum peak prominence, as a fraction of that spectrum's own max intensity, for peak detection (both the standalone [3] SPECTRUM peak list and --experimental's matching) (default: 0.01 -- filters out sub-1% noise bumps).
  --degenerate-tol THZ  Two modes within this frequency tolerance (THz) are reported as a degenerate group with a combined intensity, in addition to their individual values -- |dmu/dQ|^2 is not itself basis-independent within a degenerate subspace (Phonopy's returned eigenvectors are an arbitrary orthogonal basis of it), but the GROUP's summed intensity is the physically meaningful, basis-independent quantity (default: 0.001 THz, comfortably above float round-trip noise through the MODE_TABLE's 6-decimal text format, comfortably below any real frequency splitting between genuinely distinct modes).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <directory>/ir_stage3.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also save the spectrum (and, with --experimental, the overlaid measured spectrum) as gnuplot .dat + .gplot scripts, under '<directory>/plot/'. Off by default.
  --view                View the IR spectrum (and, with --experimental, the overlaid measured spectrum on a second y-axis) interactively via matplotlib now. Off by default. Needs a display. Independent of --save-gnuplot -- matplotlib here is only an on-screen preview, never written to disk.
  --view-modes          Open each analyzed mode's eigendisplacement animation interactively in ASE's 3D viewer, one at a time (close a window to advance to the next) -- needs a display and Stage 1's 'phonon_disp/' folder to still be present (reloads the same force constants Stage 2/this stage's own always-on XYZ export already use). Off by default.
  --animation-frames ANIMATION_FRAMES
                        Frames per mode animation, for both --view-modes and the always-on extended-XYZ export below (default: 20).
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (Ang), only used when reloading the phonon force constants for mode animations (--view-modes and the always-on XYZ export) -- same default as every other stage of this workflow (0.01, pymatgen's own default). Does not affect the IR-active/inactive classification (that was already decided in Stage 2) or the spectrum itself.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-irAnalysis --directory ir_study
  stb-irAnalysis --directory ir_study --save-gnuplot --view
  stb-irAnalysis --directory ir_study --view-modes --animation-frames 30

stb-irModes.help:
usage: stb-irModes [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [-l LABEL] [-p DIR] -c CALC
                   [--modes N [N ...]] [--freq-min FREQ_MIN] [--freq-max FREQ_MAX]
                   [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                   [--rotational-mode-tol ROTATIONAL_MODE_TOL]
                   [--displacement DISPLACEMENT] [--use-symmetry] [--skip-degenerate]
                   [--export-animations] [--animation-frames ANIMATION_FRAMES]
                   [--fc-displ BOHR] [--polarization-grid N N N N N N N N N] [-v]
                   [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 3: builds FORCE_SETS from Stage 1's phonon displacements, identifies the Gamma-point vibrational modes, and generates whichever follow-up SIESTA folder(s) the IR dipole-derivative calculation needs.
The path is AUTO-SELECTED by structure dimensionality (core.kspace.detect_vacuum_axes on the
primitive cell), no flag needed:

  - Non-bulk (0D molecule, or 1D wire -- zero or two vacuum-padded axes): SIESTA prints the
    total dipole moment automatically for a non-periodic direction, no special fdf block
    needed. Writes exactly 2 folders per selected mode (dipole_disp/mode_XX_plus/,
    mode_XX_minus/) -- a simple single-point SCF, no per-axis probing (unlike
    stb-ramanModes' Optical.Vector sweep): the dipole derivative dmu/dQ already comes out as
    a full 3-vector from one +/-delta pair. NOTE: for a 1D wire this is only valid along the
    two genuinely non-periodic transverse directions -- the along-axis component is subject
    to the same periodic-direction caveat the HYBRID path below exists to fix for 2D; 1D isn't
    covered by that fix yet.

  - Bulk (3D periodic, zero vacuum axes): a naive dipole moment is gauge-ambiguous for a fully
    periodic system. Writes exactly ONE equilibrium folder (born_charge_disp/equilibrium/,
    the undisplaced structure) using SIESTA's own native Born-effective-charge automation
    (MD.TypeOfRun FC + BornCharge T + %block PolarizationGrids) -- independent of how many
    modes are selected. Also writes a small eigendisplacement JSON sidecar per selected mode
    (born_charge_disp/mode_XX_eigendisplacement.json) so stb-irAnalysis can combine it with the
    Born-charge tensors without reloading Phonopy itself.

  - Hybrid (2D slab, exactly one vacuum-padded axis): a naive dipole moment is only valid
    along the slab's non-periodic (vacuum) axis -- the two in-plane axes are genuinely
    periodic, same gauge-ambiguity problem the bulk path exists to solve. Writes BOTH the
    bulk path's single shared born_charge_disp/equilibrium/ folder (PolarizationGrids built
    vacuum-aware -- the vacuum axis's own row zeroed, so SIESTA skips its ill-defined
    out-of-plane polarization component entirely) AND the non-bulk path's per-mode
    dipole_disp/mode_XX_plus/mode_XX_minus/ folders. stb-irAnalysis takes the in-plane
    dmu/dQ components from the Born-charge run and the vacuum-axis component from the
    dipole-difference pair, combining them into one physically valid 3-vector per mode.

Doesn't run SIESTA itself -- run each folder's calculation yourself, then use stb-irAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-ir (Stage 1) -- must contain 'phonon_disp/' (default: ir_study).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel used in Stage 1's calc.fdf (default: auto-detected).
  -p DIR, --pseudo-dir DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank or a folder path. Default: reuse whatever Stage 1 already resolved and copied into its phonon_disp/disp-*/ folders (the normal, self-contained case -- no need to point at a source a second time). Only needed if that folder is missing pseudopotentials for some reason (e.g. hand-built phonon_disp/ instead of a real stb-ir run).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template for the follow-up SIESTA calculation(s) -- can be the same file used in Stage 1 or a different one, since these are now single-point evaluations on the small unit cell, not the phonon supercell.
  --modes N [N ...]     1-based mode index/indices to process (in ascending-frequency order, acoustic modes already excluded -- see Stage 2's own [1] PHONON MODES table for the numbering). Default: every non-acoustic mode. On the bulk path this only controls which modes appear in the report/MODE_TABLE and get an eigendisplacement sidecar -- the single equilibrium folder is written regardless.
  --freq-min FREQ_MIN   Skip modes below this frequency (THz).
  --freq-max FREQ_MAX   Skip modes above this frequency (THz).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum gap (Ang) along an axis to consider it vacuum-padded, same convention as stb-ir (default: 10.0). Used both for the 0D extra-trivial-mode detection AND to auto-select the bulk vs. non-bulk IR path.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (Ang) Phonopy uses internally when loading the force constants -- drives both the reported point group and, when --use-symmetry is on, the IR-active/inactive classification and degenerate-mode grouping (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default -- matches the rest of the suite, and deliberately NOT Phonopy's own raw default of 1e-5, which is far too tight for a real DFT-relaxed structure and can misdetect the true point group: a mode that should be exactly degenerate can come out as two separate near-identical frequencies, and a symmetry-silent mode can be misclassified as IR-active). Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance.
  --rotational-mode-tol ROTATIONAL_MODE_TOL
                        0D (molecule) only: a mode within the first 3 bands after the translations is treated as free rotation (trivial, excluded) if |frequency| is below this (THz) (default: 2.0). Lower this if your molecule has genuine low-frequency skeletal/torsional vibrational modes you want to make sure aren't mistaken for rotation.
  --displacement DISPLACEMENT
                        Finite-difference displacement (Ang) along each mode's eigendisplacement for the non-bulk dipole derivative, and the default amplitude for --export-animations (default: 0.02). Has no effect on the bulk path's folder (it's the equilibrium structure, never displaced).
  --use-symmetry        Skip modes that group theory guarantees are IR-INACTIVE (their irreducible representation at Gamma isn't contained in the vector (x,y,z) representation -- their dipole derivative is exactly zero, not just numerically small). Works for any of the 32 point groups. Only applies to the default mode selection (every non-acoustic mode) -- an explicit --modes list is never second-guessed. On the bulk path this only reduces what's listed/sidecar'd, never the folder count (always 1). Needs a PRIMITIVE cell (see stb-unitcell --mode primitive); falls back to running every mode, with a warning, if that's not available.
  --skip-degenerate     Non-bulk path only: for a degenerate group of modes (2 or more bands sharing one irrep), write dipole-displacement folders for only ONE representative band and skip the rest -- the IR intensity |dmu/dQ|^2 is a rotational invariant, identical for every degenerate partner regardless of phonopy's arbitrary eigenvector choice within the subspace. stb-irAnalysis reuses the representative's value automatically. No effect on the bulk path (already exactly 1 folder regardless of mode count -- nothing to save by skipping). Needs a PRIMITIVE cell, same as --use-symmetry.
  --export-animations   Write a looping animation of each selected mode's eigendisplacement (a smooth 0/+A/0/-A/0 sweep) as a mode_XX_animation.axsf file -- open in XCrySDen/VESTA to see which atoms move before interpreting the spectrum. Same amplitude as --displacement.
  --animation-frames ANIMATION_FRAMES
                        Frames per mode animation, with --export-animations (default: 20).
  --fc-displ BOHR       Bulk path only: MD.FCDispl for SIESTA's own native Born-effective-charge finite-displacement automation, in Bohr (default: 0.02). Has no effect on the non-bulk path.
  --polarization-grid N N N N N N N N N
                        Bulk path only: the 9 integers (row-major 3x3, one row per lattice vector) for SIESTA's %block PolarizationGrids -- diagonal entries are 1D line-integral k-point counts, off-diagonal entries are the 2D surface-integral mesh (default: 10 4 4 4 10 4 4 4 10). Manual, not auto-generated from a density heuristic -- consult the SIESTA manual for your structure. Has no effect on the non-bulk path.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-irModes --directory ir_study --calc calc.fdf
  stb-irModes --directory ir_study --calc calc.fdf --modes 1 2 3

stb-kgrid.help:
usage: stb-kgrid [-h] -f STRUCTURE_FILE -d DENSITY [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                 [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Compute a Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid from a SIESTA structure file (.fdf) and a target k-point density.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f STRUCTURE_FILE, --file STRUCTURE_FILE
                        Path to the SIESTA structure file (.fdf).
  -d DENSITY, --density DENSITY
                        Target k-point density (in 1/Ang). Example: 0.2
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum empty span (in Angstrom) between atoms along an axis,
                        wrapped periodically, to treat that axis as vacuum-padded
                        (non-periodic) and force a single k-point there regardless of
                        density. Default: 10.0
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_kgrid_report.txt. Off by
                        default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-kgrid -f structure.fdf -d 0.2
  stb-kgrid -f slab.fdf -d 0.2 --vacuum-gap 15

stb-kpath.help:
usage: stb-kpath [-h] -f FILENAME [-p EPS] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                 [--symprec SYMPREC] [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE] [-o OUTPUT]
                 [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Finds the high-symmetry k-path for a SIESTA structure file (.fdf). Dimension-aware (1D/2D/3D) via ASE's Bravais-lattice path finder.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        The structure file name (e.g., struct.fdf).
  -p EPS, --prec EPS    Tolerance (ase.cell.Cell's 'eps') for Bravais-lattice/symmetry detection.
                        Default: 0.0002
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum empty span (in Angstrom) between atoms along an axis, wrapped periodically, to treat that axis as vacuum-padded (non-periodic) when detecting the system's dimensionality. Default: 10.0
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance for the crystallographic space-group analysis. Default: 0.01 (pymatgen's own default). Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance -- a tighter value than the relaxation's own residual numerical noise can misdetect the true space group.
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry angle tolerance (degrees) for the crystallographic space-group analysis. Default: 5.0
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: kpath_bs.fdf).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_kpath_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

stb-mladsorb.help:
usage: stb-mladsorb [-h] --slab SLAB --adsorbate ADSORBATE
                    [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                    [--skip-foundation-comparison]
                    [--site-type {all,ontop,bridge,hollow}] [--height HEIGHT]
                    [--height-sweep MIN MAX STEP] [--n-orientations N_ORIENTATIONS]
                    [--seed SEED] [--diffusion-barrier] [--diffusion-adsorbate NAME]
                    [--diffusion-n-images DIFFUSION_N_IMAGES] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                    [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX] [--fmax FMAX]
                    [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--top-k TOP_K] [--device {cpu,cuda}]
                    [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-data] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Standalone adsorption-site screening driven entirely by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). Enumerates candidate ontop/bridge/hollow sites (pymatgen's AdsorbateSiteFinder), relaxes each (substrate fixed) with MACE, and reports a genuine ML adsorption energy per site (relative to the clean slab + isolated, relaxed adsorbate) -- no SIESTA and no calc.fdf/pseudopotentials needed. Also supports a foundation-model comparison, random-orientation sampling for molecular adsorbates, a binding-energy-vs-height curve (--height-sweep), and a surface-diffusion-barrier estimate between the top sites (--diffusion-barrier). For the real DFT-level pipeline, see stb-adsorb (and its own --ml-rank preview mode, which this tool's machinery was extracted from).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --slab SLAB           Slab/2D-material structure (.fdf), vacuum along one axis.
  --adsorbate ADSORBATE
                        Adsorbate(s): an ASE G2 molecule name (e.g. 'H2O') or element symbol, comma-separated for multiple (e.g. 'H,O').
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --skip-foundation-comparison
                        If --custom-model is given, also screen every site with the raw (non-fine-tuned) foundation model (--model) and overlay both on the ranking plot plus a side-by-side table. On by default; pass this to skip it.
  --site-type {all,ontop,bridge,hollow}
                        Which candidate site type(s) to screen (default: all).
  --height HEIGHT       Adsorbate height above the surface, Ang (default: 2.0).
  --height-sweep MIN MAX STEP
                        Sweep multiple heights instead of a single --height -- also produces a binding-energy-vs-height curve per site.
  --n-orientations N_ORIENTATIONS
                        For a multi-atom adsorbate, cheaply screen this many random orientations per site (single-point energy, no relax) and keep the best-looking one before the full relax (default: 1, i.e. no sampling -- use the adsorbate's default G2 orientation). No effect on single-atom adsorbates (no orientation to sample).
  --seed SEED           Random seed for --n-orientations reproducibility (default: unseeded).
  --diffusion-barrier   Also estimate the adsorbate's own surface-diffusion barrier between its 2 most stable, distinct sites via a real climbing-image NEB. Off by default.
  --diffusion-adsorbate NAME
                        Which adsorbate's top sites to use for --diffusion-barrier when multiple were given (default: the first one in --adsorbate).
  --diffusion-n-images DIFFUSION_N_IMAGES
                        Total NEB images (including both endpoints) for --diffusion-barrier (default: 5).
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry tolerance for site-finding/reduction (default: 0.01).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect the slab's vacuum axis (default: 10.0).
  --vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX
                        Cubic box size (Ang) for the isolated-adsorbate reference (default: 20.0).
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for all relaxations, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max optimizer steps per relaxation (default: 200).
  --top-k TOP_K         Only write out the N best-ranked sites as bare .fdf (default: all).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all files (default: mladsorb_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw ranking data (.dat). Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mladsorb_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mladsorb --slab slab.fdf --adsorbate H
  stb-mladsorb --slab slab.fdf --adsorbate O,H --site-type hollow --top-k 3
  stb-mladsorb --slab slab.fdf --adsorbate H2O --n-orientations 8 --diffusion-barrier

stb-mlconvergence.help:
usage: stb-mlconvergence [-h] --file FILE
                         [--models {small,medium,large} [{small,medium,large} ...]]
                         [--custom-models PATH [PATH ...]] [--no-relax] [--fmax FMAX]
                         [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                         [--energy-tolerance ENERGY_TOLERANCE]
                         [--lattice-tolerance LATTICE_TOLERANCE] [--device {cpu,cuda}]
                         [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-data] [--save-report] [--no-intro]
                         [-v]

Model-size convergence check for MACE-MP-0 -- runs the same reference calculation (full relax, cell + positions) independently with each requested model size (--models, default small medium large) and any --custom-models, then reports how much energy/atom, cell volume/lattice parameters, and wall-clock time actually change between them. Helps pick a model size instead of guessing -- NOT a check against real DFT, only whether MACE-MP-0's own answer has converged with size.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf).
  --models {small,medium,large} [{small,medium,large} ...]
                        Foundation model sizes to compare (default: small medium large).
  --custom-models PATH [PATH ...]
                        Also include one or more custom MACE model files (e.g. fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis) in the comparison, labeled by filename.
  --no-relax            Skip the full relax (cell + positions) -- just a single-point energy/force evaluation on the structure as given, for each model. On by default (a relax is what most workflows actually care about converging).
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for the relax, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max optimizer steps for the relax (default: 200).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes, for the relax's cell mask (default: 10.0).
  --energy-tolerance ENERGY_TOLERANCE
                        Flag a pair of consecutive models as NOT converged if their energy/atom differs by more than this, meV/atom (default: 5.0).
  --lattice-tolerance LATTICE_TOLERANCE
                        Flag a pair of consecutive models as NOT converged if their cell volume differs by more than this, % (default: 1.0).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the models on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all files (default: mlconvergence_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw per-model comparison data (.dat). Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlconvergence_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlconvergence --file structure.fdf
  stb-mlconvergence --file structure.fdf --models small medium --custom-models mlff_model.model

stb-mldiffusion.help:
usage: stb-mldiffusion [-h] --file FILE --vacancy-index VACANCY_INDEX
                       [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                       [--shell-tolerance SHELL_TOLERANCE] [--n-images N_IMAGES]
                       [--autosort-tol AUTOSORT_TOL] [--no-idpp]
                       [--idpp-fmax IDPP_FMAX] [--idpp-steps IDPP_STEPS]
                       [--no-pre-relax-endpoints] [--freeze-substrate]
                       [--freeze-threshold FREEZE_THRESHOLD] [--k K] [--fmax FMAX]
                       [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                       [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Vacancy migration-barrier screening via MACE-driven NEB -- given a PERFECT bulk reference structure and the index of one atom to remove (--vacancy-index), auto-detects every neighbor in the first coordination shell, builds the vacancy-hop endpoint pair for each, and runs a real climbing-image NEB (reusing stb-mlneb's own pipeline) on every candidate, reporting a migration barrier per hop. No SIESTA and no separate endpoint structures to build by hand.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Perfect bulk reference structure (.fdf).
  --vacancy-index VACANCY_INDEX
                        0-based index of the atom to remove, creating the vacancy.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --shell-tolerance SHELL_TOLERANCE
                        Fraction above the nearest-neighbor distance still counted as the first coordination shell (default: 0.15).
  --n-images N_IMAGES   Total images including both endpoints, per candidate hop (default: 5).
  --autosort-tol AUTOSORT_TOL
                        Atom-correspondence tolerance, Ang (default: 0.5).
  --no-idpp             Skip IDPP refinement of interior images. On by default.
  --idpp-fmax IDPP_FMAX
                        IDPP force convergence (default: 0.1).
  --idpp-steps IDPP_STEPS
                        Max IDPP steps (default: 100).
  --no-pre-relax-endpoints
                        Skip the MACE relax (positions only) of each hop's endpoints. On by default.
  --freeze-substrate    Freeze atoms that barely move between each hop's endpoints during the NEB relax. Off by default.
  --freeze-threshold FREEZE_THRESHOLD
                        Displacement threshold for --freeze-substrate, Ang (default: 0.3).
  --k K                 NEB spring constant, eV/Ang^2 (default: 0.1).
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for relax/NEB, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max steps per stage (default: 200).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all files (default: mldiffusion_out).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mldiffusion_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mldiffusion --file bulk.fdf --vacancy-index 0
  stb-mldiffusion --file bulk.fdf --vacancy-index 0 --custom-model mlff_model.model

stb-mlelastic.help:
usage: stb-mlelastic [-h] --file FILE [--model {small,medium,large}]
                     [--custom-model PATH] [--skip-foundation-comparison]
                     [--no-pre-relax] [--no-relax] [--fmax FMAX]
                     [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--max MAX] [--steps STEPS]
                     [--check-convergence] [--convergence-strains PCT [PCT ...]]
                     [--dimensionality {auto,3d,2d,1d}] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                     [--fit-quality-tolerance FIT_QUALITY_TOLERANCE]
                     [--skip-anisotropy-surface] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                     [--save-data] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Standalone elastic-constants calculation driven entirely by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). Strains the reference cell along every physically valid canonical Voigt direction, computes MACE stress at each strain point, and fits the full stiffness matrix -- no SIESTA and no separate strain_*/ folders needed. Also reports sound velocities/Debye temperature and a directional Young's-modulus anisotropy surface (3D only), or, with --check-convergence, how the fit changes across multiple strain magnitudes. A fast heuristic preview, not a substitute for the real SIESTA-based stb-elasticInputs/stb-elasticAnalysis workflow.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --skip-foundation-comparison
                        If --custom-model is given, also evaluate the same elastic-constants pipeline with the raw (non-fine-tuned) foundation model (--model) and overlay both on the stress-strain plot plus a side-by-side constants table. On by default; pass this to skip it (--check-convergence never does this comparison, regardless of this flag).
  --no-pre-relax        Skip the full MACE pre-relax (cell + positions) of the reference structure before straining. On by default -- straining around a structure that isn't already at a MACE-relaxed minimum shows up as a non-negligible residual stress at zero strain in the fit diagnostics, contaminating every constant.
  --no-relax            Skip the per-strain-point atomic-position relax (cell fixed at the strained shape). On by default -- real elastic-constant methodology relaxes internal coordinates at fixed strained cell (matters for e.g. diamond-structure C44); skip only for a single -atom-per-primitive-cell material, or a quick sanity check.
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for both relax stages, eV/Ang (default: 0.02 -- tighter than stb-mlrelax's 0.05 default, since elastic constants are a second derivative and more sensitive to residual forces).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max optimizer steps for both relax stages (default: 200).
  --max MAX             Max strain magnitude, % (default: 1.0 -- smaller than stb-elasticInputs' 2.0 default, to stay safely in the linear regime given MACE's own accuracy limits).
  --steps STEPS         Strain points per direction, spanning [-max, +max] (default: 4).
  --check-convergence   Instead of a single fit, re-run the pipeline at multiple --max strain magnitudes (--convergence-strains) and report how each diagonal constant changes -- checks whether the linear-regime assumption actually holds at the strain used. No foundation-model comparison in this mode. Off by default.
  --convergence-strains PCT [PCT ...]
                        Max strain magnitudes (%) to compare for --check-convergence (default: half, the given --max, and double it).
  --dimensionality {auto,3d,2d,1d}
                        Physical dimensionality, controlling report units and which constants are physically meaningful (default: auto-detected from vacuum padding). Manual override assumes the same axis convention as stb-elasticAnalysis: in-plane xy for 2D, wire-along-c for 1D.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes (default: 10.0).
  --fit-quality-tolerance FIT_QUALITY_TOLERANCE
                        Minimum R^2 for a direction's stress-strain fit before it's flagged as low-quality (default: 0.995).
  --skip-anisotropy-surface
                        Skip the directional Young's-modulus anisotropy surface plot (3D only) -- it's an O(n_theta*n_phi) tensor contraction, cheap, but this opts out if not wanted. Off by default.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for the plot/data (default: mlelastic_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw stress-strain data (.dat) behind the plot. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlelastic_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlelastic --file structure.fdf
  stb-mlelastic --file structure.fdf --custom-model mlff_model.model --max 1.0 --steps 6
  stb-mlelastic --file structure.fdf --check-convergence

stb-mleos.help:
usage: stb-mleos [-h] --file FILE [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                 [--skip-foundation-comparison] [--no-pre-relax] [--no-relax]
                 [--fmax FMAX] [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--n-volumes N_VOLUMES]
                 [--strain-range STRAIN_RANGE]
                 [--eos {birchmurnaghan,birch_murnaghan,vinet,murnaghan,sj}]
                 [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                 [--save-data] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Standalone equation-of-state (E vs V) calculation driven entirely by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). Scans isotropically-scaled volumes around equilibrium and fits V0/E0/B0/B0' (Birch-Murnaghan by default). Gives an independent, curvature-based bulk modulus to cross-check against stb-mlelastic's stress-strain-derived one. A fast heuristic, not a substitute for a real SIESTA volume scan.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --skip-foundation-comparison
                        If --custom-model is given, also fit the EOS with the raw (non-fine-tuned) foundation model (--model) and overlay both curves plus a side-by-side V0/E0/B0/B0' table. On by default; pass this to skip it.
  --no-pre-relax        Skip the full MACE pre-relax (cell + positions) of the reference structure before scanning volumes. On by default -- scanning around a structure that isn't already at a MACE-relaxed minimum shifts V0 away from the true equilibrium and can leave it outside the scanned range entirely.
  --no-relax            Skip the per-volume atomic-position relax (cell fixed at the scaled volume). On by default -- for any structure with more than one atom per primitive cell, internal coordinates generally need to relax at each fixed strained cell for the energy to be physically meaningful.
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for both relax stages, eV/Ang (default: 0.02).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max optimizer steps for both relax stages (default: 200).
  --n-volumes N_VOLUMES
                        Number of volumes to scan (default: 9). Needs >= 5 for a robust 4-parameter EOS fit.
  --strain-range STRAIN_RANGE
                        Max isotropic volume strain, % (default: 5.0 -- wider than stb-mlelastic's linear-regime strain, since an EOS fit wants genuine curvature in the E-V curve, not a small-strain linear response).
  --eos {birchmurnaghan,birch_murnaghan,vinet,murnaghan,sj}
                        Equation-of-state form to fit (default: birchmurnaghan). 'sj' = stabilized jellium (no B0' reported).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes -- bulk-only, rejects any vacuum-padded structure (default: 10.0).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for the plot/data (default: mleos_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw volume-energy data (.dat) behind the plot. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mleos_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mleos --file structure.fdf
  stb-mleos --file structure.fdf --custom-model mlff_model.model --n-volumes 11 --strain-range 8.0
  stb-mleos --file structure.fdf --eos vinet

stb-mlff.help:
usage: stb-mlff [-h] --file FILE [--n-configs N_CONFIGS] [--stdev STDEV [STDEV ...]]
                [--pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR] [--from-aimd LABEL] [--n-samples N_SAMPLES]
                [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--seed SEED] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Stage 1 (Prep) of the Custom ML Force Field workflow: generates training configurations (rattled displacements and/or AIMD-sampled snapshots) from a reference SIESTA calculation, ready for the user to run through SIESTA. Stage 2 (stb-mlffAnalysis) aggregates the finished calculations and fine-tunes a MACE-MP foundation model on them.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Reference SIESTA .fdf (basis/mesh cutoff/pseudos/SCF settings are reused verbatim in every generated configuration).
  --n-configs N_CONFIGS
                        Number of rattled configurations to generate (default: 10). Ignored if --from-aimd is given without also wanting rattled configs (see --n-configs 0 to disable rattling entirely).
  --stdev STDEV [STDEV ...]
                        One or more rattling displacement standard deviations, in Angstrom (default: 0.05). Cycled round-robin across --n-configs.
  --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Directory to search for <element>.psf/.psml pseudopotentials (default: current directory).
  --from-aimd LABEL     Also sample starting geometries from an existing AIMD trajectory ('<LABEL>.ANI' + '.out'), in addition to (or instead of, with --n-configs 0) rattled configurations -- more physically realistic diversity than rattling alone.
  --n-samples N_SAMPLES
                        Number of evenly-spaced AIMD frames to sample when --from-aimd is given (default: 5).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory under which mlff_config_NNN/ folders are created (default: current directory).
  --seed SEED           Random seed for rattling (default: 42).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlff_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlff --file calc.fdf --n-configs 10 --stdev 0.05 0.1
  stb-mlff --file calc.fdf --n-configs 6 --from-aimd aimd --n-samples 6

stb-mlffActiveLearning.help:
usage: stb-mlffActiveLearning [-h] --model MODEL --file FILE [--pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR]
                              [--sampling-method {rattle,md}]
                              [--n-candidates N_CANDIDATES]
                              [--stdev STDEV [STDEV ...]] [--md-steps MD_STEPS]
                              [--md-temperature MD_TEMPERATURE] [--stride STRIDE]
                              [--top-k TOP_K] [--seed SEED] [--device {cpu,cuda}]
                              [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Stage 3 (Active Learning) of the Custom ML Force Field workflow: uses an already fine-tuned model (stb-mlffAnalysis) to screen a fresh batch of candidate configurations (independent rattled snapshots, or frames from a short real NVT trajectory driven by the model itself via --sampling-method md, reusing stb-mlmd's own dynamics) and writes the ones with the largest predicted atomic force as new mlff_config_NNN/ folders, ready for the user to label with real SIESTA and feed back into another round of stb-mlffAnalysis. NOT rigorous uncertainty quantification (that needs a committee of independently-trained models) -- a cheap, single-model heuristic for where the current model is likely weakest.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL         Fine-tuned MACE model file (from stb-mlffAnalysis).
  --file FILE           Reference SIESTA .fdf (same one stb-mlff used, or any structure of the same system) -- basis/pseudos/SCF settings are reused verbatim in every candidate written out.
  --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Directory to search for <element>.psf/.psml pseudopotentials (default: current directory).
  --sampling-method {rattle,md}
                        How to generate candidate configurations (default: rattle):
                          rattle - independent, static Gaussian-displaced snapshots (cheap: 1 evaluation per candidate).
                          md     - one short NVT trajectory with the model itself (stb-mlmd's own dynamics, reused directly); more physically representative of the configuration space the system actually explores, at the cost of running real MD steps.
  --n-candidates N_CANDIDATES
                        Number of candidate configurations to screen (--sampling-method rattle only, default: 50).
  --stdev STDEV [STDEV ...]
                        Rattling standard deviation(s) in Angstrom for the candidate batch (--sampling-method rattle only, default: 0.15 -- typically larger than the amplitude(s) used for the original training set, to probe configuration space not yet covered).
  --md-steps MD_STEPS   Total NVT steps to run (--sampling-method md only, default: 500).
  --md-temperature MD_TEMPERATURE
                        NVT temperature, K (--sampling-method md only, default: 800 -- deliberately higher than a typical production temperature, purely to cover more configuration space per step; not a claim about the material's real operating conditions).
  --stride STRIDE       Score one frame every Nth MD step (--sampling-method md only, default: 10).
  --top-k TOP_K         Number of highest-scoring candidates to write out (default: 5).
  --seed SEED           Random seed for rattling / initial MD velocities (default: 42).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory under which new mlff_config_NNN/ folders are created (default: current directory -- continues the numbering of any already present there).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlffActiveLearning_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlffActiveLearning --model mlff_model_compiled.model --file calc.fdf \
                          --n-candidates 50 --stdev 0.15 --top-k 5
  stb-mlffActiveLearning --model mlff_model_compiled.model --file calc.fdf \
                          --sampling-method md --md-steps 500 --md-temperature 800

stb-mlffAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-mlffAnalysis [-h] [--path PATH] [--foundation-model {small,medium,large}]
                        [--epochs EPOCHS] [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--lr LR]
                        [--valid-fraction VALID_FRACTION] [--device {cpu,cuda}]
                        [--name NAME] [--seed SEED] [-o WORK_DIR]
                        [--skip-foundation-comparison] [--save-data] [--export-lammps]
                        [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Stage 2 (Analysis) of the Custom ML Force Field workflow: aggregates the finished SIESTA calculations stb-mlff generated (energy + forces, best-effort stress), builds a MACE-format training set, and fine-tunes a MACE-MP foundation model on it via 'mace_run_train' -- specializing the generic foundation potential to the user's own material using real SIESTA data.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --path PATH           Glob pattern matching the stb-mlff-generated config folders (default: 'mlff_config_*').
  --foundation-model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP foundation checkpoint to fine-tune from (default: small -- fastest, appropriate for the typically small dataset size of a SIESTA-based fine-tuning run).
  --epochs EPOCHS       Max training epochs (default: 100).
  --batch-size BATCH_SIZE
                        Training batch size (default: 5).
  --lr LR               Learning rate (default: 0.01).
  --valid-fraction VALID_FRACTION
                        Fraction of configurations held out for validation (default: 0.1).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Training device (default: auto-detect, cuda if available).
  --name NAME           Experiment/model name (default: mlff_model).
  --seed SEED           Training random seed (default: 123).
  -o WORK_DIR, --work-dir WORK_DIR
                        Working directory for the training run and its outputs (default: current directory).
  --skip-foundation-comparison
                        Skip evaluating the raw (non-fine-tuned) foundation model on the validation set for comparison. On by default (comparison runs unless this is passed).
  --save-data           Also write the raw parity-plot data (.dat) behind the plot. Off by default.
  --export-lammps       Also compile the fine-tuned model into a TorchScript file loadable by LAMMPS's 'pair_style mace' (via mace_create_lammps_model, part of mace-torch) -- '<model>-lammps.pt'. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlffAnalysis_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlffAnalysis --path 'mlff_config_*' --epochs 100 --device cpu
  stb-mlffAnalysis --path 'mlff_config_*' --foundation-model medium --device cuda
  stb-mlffAnalysis --path 'mlff_config_*' --export-lammps

stb-mlgcmc.help:
usage: stb-mlgcmc [-h] --host HOST --adsorbate ADSORBATE
                  [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                  [--ensemble {canonical,grand-canonical}] [--n-initial N_INITIAL]
                  [--mu MU] [--mu-scan EV [EV ...]] [--temperature TEMPERATURE]
                  [--steps STEPS] [--equilibration-steps EQUILIBRATION_STEPS]
                  [--dr DR] [--insert-delete-prob INSERT_DELETE_PROB]
                  [--insertion-zmin INSERTION_ZMIN] [--insertion-zmax INSERTION_ZMAX]
                  [--seed SEED] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-data]
                  [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Monte Carlo (canonical or grand-canonical) adsorption simulation driven entirely by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). A single-atom adsorbate species is inserted/moved/deleted in a fixed host framework via the Metropolis criterion. --ensemble canonical: fixed adsorbate count, displacement moves only. --ensemble grand-canonical: additionally inserts/deletes at a given chemical potential (--mu), reporting the equilibrium loading -- --mu-scan sweeps multiple values for a full adsorption isotherm.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --host HOST           Host framework structure (.fdf), treated as rigid.
  --adsorbate ADSORBATE
                        Adsorbate element symbol (single atom, e.g. Ar).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --ensemble {canonical,grand-canonical}
                        Monte Carlo ensemble (default: grand-canonical).
  --n-initial N_INITIAL
                        Initial number of adsorbate atoms, randomly placed (default: 0).
  --mu MU               Chemical potential, eV (required for --ensemble grand-canonical unless --mu-scan is given). Loading is extremely sensitive to this value (roughly a 50x change per 0.1 eV at 300 K for a light adsorbate) -- check the printed 'ideal-gas reference loading' before waiting on a full run, and bracket a transition with a coarse --mu-scan first rather than guessing a single value.
  --mu-scan EV [EV ...]
                        Multiple chemical potentials to scan (grand-canonical only) -- produces a full loading-vs-mu isotherm instead of a single run. Given the sensitivity noted under --mu, an initial scan should use a wide range/coarse step to find where loading transitions at all, before refining.
  --temperature TEMPERATURE
                        Temperature, K (default: 300).
  --steps STEPS         Total MC steps (default: 2000).
  --equilibration-steps EQUILIBRATION_STEPS
                        MC steps discarded before collecting statistics (default: 500).
  --dr DR               Max random displacement per move step, Angstrom (default: 0.5).
  --insert-delete-prob INSERT_DELETE_PROB
                        Probability of attempting an insert-or-delete move instead of a displacement move each step, grand-canonical only (default: 0.5).
  --insertion-zmin INSERTION_ZMIN
                        Min fractional c-coordinate for insertion (default: 0.0, whole cell).
  --insertion-zmax INSERTION_ZMAX
                        Max fractional c-coordinate for insertion (default: 1.0, whole cell).
  --seed SEED           Random seed (default: unseeded).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all files (default: mlgcmc_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw N/energy history data (.dat). Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlgcmc_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlgcmc --host slab.fdf --adsorbate Ar --ensemble canonical --n-initial 4
  stb-mlgcmc --host slab.fdf --adsorbate Ar --mu -0.3 --steps 5000
  stb-mlgcmc --host slab.fdf --adsorbate Ar --mu-scan -0.6 -0.4 -0.2 0.0

stb-mlmd.help:
usage: stb-mlmd [-h] --file FILE [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                [--ensemble {nve,nvt,npt}] [--temperature TEMPERATURE]
                [--pressure PRESSURE] [--timestep TIMESTEP] [--n-steps N_STEPS]
                [--equilibration-steps EQUILIBRATION_STEPS] [--friction FRICTION]
                [--taut TAUT] [--taup TAUP] [--compressibility COMPRESSIBILITY]
                [--stride STRIDE] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [-of {pdb,xsf,xyz}]
                [-o OUTPUT] [--output-structure OUTPUT_STRUCTURE]
                [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--seed SEED] [--save-data] [--save-report]
                [--no-intro] [-v]

Molecular dynamics driven by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). NVE (microcanonical), NVT (Langevin thermostat), or NPT (Berendsen thermostat+barostat, bulk-only) ensembles. A fast heuristic exploration tool, not a substitute for a real ab initio MD run.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --ensemble {nve,nvt,npt}
                        MD ensemble (default: nvt). npt requires a bulk (no vacuum-padded axis) structure -- cell dynamics on a slab/wire/molecule would be physically meaningless.
  --temperature TEMPERATURE
                        Target temperature, K (default: 300).
  --pressure PRESSURE   Target pressure, GPa (npt only, default: 0.0 -- ambient).
  --timestep TIMESTEP   MD timestep, fs (default: 1.0).
  --n-steps N_STEPS     Number of PRODUCTION MD steps, after --equilibration-steps (default: 1000).
  --equilibration-steps EQUILIBRATION_STEPS
                        Steps to run and discard BEFORE production (default: 0). Verified live that a freshly Maxwell-Boltzmann-seeded structure relaxes for ~100-200 steps before settling -- letting that transient into the saved trajectory/statistics biases them towards the initial condition.
  --friction FRICTION   Langevin friction coefficient, fs^-1 (nvt only, default: 0.01).
  --taut TAUT           Thermostat coupling time, fs (nvt/npt, default: 100).
  --taup TAUP           Barostat coupling time, fs (npt only, default: 500).
  --compressibility COMPRESSIBILITY
                        Compressibility, eV/Ang^3 (npt only, default: 4.57e-5 -- water's value, a generic placeholder; override with something closer to 1/bulk-modulus for the actual material for a better-calibrated barostat response).
  --stride STRIDE       Save one trajectory frame every Nth MD step (default: 10).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes (default: 10.0, matches stb-kgrid/stb-mlrelax).
  -of {pdb,xsf,xyz}, --out-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}
                        Trajectory format (default: xsf). Same 3 choices as stb-ani2traj.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Trajectory filename. Default: <input stem>_md_traj.<ext>
  --output-structure OUTPUT_STRUCTURE
                        Final-frame structure output (default: md_final.fdf).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  --seed SEED           Random seed for initial velocities.
  --save-data           Also write the raw energy/temperature-vs-time data (.dat) behind the diagnostics plot. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlmd_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlmd --file structure.fdf --ensemble nvt --temperature 300 --n-steps 5000
  stb-mlmd --file structure.fdf --ensemble nvt --equilibration-steps 200 --n-steps 5000
  stb-mlmd --file structure.fdf --custom-model mlff_model.model --ensemble npt \
                           --temperature 500 --pressure 0.0 --n-steps 10000

stb-mlmelting.help:
usage: stb-mlmelting [-h] --file FILE [--model {small,medium,large}]
                     [--custom-model PATH] [--temp-min TEMP_MIN] [--temp-max TEMP_MAX]
                     [--temp-step TEMP_STEP] [--temperatures K [K ...]]
                     [--equilibration-steps EQUILIBRATION_STEPS]
                     [--production-steps PRODUCTION_STEPS] [--timestep TIMESTEP]
                     [--friction FRICTION] [--stride STRIDE]
                     [--lindemann-threshold LINDEMANN_THRESHOLD] [--fmax FMAX]
                     [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--seed SEED]
                     [--save-trajectories] [--trajectory-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}]
                     [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-data]
                     [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Melting-point bracketing via a sequence of short MACE-driven MD runs at increasing temperature, tracking the Lindemann index (RMS atomic displacement from each atom's own time-averaged position, over the nearest-neighbor distance) -- crosses a threshold (default 0.10, the classic literature value) around the real melting point. Also reports the self-diffusion coefficient vs. temperature as a cross-check (compute_msd/fit_diffusion_coefficient, same as stb-aimdAnalysis). Bulk (3D periodic) only. A coarse, cheap heuristic screen, NOT a rigorous free-energy/coexistence melting-point calculation.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --temp-min TEMP_MIN   Lowest scanned temperature, K (default: 300).
  --temp-max TEMP_MAX   Highest scanned temperature, K (default: 3000).
  --temp-step TEMP_STEP
                        Temperature step, K (default: 300).
  --temperatures K [K ...]
                        Explicit list of temperatures, K -- overrides --temp-min/--temp-max/--temp-step.
  --equilibration-steps EQUILIBRATION_STEPS
                        MD steps discarded before collecting data at each temperature (default: 200).
  --production-steps PRODUCTION_STEPS
                        MD steps collected (after equilibration) at each temperature (default: 500).
  --timestep TIMESTEP   MD timestep, fs (default: 1.0).
  --friction FRICTION   Langevin friction, fs^-1 (default: 0.01).
  --stride STRIDE       Save one frame every this many production steps (default: 5).
  --lindemann-threshold LINDEMANN_THRESHOLD
                        Lindemann index melting threshold (default: 0.10 -- the classic literature value; real materials vary roughly 0.05-0.15).
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for the initial full relax, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max optimizer steps for the initial full relax (default: 200).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes -- bulk-only, rejects any (default: 10.0).
  --seed SEED           Random seed for reproducible velocity initialization (default: unseeded).
  --save-trajectories   Also save each temperature's production trajectory (xsf/pdb/xyz, --trajectory-format). Off by default -- can add up to a lot of files across a wide temperature scan.
  --trajectory-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}
                        Format for --save-trajectories, same convention as stb-ani2traj/stb-mlmd (default: xsf).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all files (default: mlmelting_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw Lindemann/diffusion-vs-temperature data (.dat). Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlmelting_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlmelting --file structure.fdf
  stb-mlmelting --file structure.fdf --temp-min 500 --temp-max 1500 --temp-step 100

stb-mlneb.help:
usage: stb-mlneb [-h] --initial INITIAL --final FINAL [--model {small,medium,large}]
                 [--custom-model PATH] [--n-images N_IMAGES]
