                 [--autosort-tol AUTOSORT_TOL] [--no-idpp] [--idpp-fmax IDPP_FMAX]
                 [--idpp-steps IDPP_STEPS] [--no-pre-relax-endpoints]
                 [--freeze-substrate] [--freeze-threshold FREEZE_THRESHOLD] [--k K]
                 [--fmax FMAX] [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--device {cpu,cuda}]
                 [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-images] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Standalone climbing-image NEB (nudged elastic band) driven entirely by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). Interpolates images between two already-relaxed endpoint structures (--initial/--final), optionally refines the path with IDPP, runs a real climbing-image NEB with MACE, and reports the barrier + reaction energy. No SIESTA and no calc.fdf/pseudopotentials needed -- for the real DFT-level path, see stb-neb (and its own --ml-neb preview mode, which this tool's machinery was extracted from).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --initial INITIAL     Initial (relaxed) endpoint structure (.fdf).
  --final FINAL         Final (relaxed) endpoint structure (.fdf).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --n-images N_IMAGES   Total images including both endpoints (default: 7).
  --autosort-tol AUTOSORT_TOL
                        Atom-correspondence tolerance between --initial/--final, Ang (default: 0.5, pymatgen's own documented value).
  --no-idpp             Skip IDPP (Image Dependent Pair Potential) refinement of the interior images before the MACE NEB. On by default -- a purely classical/geometric smoothing that usually gives a much better starting guess than plain linear interpolation.
  --idpp-fmax IDPP_FMAX
                        Force convergence for IDPP refinement (default: 0.1).
  --idpp-steps IDPP_STEPS
                        Max steps for IDPP refinement (default: 100).
  --no-pre-relax-endpoints
                        Skip the initial MACE relax (positions only) of both endpoints. On by default, so the reported barrier isn't contaminated by residual forces already present in --initial/--final.
  --freeze-substrate    Freeze atoms that barely move between --initial/--final (< --freeze-threshold) during the NEB relax -- fewer degrees of freedom, and avoids a spectator atom spuriously wandering during a fast/loose ML relax. Off by default.
  --freeze-threshold FREEZE_THRESHOLD
                        Displacement threshold for --freeze-substrate, Ang (default: 0.3).
  --k K                 NEB spring constant, eV/Ang^2 (default: 0.1).
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for the NEB relax, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max steps per NEB stage (default: 200).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all files (default: mlneb_out).
  --save-images         Also write each relaxed image as its own image_NN.fdf (bare structure, no calc/pseudopotentials) -- e.g. to hand off to a real SIESTA NEB later. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlneb_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlneb --initial initial.fdf --final final.fdf
  stb-mlneb --initial initial.fdf --final final.fdf --custom-model mlff_model.model --n-images 9 --freeze-substrate

stb-mlphonons.help:
usage: stb-mlphonons [-h] --file FILE [--model {small,medium,large}]
                     [--custom-model PATH] [--skip-foundation-comparison]
                     [--dim NA NB NC] [--distance DISTANCE] [--no-relax] [--fmax FMAX]
                     [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--band-points BAND_POINTS]
                     [--mesh NA NB NC] [--tmin TMIN] [--tmax TMAX] [--tstep TSTEP]
                     [--qha] [--n-volumes N_VOLUMES] [--strain-range STRAIN_RANGE]
                     [--eos {vinet,murnaghan,birch_murnaghan}] [--check-convergence]
                     [--convergence-dims N [N ...]] [--freeze-unstable-mode]
                     [--freeze-amplitude FREEZE_AMPLITUDE] [--animate-mode BAND_INDEX]
                     [--animate-qpoint QA QB QC] [--animate-dim NA NB NC]
                     [--animate-amplitude ANIMATE_AMPLITUDE]
                     [--animate-frames ANIMATE_FRAMES]
                     [--animate-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}] [--device {cpu,cuda}]
                     [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-data] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Standalone phonon calculation driven entirely by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). One shot: displacements, force constants, band structure, DOS (total + per-species), and thermal properties -- or, with --qha, a quasi-harmonic volume scan (thermal expansion, bulk modulus vs. T). No SIESTA and no separate analysis tool needed. A fast heuristic preview, not a substitute for the real SIESTA-based stb-phononsCreate/stb-phononsPos workflow -- ML potentials are markedly less reliable for phonons (imaginary modes especially) than DFT.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --skip-foundation-comparison
                        If --custom-model is given, also evaluate the same phonon pipeline with the raw (non-fine-tuned) foundation model (--model) and overlay both on the bands/DOS/thermal plots, to show whether fine-tuning actually changed the phonon prediction. On by default; pass this to skip it (--qha never does this comparison, regardless of this flag).
  --dim NA NB NC        Supercell dimensions for the finite-displacement method (default: 2 2 2).
  --distance DISTANCE   Displacement distance, Angstrom (default: 0.01).
  --no-relax            Skip the MACE pre-relax (positions only) before generating displacements. On by default -- a phonon calculation assumes ~zero net force at the reference geometry; skipping this on an unrelaxed structure is a common cause of spurious imaginary modes.
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for the pre-relax, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes (default: 10.0).
  --band-points BAND_POINTS
                        q-points per band-structure segment (default: 101).
  --mesh NA NB NC       q-point mesh for DOS/thermal properties (default: 20 20 20).
  --tmin TMIN           Min temperature, K (default: 0).
  --tmax TMAX           Max temperature, K (default: 1000).
  --tstep TSTEP         Temperature step, K (default: 10).
  --qha                 Quasi-harmonic approximation instead of a single-volume calculation: scans --n-volumes isotropically-scaled volumes and fits an equation of state (thermal expansion, bulk modulus vs. T). No foundation-model comparison in this mode. Off by default.
  --n-volumes N_VOLUMES
                        Number of volume points for --qha, >= 4 (default: 5).
  --strain-range STRAIN_RANGE
                        Volume range around equilibrium for --qha, +/- % (default: 3.0).
  --eos {vinet,murnaghan,birch_murnaghan}
                        Equation of state for --qha (default: vinet).
  --check-convergence   Instead of a single-volume calculation, run the same pipeline at multiple supercell sizes (--convergence-dims) and report how the max frequency / heat capacity / entropy change between them -- MACE is cheap enough to check --dim convergence directly, unlike DFT. Not supported together with --qha. Off by default.
  --convergence-dims N [N ...]
                        Flat list of supercell sizes for --check-convergence, given as consecutive NA NB NC triples (e.g. 1 1 1 2 2 2 3 3 3 tests 1x1x1, 2x2x2, and 3x3x3) -- must be a multiple of 3 values. Default: --dim itself and --dim+1 on every non-vacuum axis (two points).
  --freeze-unstable-mode
                        If the phonon mesh has a genuine imaginary (unstable) mode, write a new structure displaced along that mode's eigenvector -- a common trick to escape a saddle point and find the true minimum. Same feature stb-phononsPos already has for the SIESTA path. Not supported together with --qha/--check-convergence. Off by default.
  --freeze-amplitude FREEZE_AMPLITUDE
                        Max atomic displacement (Angstrom) for --freeze-unstable-mode (default: 0.05).
  --animate-mode BAND_INDEX
                        Animate a normal mode's vibration and write it as a multi-frame trajectory (xsf/pdb/xyz, same convention as stb-ani2traj/stb-mlmd) for viewing in OVITO/VMD -- BAND_INDEX selects which mode (0 = lowest frequency) at --animate-qpoint. Not supported together with --qha/--check-convergence. Off by default.
  --animate-qpoint QA QB QC
                        Fractional q-point to animate a mode at (default: 0 0 0, Gamma).
  --animate-dim NA NB NC
                        Supercell size used to build the animated modulation -- must make --animate-qpoint commensurate (q x dim ~ integer vector); the default 1 1 1 only works exactly at Gamma (default: 1 1 1).
  --animate-amplitude ANIMATE_AMPLITUDE
                        Max atomic displacement for the animation, Angstrom -- deliberately larger than --freeze-amplitude since this is for visualization, not a physical perturbation (default: 0.5).
  --animate-frames ANIMATE_FRAMES
                        Number of frames in one full vibration cycle (default: 30).
  --animate-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}
                        Output trajectory format for --animate-mode, same convention as stb-ani2traj/stb-mlmd (default: xsf).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all plots/data (default: mlphonons_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw numeric data (.dat) behind each plot. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlphonons_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlphonons --file structure.fdf --dim 2 2 2
  stb-mlphonons --file structure.fdf --custom-model mlff_model.model --dim 3 3 3
  stb-mlphonons --file structure.fdf --qha --n-volumes 7 --strain-range 5

stb-mlrelax.help:
usage: stb-mlrelax [-h] -f FILENAME [--relax-cell] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                   [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH] [--fmax FMAX]
                   [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--optimizer {FIRE,BFGS,LBFGS}]
                   [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-o OUTPUT] [--save-report] [--save-data]
                   [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Fast ML pre-relaxation with the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential.
Cleans up obviously-wrong geometry (bad lattice guesses, freshly-added
defect/passivant atoms at the wrong bond length) cheaply, so a follow-up
SIESTA relaxation starts much closer to its own equilibrium and needs far
fewer ionic steps. This is a pre-relaxation heuristic, NOT a substitute for
a real DFT relaxation -- universal MLIPs are trained mostly on
Materials-Project-like inorganic crystals and are less reliable far from
that distribution.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input structure file (.fdf).
  --relax-cell          Also relax the lattice, not just atomic positions. Automatically adapts to the structure's periodicity: for a slab/wire (vacuum-padded axes, e.g. from stb-slab), only the genuinely periodic direction(s) relax and the vacuum thickness is held exactly fixed -- relaxing stress along a vacuum direction would be physically meaningless. A fully isolated structure (vacuum in all 3 directions, e.g. a molecule) has nothing to relax; --relax-cell is ignored.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes for --relax-cell (default: 10.0, matches stb-kgrid).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size: speed/accuracy tradeoff (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Maximum optimizer steps (default: 200).
  --optimizer {FIRE,BFGS,LBFGS}
                        ASE optimizer to use (default: FIRE).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: relaxed.fdf).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlrelax_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-data           Also write the raw per-step relaxation convergence trace (<stem>_relax_convergence.dat). Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the structure before and after relaxation (page through frames in ase-gui). Needs a display. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-mlrelax -f defect.fdf
  stb-mlrelax -f bulk.fdf --relax-cell -o bulk_relaxed.fdf
  stb-mlrelax -f slab2d.fdf --relax-cell -o slab2d_relaxed.fdf
  stb-mlrelax -f defect.fdf --save-report --save-data --view

Note: an initial guess that's very far from equilibrium (e.g. a lattice constant off by 15-20% or more) can occasionally lead a universal MLIP to a spurious low-energy state instead of the real minimum -- sanity-check a large --relax-cell change before trusting it.

stb-mlsearch.help:
usage: stb-mlsearch [-h] --file FILE [--model {small,medium,large}]
                    [--custom-model PATH]
                    [--algorithm {basin-hopping,simulated-annealing}] [--steps STEPS]
                    [--dr DR] [--temperature TEMPERATURE] [--temp-start TEMP_START]
                    [--temp-end TEMP_END] [--schedule {exponential,linear}]
                    [--snapshot-interval SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL] [--timestep TIMESTEP]
                    [--friction FRICTION] [--fmax FMAX] [--max-steps MAX_STEPS]
                    [--seed SEED] [--no-pre-relax] [--no-final-cell-relax]
                    [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--trajectory-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}]
                    [--device {cpu,cuda}] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-data]
                    [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

Global structure search driven entirely by a MACE potential -- the MACE-MP-0 foundation model, or a custom model fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis (--custom-model). Two algorithms (--algorithm): 'basin-hopping' (default, ase.optimize.basin.BasinHopping -- random perturbation + local relax + Metropolis accept/reject) or 'simulated-annealing' (one continuous cooling NVT MD trajectory, periodically snapshotted and locally relaxed). Both search for the lowest-energy atomic arrangement at a FIXED cell -- e.g. defect/vacancy site occupation, disordered/alloy configurations, local amorphous-like rearrangements. NOT crystal structure prediction (the cell shape itself is untouched during the search) and NOT a proof of finding the true global minimum -- both are heuristic searches.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Input structure (.fdf).
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --custom-model is given.
  --custom-model PATH   Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --model.
  --algorithm {basin-hopping,simulated-annealing}
                        Search algorithm (default: basin-hopping). 'basin-hopping': random perturbation (--dr) + local relax + Metropolis accept/reject (--temperature). 'simulated-annealing': one continuous cooling NVT MD trajectory (--temp-start/--temp-end/--schedule), periodically snapshotted (--snapshot-interval) and locally relaxed.
  --steps STEPS         Number of basin-hopping perturb+relax+accept/reject attempts (basin-hopping), or total MD steps in the cooling trajectory (simulated-annealing) (default: 50).
  --dr DR               [basin-hopping] Max random atomic displacement per step, Angstrom, uniform per Cartesian component (default: 0.3).
  --temperature TEMPERATURE
                        [basin-hopping] Search 'temperature', Kelvin, controlling the Metropolis acceptance probability exp(-dE/kT) for an uphill move (default: 1000 -- deliberately higher than any physical temperature, to encourage escaping shallow local minima; a common basin-hopping convention, not a claim about the material's real conditions).
  --temp-start TEMP_START
                        [simulated-annealing] Starting temperature, Kelvin (default: 1500).
  --temp-end TEMP_END   [simulated-annealing] Final temperature, Kelvin (default: 50 -- near-zero, not exactly 0, since the cooling schedule is multiplicative for --schedule exponential).
  --schedule {exponential,linear}
                        [simulated-annealing] Cooling schedule from --temp-start to --temp-end (default: exponential -- the classic simulated-annealing convention, cools fast initially then slows down).
  --snapshot-interval SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL
                        [simulated-annealing] MD steps between snapshot+local-relax candidate evaluations (default: 20).
  --timestep TIMESTEP   [simulated-annealing] MD timestep, fs (default: 1.0).
  --friction FRICTION   [simulated-annealing] Langevin friction, fs^-1 (default: 0.01).
  --fmax FMAX           Force convergence threshold for each candidate's local relax, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --max-steps MAX_STEPS
                        Max local-optimizer steps per candidate relax (default: 200).
  --seed SEED           Random seed for reproducible searches (default: unseeded).
  --no-pre-relax        Skip the initial full MACE relax (cell + positions) of the input structure before starting the search. On by default, so the search starts from a sane reference rather than a raw input.
  --no-final-cell-relax
                        Skip the final full relax (cell + positions) of the winning configuration. On by default -- the search itself only moves atomic positions at a fixed cell (see module docstring), so the final structure otherwise keeps the pre-search cell shape exactly, even if the winning arrangement would relax to a slightly different one.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Gap (Ang) used to detect vacuum-padded axes, for the final cell relax's mask (default: 10.0).
  --trajectory-format {pdb,xsf,xyz}
                        Output format for the full search trajectory (every attempted, locally-relaxed candidate), same convention as stb-ani2traj/stb-mlmd/stb-mlphonons (default: xsf).
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the model on (default: cpu).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Output directory for all files (default: mlsearch_out).
  --save-data           Also write the raw search-history data (.dat). Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_mlsearch_report.txt. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-mlsearch --file structure.fdf --steps 100
  stb-mlsearch --file structure.fdf --custom-model mlff_model.model --dr 0.4 --temperature 1500
  stb-mlsearch --file structure.fdf --algorithm simulated-annealing --steps 2000 --temp-start 1500 --temp-end 50

stb-molecule.help:
usage: stb-molecule [-h] [--name NAME] [--list] [--vacuum VACUUM] [--ml-relax]
                    [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                    [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report] [--view] [-o OUTPUT] [-v]
                    [--no-intro]

Builds a reference molecule from ASE's G2 database.
Places the molecule in a vacuum box, ready as an isolated-molecule
reference (e.g. for stb-cohesive) or a quick starting structure.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --name NAME           Exact (case-sensitive) name from ASE's G2 database, e.g. 'H2O', 'CO2', 'C6H6'. See --list for all names. Required unless --list is given.
  --list                Print all available molecule names and exit.
  --vacuum VACUUM       Vacuum padding in Angstrom, added in every direction around the molecule (default: 10.0).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax the molecule's geometry with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) before writing it out. Positions only -- there is no physically meaningful periodic cell to relax for an isolated molecule, so no --ml-relax-cell option exists here. Off by default.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_molecule_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the as-built and final molecule (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: molecule.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-molecule --name H2O
  stb-molecule --name CH3OH --vacuum 12 -o methanol.fdf
  stb-molecule --name H2O --ml-relax --save-report --view
  stb-molecule --list

stb-nanotube.help:
usage: stb-nanotube [-h] -f FILENAME --chirality N M [--mode {tube,ribbon}]
                    [--repeats REPEATS] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                    [--min-vacuum-size MIN_VACUUM_SIZE] [--lattice-tol LATTICE_TOL]
                    [--search-bound SEARCH_BOUND] [--symprec SYMPREC] [--passivate]
                    [--passivant PASSIVANT] [--cutoff CUTOFF]
                    [--bond-length BOND_LENGTH] [--ml-relax] [--ml-relax-cell]
                    [--model {small,medium,large}] [--custom-model PATH]
                    [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report] [--view] [-o OUTPUT] [-v]
                    [--no-intro]

Rolls a 2D monolayer FDF into a nanotube or nanoribbon.
Chirality (n, m) picks the vector to roll around (tube) or the finite
width direction (ribbon); works for any oblique 2D lattice, not just
hexagonal (no gcd/(n-m)%3d hexagonal-only shortcut is used).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input 2D monolayer structure file (.fdf).
  --chirality N M       Chirality indices (n, m), e.g. --chirality 6 0
  --mode {tube,ribbon}  'tube': roll into a cylinder. 'ribbon': finite-width flat strip. Default: tube.
  --repeats REPEATS     Axial repeats (tube) or width repeats along the chirality vector (ribbon). Default: 1.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum empty span (Angstrom) used to detect which axis of the INPUT monolayer is vacuum-padded (default: 10.0). Same meaning as stb-kgrid/stb-kpath's --vacuum-gap.
  --min-vacuum-size MIN_VACUUM_SIZE
                        Vacuum padding (Angstrom) added around the generated tube/ribbon (default: 15.0). Same meaning as stb-slab's --min-vacuum-size.
  --lattice-tol LATTICE_TOL
                        Fractional-coordinate tolerance for the C x T cell-membership test (default: 1e-6).
  --search-bound SEARCH_BOUND
                        Override the search range for the translation vector T (default: auto, 3*(|n|+|m|)+5).
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry tolerance, Ang, for the before/after symmetry table (default: 0.01).
  --passivate           Cap dangling bonds on the built tube/ribbon with a passivating atom (same logic as stb-passivate/stb-slab). A properly closed, axially-periodic tube has no dangling bonds to begin with (every atom already has 3 real neighbors) -- this mainly matters for --mode ribbon, whose two finite edges are real, physical dangling bonds. Only single-missing-bond sites are auto-passivated; sites missing 2+ bonds are reported instead of guessed.
  --passivant PASSIVANT
                        Element to cap dangling bonds with, only with --passivate (default: H).
  --cutoff CUTOFF       Neighbor-search radius in Angstrom for --passivate. Default: auto-detected (see stb-passivate --help).
  --bond-length BOND_LENGTH
                        Passivant bond length in Angstrom for --passivate. Default: auto per species pair (see stb-passivate --help).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax the built tube/ribbon with a MACE potential before writing it out (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the axial period (the vacuum-padded width/thickness axes always stay exactly fixed). Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_nanotube_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the input monolayer and the final tube/ribbon (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: nanotube.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-nanotube -f graphene.fdf --chirality 6 0 --mode tube
  stb-nanotube -f graphene.fdf --chirality 6 0 --mode ribbon --repeats 4
  stb-nanotube -f graphene.fdf --chirality 6 0 --mode ribbon --repeats 4 --passivate
  stb-nanotube -f graphene.fdf --chirality 6 0 --ml-relax --save-report --view

stb-nativecharges.help:
usage: stb-nativecharges [-h] [--path PATH] [-l LABEL] [--save-report] [--no-intro]
                         [-v]

Reads and tabulates SIESTA's own native Hirshfeld/Voronoi atomic-charge sections from
a finished .out log (Charge.Hirshfeld end / Charge.Voronoi end). No new charge-
partitioning method -- just formats what SIESTA already wrote. --path can be a glob
pattern to scan several folders at once (e.g. 'strain_*').

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --path PATH           Directory to inspect, or a glob pattern (e.g. 'strain_*')
                        matching several directories (default: current directory).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel override, applied to every matched directory.
                        Auto-detected per directory from its .fdf file(s) if not
                        given.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_nativecharges_report.txt. Off
                        by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

stb-neb.help:
usage: stb-neb [-h] -i INITIAL -f FINAL -c CALC [-p PSEUDO_DIR] [--force-spin]
               [--no-force-spin] [--force-vdw] [--no-force-vdw] [--force-dipole]
               [--no-force-dipole] [-n N_IMAGES] [--autosort-tol AUTOSORT_TOL]
               [--idpp] [--idpp-fmax IDPP_FMAX] [--idpp-steps IDPP_STEPS]
               [--mode {1,2,3}] [--ml-model {small,medium,large}]
               [--ml-device {cpu,cuda}] [--ml-fmax ML_FMAX] [--ml-k ML_K]
               [--ml-max-steps ML_MAX_STEPS] [--ml-freeze-substrate]
               [--no-ml-freeze-substrate] [--ml-freeze-threshold ML_FREEZE_THRESHOLD]
               [--ml-prerelax-endpoints] [-O OUTPUT_DIR] [--max-cycles MAX_CYCLES]
               [--siesta-exe SIESTA_EXE] [--mpirun-np N] [--conda-env CONDA_ENV]
               [--cycle-fmax CYCLE_FMAX] [-v] [--no-intro]

Prepares SIESTA folders for a NEB (Nudged Elastic Band) reaction-path study: interpolates images between two already-relaxed endpoint structures, optionally refining the path with MACE-MP-0 before writing single-point SIESTA folders per image.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -i INITIAL, --initial INITIAL
                        Initial (already-relaxed) endpoint: a structure.fdf file, or a directory containing one -- a directory's own finished siesta.XV, if present, is preferred over its structure.fdf guess.
  -f FINAL, --final FINAL
                        Final (already-relaxed) endpoint -- same file-or-directory convention as --initial, same composition.
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template (kgrid, basis, XC, %include structure.fdf, etc.) -- copied into every image_NN/ folder with MD.TypeOfRun/MD.Steps forced to a single-point evaluation.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank or a folder path.
  --force-spin          Force Spin polarized (via config_extra.fdf, overriding --calc's own Spin tag if any) in every image_NN/ (default: ON) -- a reacting atom commonly leaves the system with a net magnetic moment, which a spin-restricted calculation cannot represent at all; costs nothing for a genuinely closed-shell path (converges to zero moment).
  --no-force-spin       Leave --calc's own Spin tag untouched in every image_NN/.
  --force-vdw           Force the Grimme DFT-D3 dispersion (van der Waals) correction (default: ON) in every image_NN/'s config_extra.fdf.
  --no-force-vdw        Leave --calc's own dispersion settings untouched.
  --force-dipole        Force the slab dipole correction (default: ON) in every image_NN/'s config_extra.fdf -- only meaningful for a genuinely one-sided slab/surface reaction path; harmless (evaluates near zero) otherwise.
  --no-force-dipole     Leave --calc's own dipole settings untouched.
  -n N_IMAGES, --n-images N_IMAGES
                        Total images along the band, endpoints included (default: 7).
  --autosort-tol AUTOSORT_TOL
                        Atom-correspondence tolerance (Ang) for linear interpolation (default: 0.5, pymatgen's own suggested value for two endpoints that may have a different atom order). Pass 0 to skip distance -based matching entirely and use --initial/--final's atom order directly -- the right choice (and more robust for a small/densely-packed cell) when both endpoints already share a guaranteed matching order (e.g. a neb_manifest.json-proven pair). If matching fails at this tolerance, stb-neb automatically retries once with --autosort-tol 0 (a [WARNING], not an [ERROR]) before giving up -- this is usually already the right correspondence, so most runs never need this flag set explicitly at all.
  --idpp                Refine the interior images with ASE's IDPP method after linear interpolation -- a better initial guess than plain linear, no MACE needed.
  --idpp-fmax IDPP_FMAX
  --idpp-steps IDPP_STEPS
  --mode {1,2,3}        How to build the path and what to write (default: 2). A pure MACE-MP-0 path with no SIESTA at all lives exclusively in stb-mlneb (ML Simulations menu), not as a mode here:
                          1 = 100% MACE-MP-0, then ONE single-point SIESTA per image -> image_NN/ (this is the old --ml-neb behavior).
                          2 = MACE-MP-0 shapes the path, then a FEW real-DFT NEB refinement cycles (via the separate stb-nebCycle CLI tool, run in your own submission-script loop) -> cycle_00/image_NN/ + a printed loop snippet.
                          3 = 100% real-DFT NEB from a plain interpolated path, no MACE at all -> cycle_00/image_NN/ + a printed loop snippet (same stb-nebCycle tool as mode 2, more cycles expected).
  --ml-model {small,medium,large}
  --ml-device {cpu,cuda}
  --ml-fmax ML_FMAX
  --ml-k ML_K           NEB spring constant, eV/Ang^2 (default: 0.1, ASE's own default).
  --ml-max-steps ML_MAX_STEPS
  --ml-freeze-substrate
                        With --mode 1/2: freeze atoms whose position barely differs between --initial and --final (default: ON) -- fewer degrees of freedom for the MACE optimizer and avoids spurious drift of atoms that are spectators to the reaction. See --ml-freeze-threshold.
  --no-ml-freeze-substrate
                        Let every atom relax during the MACE path-shaping stage (modes 1/2), even ones that don't move between --initial and --final.
  --ml-freeze-threshold ML_FREEZE_THRESHOLD
                        Displacement threshold in Ang (default: 0.3) below which an atom is considered a spectator and frozen by --ml-freeze-substrate.
  --ml-prerelax-endpoints
                        Relax both endpoints' positions (cell fixed) with MACE-MP-0 before interpolating -- independent of --mode (a cheap safety net when you're not fully certain the endpoints are already relaxed). Needs the optional 'ml' extra.
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory (default: current directory) for every image_NN/.
  --max-cycles MAX_CYCLES
                        Cluster-submission snippet only (--mode 2/3): max number of stb-nebCycle refinement cycles the printed loop will attempt before giving up (default: 30). Has no effect on this run itself.
  --siesta-exe SIESTA_EXE
                        Cluster-submission snippet only (--mode 2/3): SIESTA executable name or path for the printed loop to call (default: 'siesta', assumed already on PATH).
  --mpirun-np N         Cluster-submission snippet only (--mode 2/3): prefix the SIESTA call in the printed loop with 'mpirun -np N'. Omit for no mpirun (default).
  --conda-env CONDA_ENV
                        Cluster-submission snippet only (--mode 2/3): conda environment name to activate at the top of the printed loop. Omit to print a generic placeholder reminder instead (default).
  --cycle-fmax CYCLE_FMAX
                        Cluster-submission snippet only (--mode 2/3): the looped stb-nebCycle call's own --fmax (real-DFT NEB force-convergence threshold, eV/Ang, default: 0.05) -- distinct from this tool's own --ml-fmax (the MACE-MP-0 path-shaping target).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-neb -i initial.fdf -f final.fdf -c calc.fdf -n 7
  stb-neb -i initial.fdf -f final.fdf -c calc.fdf --idpp
  stb-neb -i initial.fdf -f final.fdf -c calc.fdf --mode 1 --idpp --ml-k 0.2
  stb-neb -i initial.fdf -f final.fdf -c calc.fdf --mode 3

stb-nebAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-nebAnalysis [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE] [-o OUTPUT]
                       [--apply STRUCTURE_FDF] [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE]
                       [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [--view-path]
                       [--save-path-xyz] [-v] [--no-intro]

Computes a NEB energy profile from an stb-neb band: reads each image_NN/'s SIESTA single-point energy and estimates the reaction barrier from the highest-energy image.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Root directory containing every 'image_NN/' (default: 'neb_run', the self-contained run folder stb-neb --Stage 1 always writes its output into -- auto-detected as '.' instead when the current directory already has its own neb_setup.txt, e.g. right after stb-neb's own printed cluster-submission snippet left you inside neb_run/ already).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each folder (default: calc.out).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename for the gnuplot data file (default: neb_curve.dat), written under '<dir>/plot/' -- only relevant with --save-gnuplot.
  --apply STRUCTURE_FDF
                        Copy the highest-energy image's structure.fdf (the approximate transition-state guess) to this path.
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05, same as stb-adsorbAnalysis/stb-cohesiveAnalysis) above which an image's calc.out is flagged as possibly not relaxed. Advisory only, never blocks the result.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <dir>/neb_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also save the energy-profile curve as gnuplot .dat + .gplot scripts, under '<dir>/plot/'. Off by default.
  --view                View the energy-profile plot interactively via matplotlib now, in addition to always saving it as a PNG. Off by default. Needs a display.
  --view-path           Open every image's structure (in band order) in ASE's interactive multi-frame 3D viewer, to step through the reaction path -- after everything else has finished. Needs a display. Independent of --view (which shows the energy-vs-reaction-coordinate plot, not structures).
  --save-path-xyz       Write the currently-analyzed band (the same images used for [1] IMAGE ENERGIES above -- the latest complete cycle for --mode 2/3, converged or not) as a single multi-frame XYZ trajectory, '<dir>/neb_path_current.xyz'. Off by default. Distinct from stb-neb's own 'neb_path.xyz', which is written once at prep time from the pre-refinement path and never updated afterwards.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-nebAnalysis                              # analyzes ./neb_run by default
  stb-nebAnalysis --dir . --file calc.out
  stb-nebAnalysis --apply ts_guess.fdf
  stb-nebAnalysis --save-gnuplot --view
  stb-nebAnalysis --view-path
  stb-nebAnalysis --save-path-xyz

stb-nebCycle.help:
usage: stb-nebCycle [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE] [--k K] [--fmax FMAX]
                    [--climb-after N] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

One real-DFT NEB step: reads the latest cycle_NN/image_*/ (finished SIESTA single-points), takes exactly one climbing-image NEB step (ASE's own FIRE optimizer, restart-persisted between calls), and either writes cycle_{N+1}/ or declares convergence. Meant to be called in a loop from a cluster submission script -- see stb-neb --mode 2/--mode 3's own printed example. Not available in the interactive stb-suite menu.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR        Root directory containing every 'cycle_NN/' (default: current directory).
  --file FILE      SIESTA output filename inside each image folder (default: calc.out).
  --k K            NEB spring constant, eV/Ang^2 (default: 0.1, ASE's own default).
  --fmax FMAX      Force convergence threshold, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --climb-after N  Only enable the climbing-image correction once the CURRENT cycle number is >= N (default: 0, climb from the start -- appropriate once a MACE-shaped path already has a sensible shape, e.g. stb-neb --mode 2; a larger value is recommended for --mode 3, which starts from a raw interpolated path).
  --save-report    Also persist this cycle's report to <dir>/neb_cycle_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version    show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro       Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-nebCycle --dir .
  stb-nebCycle --dir . --fmax 0.03 --climb-after 5

stb-oer.help:
usage: stb-oer [-h] -s STRUCTURE -c CALC [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
               [--site-type {ontop,bridge,hollow,all}] [--height HEIGHT]
               [--oh-bond-length OH_BOND_LENGTH] [--both-sides] [--position X Y]
               [--positions-file PATH] [--n-orientations-polar N_ORIENTATIONS_POLAR]
               [--n-orientations-azimuthal N_ORIENTATIONS_AZIMUTHAL] [--ml-rank]
               [--ml-model {small,medium,large}] [--ml-device {cpu,cuda}]
               [--ml-fmax ML_FMAX] [--orientation-top-k ORIENTATION_TOP_K]
               [--orientation-rmsd-tol ORIENTATION_RMSD_TOL] [--symprec SYMPREC]
               [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [-O OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [-v]
               [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 4: finds candidate OH-adsorption sites on a slab/2D material and writes one relaxation folder per site.
Part of the OER (Oxygen Evolution Reaction) workflow -- computes the computational hydrogen
electrode (CHE, Rossmeisl et al. 2007; Man et al. 2011) descriptors Delta-G1..4, the theoretical
overpotential eta, and the potential-determining step, via the 3 adsorbed intermediates OH*, O*,
OOH*. This is Stage 1: it only searches for the OH* site (the other two intermediates are derived
or independently searched from the winning OH* site by stb-oerIntermediates, Stage 2). Every
symmetrically distinct site of --site-type is written (no --site-index/--all-sites choice) --
OER's whole point is finding the GLOBAL most stable site. Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each folder's
relaxation yourself, then use stb-oerIntermediates.

[NOTE] No O2 gas-phase reference is ever generated by this workflow (stb-oer/stb-oerIntermediates/
stb-oerRefs/stb-oerAnalysis) -- intentional, not an oversight. DFT/GGA badly describes the O2
triplet ground state (systematic error of at least ~0.3 eV, Sargeant et al. 2021), so
stb-oerAnalysis derives G(O2) from the experimental total reaction free energy instead. See
stb-oerAnalysis --help for details.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input slab/2D structure.fdf (vacuum along one axis).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template for the site relaxations (kgrid, basis, XC, %include structure.fdf, MD.TypeOfRun CG, etc.) -- untouched and copied into every 'sites/site_*/' folder, with a config_extra.fdf sidecar %include'd on top forcing a fixed cell, Slab.DipoleCorrection, Spin polarized and DFTD3 (all mandatory, not opt-in -- see write_site_folder's docstring).
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank or a folder path.
  --site-type {ontop,bridge,hollow,all}
                        Which family/families of adsorption sites to search (default: all -- OER wants the global minimum across site types). Ignored with --position/--positions-file.
  --height HEIGHT       OH adsorption distance above the surface, in Ang (default: 1.8 -- slightly higher than a bare H atom's default, since OH sits further from the surface at equilibrium; still just a CG-relaxation starting guess). Also used as the offset along the surface normal for --position/--positions-file.
  --oh-bond-length OH_BOND_LENGTH
                        O-H bond length of the adsorbing OH group, in Ang (default: 0.97, the experimental gas-phase OH radical equilibrium value). CG relaxation refines it further.
  --both-sides          Adsorb on both exposed faces (for a free-standing 2D material with vacuum on both sides). Needs a symmetry operation mapping top to bottom (same requirement as stb-her --both-sides). Requires a concrete --site-type (not 'all'); mutually exclusive with --position/--positions-file/orientation sampling.
  --position X Y        Manual Cartesian (X, Y) position in Ang for a single OH site, overriding automatic site-finding entirely (--site-type/--symprec are ignored when this is given). Mutually exclusive with --positions-file, --both-sides and orientation sampling.
  --positions-file PATH
                        '.dat' file with one or more OH-adsorption site positions, as in-plane fractional (a, b) coordinates relative to the file's own LATTICE_A/LATTICE_B/LATTICE_C lines ('number type frac_a frac_b' per site line; '#' comments and blank lines ignored) -- used INSTEAD of automatic site-finding (--site-type/--symprec are ignored). EVERY position in the file gets its own site_N/ folder -- unlike stb-adsorb, stb-oer has no --site-index/--all-sites choice to make (OER always wants every distinct site). stb-oer always writes 'sites/site_positions.dat' with the lattice and positions actually used this run (auto-found or manual alike), in the same format, so it can be inspected, hand-edited, and fed back here for a future run. Mutually exclusive with --position, --both-sides and orientation sampling.
  --n-orientations-polar N_ORIENTATIONS_POLAR
                        Systematically sample this many initial OH orientations PER SITE before writing/relaxing (default: 1, the previous single-orientation behavior -- O anchored to the surface, H pointing outward). AdsorbateSiteFinder.add_adsorbate always touches down whichever end of OH sits at the molecule's own most-negative local z, so pre-rotating it (same Fibonacci-sphere sampling as stb-adsorb's --n-orientations-polar) changes which end faces the surface and at what tilt. Combined with --n-orientations-azimuthal below (total orientations per site = polar x azimuthal). Without --ml-rank, EVERY sampled orientation is written as its own 'site_N_<type>_orientM/' folder directly -- fine for a small grid, but can explode the folder count for a large one (e.g. 4 sites x 5x8 orientations = 160 folders). With --ml-rank, each orientation is MACE-MP-0 pre-relaxed and ranked first, and only the unique/top-k survivors become SIESTA folders. Only usable with automatic site-finding (mutually exclusive with --both-sides/--position/--positions-file).
  --n-orientations-azimuthal N_ORIENTATIONS_AZIMUTHAL
                        Evenly spaced in-plane rotations sampled per polar direction (see --n-orientations-polar). Default 1.
  --ml-rank             With orientation sampling: pre-screen every sampled orientation with MACE-MP-0 (substrate fixed, adsorbate free) before writing SIESTA folders -- relaxes each, ranks by energy, deduplicates near-identical relaxed orientations (--orientation-rmsd-tol), optionally keeps only the --orientation-top-k best per site. Needs the optional 'ml' extra. Only meaningful with orientation sampling (--n-orientations-polar/--n-orientations-azimuthal > 1) -- OER always writes every distinct SITE regardless (see --help), --ml-rank only ever prunes/ranks orientations WITHIN a site, never removes a whole site from consideration.
  --ml-model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size, with --ml-rank (default: medium).
  --ml-device {cpu,cuda}
                        Device for --ml-rank (default: cpu).
  --ml-fmax ML_FMAX     Force convergence threshold in eV/Ang, with --ml-rank (default: 0.05).
  --orientation-top-k ORIENTATION_TOP_K
                        With --ml-rank: keep only the N best-ranked unique (post-deduplication) orientations per site, instead of every surviving one. Unset (default) keeps every unique orientation.
  --orientation-rmsd-tol ORIENTATION_RMSD_TOL
                        With --ml-rank: two relaxed orientations of the same site within this RMSD (Ang, adsorbate atoms only) AND within 0.01 eV of each other are treated as duplicates (default: 0.3).
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-reduction tolerance for site-finding (default: 0.01). Also used for the [1] SLAB SYMMETRY report. Ignored with --position/--positions-file.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum-axis detection threshold in Ang (default: 10.0).
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory for the whole OER workflow (default: oer_study).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/oer_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-oer -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --site-type all
  stb-oer -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --site-type ontop --both-sides
  stb-oer -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --position 1.23 0.71 --height 1.8
  stb-oer -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --positions-file sites/site_positions.dat
  stb-oer -s slab.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --n-orientations-polar 5 --n-orientations-azimuthal 8 --ml-rank --orientation-top-k 2

stb-oerAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-oerAnalysis [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [--file FILE] [--temp TEMP]
                       [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE] [-o OUTPUT] [--save-report]
                       [--plot] [--no-plot] [--show] [--no-show] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 4 of 4: combines every reference energy from stb-oerRefs into Delta-G1..4, the theoretical overpotential eta, and the potential-determining step (PDS).
The 4-electron computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) descriptor for OER (Rossmeisl et al. 2007;
Man et al. 2011), via the 3 adsorbed intermediates OH*, O*, OOH*:
    * + H2O(l)  -> OH*  + (H+ + e-)      dG1 = G(OH*)  + 0.5*G(H2) - G(*)    - G(H2O)
    OH*         -> O*   + (H+ + e-)      dG2 = G(O*)   + 0.5*G(H2) - G(OH*)
    O* + H2O(l) -> OOH* + (H+ + e-)      dG3 = G(OOH*) + 0.5*G(H2) - G(O*)   - G(H2O)
    OOH*        -> *    + O2 + (H+ + e-) dG4 = G(*) + G(O2) - G(OOH*) + 0.5*G(H2)
eta = max(dG1..dG4) - 1.23 V; the step with the largest dG is the potential-determining step (PDS).

[IMPORTANT] No O2 SIESTA reference is ever used. DFT/GGA badly describes the O2 triplet ground
state (a systematic error of at least ~0.3 eV across common functionals -- Sargeant et al. 2021,
J. Electroanal. Chem.), so G(O2) is instead DERIVED from the experimental total reaction free
energy of the overall 4-electron reaction (4 * 1.23 V = 4.92 eV):
    G(O2) = 2*G(H2O) - 2*G(H2) + 4.92 eV
By construction dG1+dG2+dG3+dG4 == 4.92 eV exactly, independent of the actual electronic
energies -- this module prints that sum as a live internal sanity check.

No --zpe-mode 'standard' is offered: every intermediate's (and H2O's own) ZPE/entropy is computed
from your own DFT+phonon data (--zpe-mode local/full in stb-oerRefs), never a hardcoded per-species
literature default -- OER would need 4 additional constants beyond HER's single well-established
H2 value, and their exact digits could not be pinned to a verified primary source during this
tool's development.

[LIMITATION] This descriptor assumes the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM: OH*/O*/OOH* bound at
a single site) -- it does NOT model the lattice oxygen evolution mechanism (LOER, where lattice
oxygen atoms participate directly, common on some oxide/oxyhydroxide catalysts and linked to
catalyst instability under anodic potential; see Exner, ChemCatChem 2021). Treat eta here as an
AEM-only estimate, not the full mechanistic picture, especially for perovskites or Ru/Ir oxides.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-oer/stb-oerIntermediates/stb-oerRefs (default: oer_study).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each folder (default: calc.out).
  --temp TEMP           Temperature in Kelvin, for the local/full ZPE modes' entropy term (default: 298.15). Has no effect on H2's own thermal term (fixed at its 298.15 K literature value regardless of --temp, see the module docstring's H2_ZPE_EV/H2_TS_298K_EV).
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05) above which a folder is flagged as possibly not relaxed/converged. Advisory only.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename (no extension) for the final report (default: OER_report).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <directory>/oer_stage4.txt. Off by default.
  --plot                Save gnuplot .dat/.gplot charts (free-energy (CHE) diagram AND BSSE-correction breakdown) to <directory>/plot/, skipping the interactive prompt this tool otherwise asks at the end. See --no-plot.
  --no-plot             Skip both charts entirely, skipping the interactive prompt (see --plot). Use this for non-interactive/scripted runs.
  --show                Open blocking matplotlib windows with the same two charts on screen (free-energy diagram, then BSSE correction), skipping the interactive prompt this tool otherwise asks. Independent of --plot/--no-plot (the gnuplot files, if any, are still the canonical saved output). Needs a display. See --no-show.
  --no-show             Skip both on-screen matplotlib windows entirely, skipping the interactive prompt (see --show). Use this for non-interactive/scripted/headless runs.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-oerAnalysis --directory oer_study --temp 298.15

stb-oerIntermediates.help:
usage: stb-oerIntermediates [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [--file FILE] [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                            [--oo-bond-length OO_BOND_LENGTH]
                            [--ooh-oh-bond-length OOH_OH_BOND_LENGTH]
                            [--ooh-bend-deg OOH_BEND_DEG]
                            [--ooh-n-orientations-polar OOH_N_ORIENTATIONS_POLAR]
                            [--ooh-n-orientations-azimuthal OOH_N_ORIENTATIONS_AZIMUTHAL]
                            [--orientation-top-k ORIENTATION_TOP_K]
                            [--orientation-rmsd-tol ORIENTATION_RMSD_TOL]
                            [--ml-prerelax] [--ml-model {small,medium,large}]
                            [--ml-device {cpu,cuda}] [--ml-fmax ML_FMAX] [-v]
                            [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 4: derives the O* and OOH* intermediates from the winning OH* site, and writes their own CG-relaxation folder.
Picks the lowest-FreeEng OH* site from Stage 1's 'sites/site_*/', reads its RELAXED geometry, and
builds starting geometries for O* and OOH* from it (O* = OH* minus H, always ONE folder -- a bare
O atom has no orientation to sample; OOH* = OH* plus a second O-H group in a chemically plausible
but illustrative starting orientation -- see build_ooh_structure --help/docstring), writing
'intermediates/o_star/' and 'intermediates/ooh_star/'. With --ooh-n-orientations-polar/-azimuthal
(> 1), OOH*'s new O-H group is instead sampled over several orientations AT THAT SAME SITE (O1,
the site's own relaxed oxygen, never moves -- see --help), optionally MACE-MP-0 ranked
(--ml-prerelax) down to the --orientation-top-k best, writing 'intermediates/ooh_star_orientN/'
folders instead of a single one.

[IMPORTANT] O*/OOH* are ALWAYS derived from the SAME winning OH* site, never independently
site-searched: the computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) descriptor's overpotential/PDS is only
physically meaningful as a single active site progressing through OH*->O*->OOH* (Rossmeisl et al.
2007; Man et al. 2011) -- the well-known ~3.2 eV universal scaling relation between
Delta-G(OOH*) and Delta-G(OH*) is itself derived assuming exactly this shared M-O bond across all
three intermediates. Deriving each intermediate from a DIFFERENT site (an earlier, now-removed
--o-strategy/--ooh-strategy search mode) mixes three different local bonding environments into
one nominal 'pathway', silently breaking that assumption and producing an eta/PDS that does not
correspond to any single physically realizable active site.

Every folder written here MUST be relaxed via SIESTA (MD.TypeOfRun CG is forced on) before
running stb-oerRefs -- O*/OOH*'s starting geometry is only a reasonable guess, not already at
equilibrium. Every folder gets its own config_extra.fdf sidecar (fixed cell,
Slab.DipoleCorrection, Spin polarized, DFTD3, all mandatory -- same combination Stage 1's own
site folders get, %include'd on top of your untouched --calc template, never edited in place).
Each derived geometry is also saved as a 1-frame extended-XYZ trajectory, viewable in OVITO/VMD.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-oer (default: oer_study).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each site folder (default: calc.out).
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank or a folder path.
  --oo-bond-length OO_BOND_LENGTH
                        Illustrative starting O-O bond length for OOH*, in Ang (default: 1.45). Refined by CG relaxation.
  --ooh-oh-bond-length OOH_OH_BOND_LENGTH
                        Illustrative starting O-H bond length for OOH*'s new terminal H, in Ang (default: 0.97).
  --ooh-bend-deg OOH_BEND_DEG
                        Illustrative starting O-O-H bend angle for OOH*, in degrees (default: 100.0, H2O2-like).
  --ooh-n-orientations-polar OOH_N_ORIENTATIONS_POLAR
                        Systematically sample this many initial OOH* orientations AT THE WINNING OH* SITE before relaxing (default: 1, the single-orientation behavior). O1 (the site's own relaxed oxygen) NEVER moves -- only where O2/H point FROM it varies (same Fibonacci-sphere sampling as stb-oer's own --n-orientations-polar, applied to the local O1-O2-H template). No equivalent flag exists for O* (a bare O atom has no orientation to sample). Combined with --ooh-n-orientations-azimuthal below (total = polar x azimuthal). Without --ml-prerelax, EVERY sampled orientation is written as its own 'ooh_star_orientN/' folder directly. With --ml-prerelax, each is MACE-MP-0 relaxed and ranked first, and only the unique/--orientation-top-k survivors become relaxation folders.
  --ooh-n-orientations-azimuthal OOH_N_ORIENTATIONS_AZIMUTHAL
                        Evenly spaced in-plane rotations sampled per polar direction (see --ooh-n-orientations-polar). Default 1.
  --orientation-top-k ORIENTATION_TOP_K
                        With --ml-prerelax and OOH* orientation sampling: keep only the N best-ranked unique (post-deduplication) orientations, instead of every surviving one. Unset (default) keeps every unique orientation.
  --orientation-rmsd-tol ORIENTATION_RMSD_TOL
                        With --ml-prerelax and OOH* orientation sampling: two relaxed orientations within this RMSD (Ang, O1/O2/H only) AND within 0.01 eV of each other are treated as duplicates (default: 0.3).
  --ml-prerelax         Relax O*/OOH*'s adsorbate atoms (positions only, substrate fixed) with MACE-MP-0 before writing the CG-relaxation folder -- same idea as stb-adsorb --ml-rank. Useful because the hand-built OOH* starting geometry (O-O bond length/bend angle) is illustrative, not literature-fitted. With OOH* orientation sampling (see --ooh-n-orientations-polar/-azimuthal above), also drives the MACE-MP-0 ranking/deduplication of sampled orientations. A better-informed starting point for the real SIESTA relaxation, NOT a substitute for it. Needs the optional 'ml' extra.
  --ml-model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size, with --ml-prerelax (default: medium).
  --ml-device {cpu,cuda}
                        Device for --ml-prerelax (default: cpu).
  --ml-fmax ML_FMAX     Force convergence threshold in eV/Ang, with --ml-prerelax (default: 0.05).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-oerIntermediates --directory oer_study
  stb-oerIntermediates --directory oer_study --ml-prerelax
  stb-oerIntermediates --directory oer_study --ooh-n-orientations-polar 4 --ooh-n-orientations-azimuthal 4 --ml-prerelax --ml-device cuda --orientation-top-k 2

stb-oerRefs.help:
usage: stb-oerRefs [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [--file FILE] [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                   [--zpe-mode {local,full}] [--displacement DISPLACEMENT]
                   [--supercell SUPERCELL SUPERCELL SUPERCELL]
                   [--vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 3 of 4: builds the H2/H2O gas-phase references, the BSSE counterpoise correction, and the ZPE/entropy calculation folders for all 3 intermediates (OH*, O*, OOH*).
Locates the final relaxed geometry of OH* (Stage 1's winning site), O*, and OOH* (Stage 2's
derived-and-relaxed intermediates, both always from that SAME winning OH* site), then writes (all
single-point unless noted): '00_clean_slab/' (pristine slab), '02_h2_molecule/' and
'03_h2o_molecule/' (RELAX, gas-phase CHE references), '04_slab_deformed/' (OH*'s geometry with
both adsorbate atoms removed -- diagnostic only), the BSSE counterpoise triads (one PER
INTERMEDIATE -- 05_bsse_OH_*/05_bsse_O_*/05_bsse_OOH_*, 9 folders total, each triad built at
THAT intermediate's own relaxed geometry -- a single triad shared across all 3 intermediates
was removed after a real system showed it systematically under-corrects OH*/O* relative to
their true per-species BSSE, changing eta by ~0.30 V), and the ZPE calculation folder(s)
(--zpe-mode local/full -- no 'standard' mode: OER's per-species thermal corrections are always
computed from your own DFT/phonon data, never a hardcoded literature default, see
stb-oerAnalysis --help). Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each folder yourself, then use
stb-oerAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-oer/stb-oerIntermediates (default: oer_study).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each folder (default: calc.out).
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (default: reuse whatever the winning OH* site's own folder already has).
  --zpe-mode {local,full}
                        ZPE/entropy calculation mode (default: local). 'local': finite-difference displacements of each intermediate's own adsorbate atoms only (fast, decoupled-oscillator approximation). 'full': complete Phonopy displacement sets for the clean slab AND all 3 intermediates (needed to subtract the clean slab's own phonon ZPE/entropy -- see stb-oerAnalysis --help).
  --displacement DISPLACEMENT
                        Finite-difference displacement in Ang, for --zpe-mode local's adsorbate displacements or --zpe-mode full's Phonopy displacements (default: 0.015).
  --supercell SUPERCELL SUPERCELL SUPERCELL
                        Supercell dimensions for --zpe-mode full's phonon calculations (default: 1 1 1).
  --vacuum-box VACUUM_BOX
                        Cubic box side (Ang) for the isolated H2/H2O references (default: 15.0).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-oerRefs --directory oer_study --zpe-mode local

stb-optical.help:
usage: stb-optical [-h] -f FILE [-c CALC] [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                   [--directions {xx,yy,zz,xy,xz,yz} [{xx,yy,zz,xy,xz,yz} ...]]
                   [--optical-mesh NX NY NZ] [--optical-broaden EV]
                   [--optical-nbands N] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [-O OUTPUT_DIR]
                   [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 2: writes one SIESTA folder per requested Cartesian/biaxial polarization direction, ready for a linear-response Optical.Calculate run.
Takes an ALREADY-RELAXED structure (--file) and a calc.fdf template (--calc, default: calc.fdf in the
current directory), and for each requested direction (--directions, default xx yy zz) writes
'<output-dir>/dir_<axis>/' with the SAME structure (no new geometry -- unlike this suite's other
WORKFLOW_TOOLS prep stages, there's nothing to deform/search/enumerate here). Every forced directive
-- MD.TypeOfRun CG / MD.Steps 0 (single-point, no relaxation) plus that folder's own
Optical.Mesh/Optical.Vector/Optical.Broaden/Optical.NumberOfBands block (SIESTA's own linear
-response/RPA dielectric-function machinery -- see the SIESTA manual's Optical.* directives) -- is
written into a config_extra.fdf sidecar, %include'd at the very top of calc.fdf, never edited into
your own --calc template text directly (this suite's standard config_extra.fdf convention -- see
CLAUDE.md). Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each folder yourself, then use stb-opticalAnalysis (which
aggregates every direction folder present into one combined report/spectrum, so run it once against
the whole --output-dir root, not once per folder).

[DIAGONAL vs. BIAXIAL DIRECTIONS] 'xx'/'yy'/'zz' set Optical.Vector to the pure Cartesian unit axis
(e_x/e_y/e_z) -- the diagonal dielectric-tensor component eps_ii comes directly from that one folder.
'xy'/'xz'/'yz' set Optical.Vector to the NORMALIZED BISECTOR of the two axes involved (e.g. xy ->
(e_x+e_y)/sqrt(2)) -- SIESTA's Optical.Vector always computes a single-direction response n^T.eps.n,
never a genuine off-diagonal component directly, so the bisector is the standard trick to reach one:
for a symmetric dielectric tensor, response along that bisector expands to
(eps_ii + eps_jj)/2 + eps_ij, so once eps_ii, eps_jj AND the bisector's own response are all known,
  eps_ij = eps_(bisector ij) - (eps_ii + eps_jj) / 2
recovers the true off-diagonal component. Requesting 'xy' without also requesting 'xx'/'yy' in the
same (or an earlier) run still writes a valid folder -- it's simply not reconstructible into eps_xy
until the 2 diagonal folders it needs also exist; the Stage 1 report flags this per direction.

Stage 2 (stb-opticalAnalysis) auto-detects each folder's direction from its own Optical.Vector value
(not the folder name) and, whenever a biaxial direction's 2 matching diagonal folders are ALSO
present in the same run, applies the reconstruction formula above automatically -- eps_ij(E) is
written to its own dedicated output alongside the raw per-direction eps_ii(E)/eps_jj(E) results, no
extra flag needed. A biaxial folder without its matching diagonal pair is still read normally by
Stage 2 (its raw eps_(bisector)(E) response is real data), just not reconstructible into eps_ij yet.

[KNOWN LIMITATION, 2D/slab inputs] No direction is skipped or specially treated for a vacuum-padded
input -- every requested direction (including out-of-plane and any biaxial one involving it) is still
written and computed. For a slab, the periodic-supercell dielectric response along ANY direction is
diluted by the vacuum region (a well-known methodological caveat for slab dielectric/polarizability
DFT calculations) -- no vacuum-thickness rescaling is applied here. Interpret out-of-plane 2D results
with this in mind.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILE, --file FILE  Already-relaxed input structure.fdf.
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template for the Optical calculations (default: calc.fdf).
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank or a folder path.
  --directions {xx,yy,zz,xy,xz,yz} [{xx,yy,zz,xy,xz,yz} ...]
                        Direction(s) to compute (default: xx yy zz). 'xx'/'yy'/'zz' are the diagonal Cartesian components (Optical.Vector = a unit axis, eps_ii read directly). 'xy'/'xz'/'yz' are BIAXIAL directions (Optical.Vector = the normalized bisector of the 2 axes, e.g. (1,1,0)/sqrt(2) for xy) -- the off-diagonal eps_ij component is only reconstructible from these once the matching xx/yy/zz pair also exists; see the description above for the exact formula.
  --optical-mesh NX NY NZ
                        Optical.Mesh k-point sampling for the optical-transition integral (default: 10 10 10).
  --optical-broaden EV  Optical.Broaden Gaussian broadening in eV (default: 0.2).
  --optical-nbands N    Optical.NumberOfBands (default: SIESTA's own default -- all bands).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum-axis detection threshold in Ang, for the report's dimensionality note only (default: 10.0).
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory for the whole optical-properties workflow (default: optical_study).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/optical_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-optical -f relaxed.fdf -p dojo
  stb-optical -f relaxed.fdf -p dojo --directions xx yy zz xy xz yz

stb-opticalAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-opticalAnalysis [-h] [--directory DIRECTORY] [--file FILE] [-l LABEL]
                           [--energy-min EV] [--energy-max EV]
                           [--plot-quantity {eps,n_k,alpha,R,L,sigma1,all}]
                           [--experimental PATH] [--peak-prominence FRACTION]
                           [--dimensionality-correction] [--thickness ANG] [-o OUTPUT]
                           [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 2: aggregates every direction folder written by stb-optical and derives the full set of linear optical properties.
Scans --directory for every subfolder containing a calc.fdf, identifies each one's direction from its
own %block Optical.Vector (not the folder name -- robust to renamed/reorganized folders; 'xx'/'yy'/
'zz' diagonal or 'xy'/'xz'/'yz' biaxial, the same convention stb-optical writes), reads its
SystemLabel.EPSIMG, and derives eps1(E)/eps2(E) (Kramers-Kronig transform), n(E)/k(E) (refractive
index/extinction coefficient), the absorption coefficient, normal-incidence reflectivity, the
electron energy-loss function, and the real optical conductivity -- all standard textbook relations
(Wooten/Fox, "Optical Properties of Solids"), not flagged [UNVERIFIED]. Missing or incomplete
direction folders are skipped with a warning, never block the directions that ARE ready (advisory
only, same convention as this suite's other multi-folder analysis stages).

[OFF-DIAGONAL RECONSTRUCTION] Whenever a biaxial direction ('xy'/'xz'/'yz') AND its 2 matching
diagonal directions are all present, also reconstructs the true off-diagonal dielectric-tensor
component eps_ij(E) = eps_(bisector ij)(E) - (eps_ii(E) + eps_jj(E)) / 2 (same bisector-based formula
raman_analysis.py's own raman_tensor_full uses for the Raman tensor's Rxy/Rxz/Ryz) and writes it to
its own dedicated output -- eps1_ij/eps2_ij only, NOT n/k/alpha/R/L/sigma1 (those textbook relations
assume a principal-axis/diagonal response and have no standalone meaning for a genuine off-diagonal
tensor component).

[ASSUMPTION] Reflectivity R(E) is normal-incidence, vacuum(n0=1)/material interface -- no angle-
dependent Fresnel formula or thin-film interference is computed. [KNOWN LIMITATION, 2D/1D/0D inputs]
The raw supercell values above are diluted by the vacuum region and NOT corrected by default -- pass
--dimensionality-correction (see its own --help entry) to additionally restore the intrinsic 2D
dielectric function or extract a 0D molecular polarizability, written ALONGSIDE the raw values, never
replacing them (1D is not yet implemented -- see --dimensionality-correction's own help text; this
correction is only ever applied to the 3 diagonal directions, never to a biaxial/reconstructed one).

When all 3 of xx/yy/zz are present, also computes and reports/plots an isotropic ('avg') average --
eps2 averaged across the 3 directions first, then every other quantity (including eps1) re-derived
from that averaged eps2 -- the standard convention for comparing against a polycrystalline/powder
experimental measurement, which doesn't correspond to any single crystallographic direction.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-optical (default: optical_study).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each direction folder, used only for the SCF-convergence advisory check (default: calc.out).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel override (default: auto-detected per folder).
  --energy-min EV       Trim the reported/plotted energy range from below (default: no trim).
  --energy-max EV       Trim the reported/plotted energy range from above (default: no trim).
  --plot-quantity {eps,n_k,alpha,R,L,sigma1,all}
                        Which quantity the combined .gplot overlays across every direction present (default: eps -- plots eps1 AND eps2 together). 'all' writes one .gplot per quantity in a single run (mutually exclusive with --experimental -- pick one specific quantity for a direct comparison instead).
  --experimental PATH   2-column (energy_eV, value) experimental spectrum (e.g. UV-Vis-NIR absorbance/reflectance) to overlay on the plot -- only valid with a single-valued --plot-quantity (alpha/R/L/sigma1), not eps/n_k/all. Peak positions are matched against the isotropic average (if all 3 directions are present) or the first available direction otherwise.
  --peak-prominence FRACTION
                        Minimum peak prominence, as a fraction of that spectrum's own max value, for --experimental's peak-finding (default: 0.01).
  --dimensionality-correction
                        Restore the intrinsic (vacuum-independent) response from the raw vacuum-padded supercell result. 2D (1 vacuum axis): rescales eps(E) via the D-field/E-field continuity argument (Laturia et al., npj 2D Mater. Appl. 2, 6, 2018; Yang & Gao, npj 2D Mater. Appl. 5, 78, 2021) -- requires --thickness. 0D (3 vacuum axes, an isolated molecule): extracts the molecular polarizability alpha(E) via the dilute-limit Clausius-Mossotti relation -- no extra input needed (uses the cell volume). 1D (2 vacuum axes): NOT implemented -- the literature approach (Maxwell-Garnett effective medium) is not a simple generalization of the 2D formula and has not been verified for this tool; prints a [NOTE] and reports only the raw supercell values. 3D (bulk): no-op, nothing to correct. Off by default -- always written ALONGSIDE (never replacing) the raw supercell .dat/.csv files.
  --thickness ANG       Physical thickness of the 2D material in Ang, required together with --dimensionality-correction for a 2D (1 vacuum axis) input. Deliberately not auto-estimated -- 'thickness' of a 2D material is not a single well-defined quantity (atomic span? + van der Waals radii? bulk interlayer spacing?), left to the user's own judgment.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename (no extension) for the .csv/.dat/.gplot outputs (default: optical_results).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <directory>/optical_stage2.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-opticalAnalysis --directory optical_study --plot-quantity alpha
  stb-opticalAnalysis --directory optical_study --plot-quantity alpha --experimental uvvis.dat
  stb-opticalAnalysis --directory optical_study --plot-quantity all
  stb-opticalAnalysis --directory optical_study --dimensionality-correction --thickness 3.13

stb-passivate.help:
usage: stb-passivate [-h] -f FILENAME [--passivant PASSIVANT] [--cutoff CUTOFF]
                     [--bond-length BOND_LENGTH] [-sp SYMPREC] [--ml-relax]
                     [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                     [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report]
                     [--view] [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Caps dangling bonds on a cut surface with a passivating atom.
Detects undercoordinated atoms (e.g. from stb-slab) via local coordination
geometry and places a passivant (default H) along each missing-bond
direction. Only single-missing-bond sites are auto-passivated -- sites
missing 2+ bonds are geometrically underdetermined from local coordination
alone and are reported instead of guessed.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input structure file (.fdf), typically a cut slab.
  --passivant PASSIVANT
                        Element to cap dangling bonds with (default: H).
  --cutoff CUTOFF       Neighbor-search radius in Angstrom, used to determine each atom's coordination number. Default: auto-detected as 1.25x the shortest pairwise distance in the structure.
  --bond-length BOND_LENGTH
                        Passivant bond length in Angstrom. Default: auto, per surface-species/passivant pair, as the sum of their pymatgen atomic radii (an approximation -- e.g. Si+H = 1.35 Ang vs. the experimental Si-H ~1.48 Ang).
  -sp SYMPREC, --symprec SYMPREC
                        Symmetry tolerance in Angstroms for the before/after symmetry analysis (default: 0.01).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax the passivated structure with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) before writing it out -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the cell -- any vacuum-padded axis always stays exactly fixed. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_passivate_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the input structure and the passivated structure (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: passivated.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-passivate -f slab.fdf
  stb-passivate -f slab.fdf --passivant F --bond-length 1.4 -o slab_F.fdf
  stb-passivate -f slab.fdf --ml-relax --save-report --view

stb-phononsCreate.help:
usage: stb-phononsCreate [-h] [-dim DIM DIM DIM] [-d DISTANCE] [-s STRUCTURE]
                         [-c CALC] [-p PSEUDO_DIR] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                         [--symprec SYMPREC] [--kgrid KGRID KGRID KGRID]
                         [--kgrid-density KGRID_DENSITY] [--ml-prerelax]
                         [--ml-model {small,medium,large}] [--ml-device {cpu,cuda}]
                         [--ml-fmax ML_FMAX] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Automate SIESTA phonon displacement folders with Phonopy.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dim DIM DIM DIM      Supercell dimensions (default: 2 2 2)
  -d DISTANCE, --distance DISTANCE
                        Displacement distance in Angstroms (default: 0.01)
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input structure file containing the unit cell (default: structure.fdf)
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  Input calculation parameters file (default: calc.fdf)
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
