                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path (default: current directory).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum gap (Ang) along an axis to consider it vacuum-padded, for the supercell-dimension advisory (default: 10.0)
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (Ang) Phonopy uses internally to reduce how many displacements are actually needed (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default -- matches the rest of the suite, and deliberately NOT Phonopy's own raw default of 1e-5, which is far too tight for a real DFT-relaxed structure and can misdetect the true space group: verified live on a real relaxed AlP zincblende structure, 1e-5 reports the wrong R3m while 0.01 correctly reports F-43m). Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance.
  --kgrid KGRID KGRID KGRID
                        Explicit Monkhorst-Pack k-grid 'X Y Z' for the SUPERCELL's own single-point SCF (e.g. --kgrid 2 2 2). Overrides the automatic --kgrid-density suggestion. Written into config_extra.fdf (see [1]) as the first directive, so it takes precedence over --calc's own k-grid, which was tuned for the smaller unit cell.
  --kgrid-density KGRID_DENSITY
                        K-point density (1/Ang) used to auto-suggest the supercell's own k-grid when --kgrid isn't given (default: 0.2, same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-strain).
  --ml-prerelax         Optional pre-flight check (opt-in): compute the residual force on the input structure with the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential, and if it's large, run a quick ML relax for reference. An unrelaxed reference structure is a common cause of spurious imaginary phonon modes. Diagnostic only -- this run still generates displacements from the original --structure file unchanged; the ML-relaxed structure is written out separately for you to review/use in a follow-up run.
  --ml-model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size for --ml-prerelax (default: medium).
  --ml-device {cpu,cuda}
                        Device for --ml-prerelax (default: cpu).
  --ml-fmax ML_FMAX     Force threshold (eV/Ang) for --ml-prerelax: above this, a warning is shown and a relax is offered (default: 0.05).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/phonon_prep_properties.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb_phonon --structure structure.fdf --calc calc.fdf --dim 2 2 2
  stb_phonon --pseudo-dir ~/pseudos --distance 0.015

stb-phononsPos.help:
usage: stb-phononsPos [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [-l LABEL] [-m MESH MESH MESH]
                      [--tmin TMIN] [--tmax TMAX] [--tstep TSTEP]
                      [--plot-dir PLOT_DIR] [--bands] [--band-points BAND_POINTS]
                      [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--dos] [--pdos]
                      [--thermal-displacements] [--freeze-unstable-mode]
                      [--freeze-amplitude FREEZE_AMPLITUDE] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                      [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Post-processing for SIESTA phonon calculations using Phonopy.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Directory containing the displacement folders (default: phonon_runs)
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel used in calc.fdf (default: auto-detected from the copied calc.fdf/structure.fdf, falling back to 'siesta')
  -m MESH MESH MESH, --mesh MESH MESH MESH
                        Q-point mesh for thermal properties (default: 20 20 20)
  --tmin TMIN           Minimum temperature in K (default: 0)
  --tmax TMAX           Maximum temperature in K (default: 1000)
  --tstep TSTEP         Temperature step in K (default: 10)
  --plot-dir PLOT_DIR   Directory (inside the phonon directory) for gnuplot .dat/.gplot output (default: phonon_plots)
  --bands               Compute and plot the phonon band structure along an auto-detected high-symmetry path
  --band-points BAND_POINTS
                        Number of q-points per band-structure path segment (default: 101)
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum gap (Ang) along an axis to consider it vacuum-padded, for --bands' periodicity detection (default: 10.0)
  --dos                 Compute and plot the total phonon density of states
  --pdos                Compute and plot the phonon density of states projected per chemical species
  --thermal-displacements
                        Compute per-atom thermal displacement (Debye-Waller) tensors and write a tdispmat.cif
  --freeze-unstable-mode
                        If the mesh has an imaginary (unstable) mode, export the structure frozen along that mode's displacement pattern as frozen_mode.fdf -- a starting point for a real relaxation
  --freeze-amplitude FREEZE_AMPLITUDE
                        Target maximum atomic displacement (Ang) for --freeze-unstable-mode (default: 0.05)
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (Ang), used for force-constant symmetrization and the --bands high-symmetry path (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default -- matches the rest of the suite, and deliberately NOT Phonopy's/ASE's own raw defaults (1e-5 / 2e-4), which are far tighter than typical DFT-relaxation noise). A much TIGHTER value than what stb-phononsCreate used to reduce the displacements (its own --symprec, also default 0.01) can fail to reconstruct force constants -- loosen, don't tighten, if in doubt.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <directory>/phonon_properties.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a .dat + .gplot pair for every computed quantity (thermal properties, bands, group velocity, DOS, PDOS, thermal displacements). Off by default -- this tool previously wrote these unconditionally on every run.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the computed plots (thermal properties, bands, DOS, PDOS) before finishing. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  phonons_post -dir phonon_runs -l siesta -m 20 20 20
  phonons_post --tmin 0 --tmax 800 --tstep 5

stb-pseudo.help:
usage: stb-pseudo [-h] [-f PATH] [--species SPECIES [SPECIES ...]] [-p BANK_OR_PATH]
                  [--fallback-dir BANK_OR_PATH] [--list-elements BANK] [-o OUTPUT]
                  [--dry-run] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Resolves the pseudopotentials a structure needs and copies them into a run folder.
Give a structure file (-f/--file, .fdf) or an explicit element list (--species),
plus a pseudopotential source (-p/--pp-path -- a bundled bank name or a
directory of your own .psf/.psml files). Reports which elements were found
and which are missing, and copies the resolved files into -o/--output
(default: the current directory) unless --dry-run is given. --fallback-dir
supplies a second source consulted only for elements missing from the
primary one. --list-elements browses a bundled bank without needing a
structure at all.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f PATH, --file PATH  Path to a SIESTA structure file (.fdf) to read the required species from. Required unless --species or --list-elements is given.
  --species SPECIES [SPECIES ...]
                        Element symbol(s) to resolve directly, instead of reading a structure file. Mutually exclusive with -f/--file.
  -p BANK_OR_PATH, --pp-path BANK_OR_PATH
                        Pseudopotential source: a bundled bank name (dojo, virtual_vault) or a directory of your own .psf/.psml files. Required unless --list-elements is given.
  --fallback-dir BANK_OR_PATH
                        A second pseudopotential source, consulted only for elements missing from -p/--pp-path -- fills gaps automatically instead of just reporting them as missing.
  --list-elements BANK  Print the elements available in a bundled bank and exit -- no structure or -p/--pp-path needed.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Directory to copy the resolved pseudopotentials into. Default: the current directory.
  --dry-run             Only run the availability check and report -- do not copy any files.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_pseudo_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-pseudo -f structure.fdf -p dojo -o .
  stb-pseudo --species Fe O -p dojo --fallback-dir virtual_vault
  stb-pseudo -f structure.fdf -p dojo --dry-run
  stb-pseudo --list-elements dojo

stb-raman.help:
usage: stb-raman [-h] [-s STRUCTURE] [-c CALC] [-p PSEUDO_DIR] [-dim DIM DIM DIM]
                 [-d DISTANCE] [--kgrid KGRID KGRID KGRID]
                 [--kgrid-density KGRID_DENSITY] [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP]
                 [--symprec SYMPREC] [-O OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 3: generates the phonon-displacement folders for a Raman spectrum workflow.
Workflow: (1) this tool generates 'raman_study/phonon_disp/disp-*/' -- run
SIESTA in every folder yourself; (2) once they're done, run stb-ramanModes
to build FORCE_SETS from them, identify the Gamma-point vibrational modes,
and generate the +/-delta Optical-calculation displacement folders needed
for the Raman tensor; (3) run SIESTA in those, then stb-ramanAnalysis to
get the Raman-active frequencies/activities and spectrum. This whole
workflow computes its own phonons -- it does NOT need item 4's
stb-phononsCreate/stb-phononsPos run first (though the underlying Phonopy
machinery is shared, via core/phonon_workflow.py).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input structure file containing the unit cell (default: structure.fdf)
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  Input calculation parameters file (default: calc.fdf)
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path (default: current directory).
  -dim DIM DIM DIM      Supercell dimensions for the phonon force-constant calculation (default: 2 2 2).
  -d DISTANCE, --distance DISTANCE
                        Phonon displacement distance in Angstroms (default: 0.02).
  --kgrid KGRID KGRID KGRID
                        Explicit Monkhorst-Pack grid for the supercell's forced single-point SCF (e.g. --kgrid 2 2 2). Overrides the automatic --kgrid-density suggestion. Written into config_extra.fdf (see [2]).
  --kgrid-density KGRID_DENSITY
                        Target k-point density (1/Ang), used to auto-suggest the supercell k-grid when --kgrid isn't given (default: 0.2, same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-strain/stb-phononsCreate).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum gap (Ang) along an axis to consider it vacuum-padded, for the supercell-dimension advisory (default: 10.0)
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (Ang) Phonopy uses internally to reduce how many displacements are actually needed (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default -- matches the rest of the suite, and deliberately NOT Phonopy's own raw default of 1e-5, which is far too tight for a real DFT-relaxed structure and can misdetect the true point group -- see stb-ramanModes' own --symprec, which is what actually drives the Raman-active/inactive classification. Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance.
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory for the whole Raman workflow (default: raman_study) -- phonon displacements are written under <output-dir>/phonon_disp/.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/raman_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-raman -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo
  stb-raman -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p ~/pseudos -dim 2 2 2 -d 0.02
  stb-raman -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo -dim 5 5 1 --symprec 0.02
  stb-raman -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo -dim 3 3 1 --kgrid-density 0.05

Notes:
  - --symprec (default 0.01 Ang) controls how many displacement folders Phonopy
    actually needs to write here: a HIGHER detected symmetry means FEWER, cheaper
    SIESTA runs (see [4] PHONON DISPLACEMENTS' reduction-percent line). But its
    real, more important effect is downstream, in stb-ramanModes: that tool
    reloads these same force constants with its OWN --symprec and uses whichever
    point group IT detects to decide which modes are Raman-active/forbidden and
    which ones are truly degenerate (--use-symmetry/--skip-degenerate). Phonopy's
    own raw default (1e-5) is far tighter than any real DFT relaxation's residual
    noise (e.g. a cell angle of 119.999 deg instead of an exact 120 deg is normal
    CG-relaxation noise, not a real symmetry breaking) and can silently DETECT A
    LOWER SYMMETRY than the crystal actually has -- this is why 0.01 (pymatgen's
    own default) is used here instead. Pass THE SAME --symprec to both stages, or
    the mode numbering/classification stb-ramanModes reports may not match what
    this stage assumed when it wrote (or skipped) a displacement here. If the
    space/point group stb-ramanModes reports doesn't match what you expect for
    this crystal, rerun both stages with a looser --symprec (e.g. 0.02-0.1).
  - --kgrid-density (default 0.2 1/Ang, same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-strain/
    stb-phononsCreate) is unrelated to symmetry -- it sets how finely the ELECTRONIC
    structure is sampled for the SUPERCELL force calculation done here, which is
    what the phonon frequencies computed by stb-ramanModes are actually built
    from. A coarse density under-samples the electronic structure and can leave
    the reported frequencies far from experiment -- most dramatically for a
    metal/semimetal with a Kohn anomaly (e.g. graphene's G-band/E2g mode, whose
    frequency is directly coupled to the Fermi-surface electrons: verified here to
    move by >100 cm^-1 just from doubling the k-density, long after the supercell
    size itself had stopped mattering). If a computed frequency looks far from the
    literature/experimental value, suspect --kgrid-density before --dim (supercell
    size) -- in practice the two are NOT interchangeable levers: --kgrid-density
    converges the frequency for a semimetal much faster than growing --dim does.
  - This flag only tunes the k-grid HERE, for [4]'s big supercell SCF. Stage 2's
    own single-point Optical (dielectric-tensor) runs are small, unit-cell-sized
    calculations that reuse whatever kgrid.MonkhorstPack is already inside the
    --calc file YOU pass to stb-ramanModes -- there is no equivalent
    --kgrid-density flag on that stage. To keep the whole workflow at a
    consistent, converged k-density end to end, edit that block by hand in the
    calc.fdf you give stb-ramanModes (it can be a different file from this one).

stb-ramanAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-ramanAnalysis [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [-l LABEL] [--file FILE]
                         [--linewidth LINEWIDTH] [--temperature K] [-o OUTPUT]
                         [--experimental FILE] [--peak-prominence FRACTION]
                         [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Stage 3 of 3: analyzes a stb-ramanModes Optical-calculation sweep and computes the Raman spectrum.
Reads each mode's folders (+/-delta x, y, z, and, if stb-ramanModes was run
with --full-tensor, also the (x+y)/sqrt(2), (x+z)/sqrt(2), (y+z)/sqrt(2)
mixed directions), extracts the imaginary part of the dielectric function
from SystemLabel.EPSIMG, obtains the static dielectric constant via a
Kramers-Kronig transform (core/dielectric.py), and takes a central finite
difference across +/-delta to get the Raman tensor per mode. Auto-detects
per mode whether the full symmetric tensor (Rxx, Ryy, Rzz, Rxy, Rxz, Ryz)
or just the diagonal (Rxx, Ryy, Rzz) is available from the folders Stage 2
actually wrote -- the full tensor gives the EXACT literature Raman-activity
invariant (45a'^2+7gamma'^2); diagonal-only gives an APPROXIMATION missing
the off-diagonal anisotropy contribution. Writes a Lorentzian-summed
spectrum (.dat/.gplot).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-raman/stb-ramanModes (default: raman_study).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel used in Stage 2's Optical calc.fdf (default: auto-detected).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each mode_*/ folder (default: calc.out).
  --linewidth LINEWIDTH
                        Lorentzian linewidth (cm^-1) for the summed spectrum (default: 10.0).
  --temperature K       Weight each mode's spectrum contribution by the Stokes Bose-Einstein thermal population factor (n+1) at this temperature (Kelvin). Default: no weighting (every mode contributes by its raw activity alone, as before this option existed).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename (no extension) for the spectrum .dat/.gplot pair (default: raman_spectrum), written under '<directory>/plot/' -- only relevant with --save-gnuplot.
  --experimental FILE   Overlay a measured Raman spectrum (2-column text file: frequency cm^-1, intensity) on the simulated one, and report a nearest-neighbor peak match (simulated vs. experimental peak positions, one row per experimental peak). Plotted on a separate y-axis (simulated 'activity' and real intensity aren't on the same scale).
  --peak-prominence FRACTION
                        Minimum peak prominence, as a fraction of that spectrum's own max intensity, for --experimental's peak-finding (default: 0.01 -- filters out sub-1% noise bumps in both spectra).
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <directory>/raman_stage3.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also save the spectrum (and, with --experimental, the overlaid measured spectrum) as gnuplot .dat + .gplot scripts, under '<directory>/plot/'. Off by default.
  --view                View the Raman spectrum (and, with --experimental, the overlaid measured spectrum on a second y-axis) interactively via matplotlib now. Off by default. Needs a display. Independent of --save-gnuplot -- matplotlib here is only an on-screen preview, never written to disk.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-ramanAnalysis --directory raman_study

stb-ramanModes.help:
usage: stb-ramanModes [-h] [-dir DIRECTORY] [-l LABEL] [-p DIR] -c CALC
                      [--modes N [N ...]] [--freq-min FREQ_MIN] [--freq-max FREQ_MAX]
                      [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                      [--rotational-mode-tol ROTATIONAL_MODE_TOL]
                      [--displacement DISPLACEMENT] [--full-tensor] [--use-symmetry]
                      [--reduce-components] [--skip-degenerate]
                      [--optical-mesh OPTICAL_MESH OPTICAL_MESH OPTICAL_MESH]
                      [--optical-nbands OPTICAL_NBANDS]
                      [--optical-broaden OPTICAL_BROADEN] [--export-animations]
                      [--animation-frames ANIMATION_FRAMES] [--view-animation] [-v]
                      [--no-intro]

Stage 2 of 3: builds FORCE_SETS from Stage 1's phonon displacements, identifies the Gamma-point vibrational modes, and generates the +/-delta Optical-calculation displacement folders needed for the Raman tensor.
For each selected mode, writes 6 folders by default (2 signs x 3
Optical.Vector axes: x, y, z -- a diagonal-only Raman tensor Rxx/Ryy/Rzz)
under <directory>/optical_disp/, or 12 with --full-tensor (adds the
(x+y)/sqrt(2), (x+z)/sqrt(2), (y+z)/sqrt(2) face-diagonal directions needed
to also recover Rxy/Rxz/Ryz). stb-ramanAnalysis auto-detects which scope
was used from the folders actually present. Doesn't run SIESTA itself --
run each folder's calculation yourself, then use stb-ramanAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -dir DIRECTORY, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Root directory written by stb-raman (Stage 1) -- must contain 'phonon_disp/' (default: raman_study).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel used in Stage 1's calc.fdf (default: auto-detected).
  -p DIR, --pseudo-dir DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source: a bundled bank or a folder path. Default: reuse whatever Stage 1 already resolved and copied into its phonon_disp/disp-*/ folders (the normal, self-contained case -- no need to point at a source a second time). Only needed if that folder is missing pseudopotentials for some reason (e.g. hand-built phonon_disp/ instead of a real stb-raman run).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template for the Optical calculations -- can be the same file used in Stage 1 or a different one (e.g. a denser k-grid, since these are now single-point evaluations on the small unit cell, not the phonon supercell).
  --modes N [N ...]     1-based mode index/indices to process (in ascending-frequency order, acoustic modes already excluded -- see Stage 2's own [1] PHONON MODES table for the numbering). Default: every non-acoustic mode.
  --freq-min FREQ_MIN   Skip modes below this frequency (THz).
  --freq-max FREQ_MAX   Skip modes above this frequency (THz).
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Minimum gap (Ang) along an axis to consider it vacuum-padded, same convention as stb-raman (default: 10.0). Only used to detect a genuinely isolated (0D) structure, which has 3 extra trivial (free-rotation) modes at Gamma beyond the usual 3 translations -- irrelevant for 3D/2D/1D structures.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (Ang) Phonopy uses internally when loading the force constants -- drives both the reported point group and, when --use-symmetry is on, the Raman-active/inactive classification and degenerate-mode grouping (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default -- matches the rest of the suite, and deliberately NOT Phonopy's own raw default of 1e-5, which is far too tight for a real DFT-relaxed structure and can misdetect the true point group: a mode that should be exactly degenerate can come out as two separate near-identical frequencies, and a symmetry-silent mode can be misclassified as Raman-active). Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance.
  --rotational-mode-tol ROTATIONAL_MODE_TOL
                        0D (molecule) only: a mode within the first 3 bands after the translations is treated as free rotation (trivial, excluded) if |frequency| is below this (THz) (default: 2.0). Lower this if your molecule has genuine low-frequency skeletal/torsional vibrational modes you want to make sure aren't mistaken for rotation.
  --displacement DISPLACEMENT
                        Finite-difference displacement (Ang) along each mode's eigendisplacement for the Raman-tensor derivative (default: 0.02).
  --full-tensor         Compute the FULL symmetric Raman tensor (Rxx, Ryy, Rzz, Rxy, Rxz, Ryz) instead of just the diagonal -- adds 3 more Optical.Vector directions per sign (the face-diagonals), doubling the folder count per mode (12 instead of 6). Off-diagonal components are recovered by stb-ramanAnalysis from these mixed-direction measurements.
  --use-symmetry        Skip modes that group theory guarantees are Raman-INACTIVE (their irreducible representation at Gamma isn't contained in the quadratic-function representation x^2/y^2/z^2/xy/xz/yz -- their Raman tensor is exactly zero, not just numerically small). Works for any of the 32 point groups, not just centrosymmetric ones. Only applies to the default mode selection (every non-acoustic mode) -- an explicit --modes list is never second-guessed. Needs a PRIMITIVE cell (see stb-unitcell --mode primitive); falls back to running every mode, with a warning, if that's not available.
  --reduce-components   For a non-degenerate mode whose Raman tensor SHAPE is fixed by symmetry up to one overall scale (a single-band irrep with multiplicity exactly 1 in the quadratic-function representation), probe only ONE Optical.Vector direction instead of all of them -- stb-ramanAnalysis reconstructs the rest algebraically. Falls back to full probing for degenerate modes or any mode whose tensor shape isn't uniquely fixed (needs a PRIMITIVE cell, same as --use-symmetry; degrades to no reduction, never a crash, if that's not available).
  --skip-degenerate     For a degenerate group of modes (2 or more bands sharing one irrep, e.g. an E or T representation), write Optical folders for only ONE representative band and skip the rest entirely -- Raman activity and the depolarization ratio are rotational invariants of the tensor, so whatever orthogonal transformation relates two degenerate partners (guaranteed to exist by group theory, even though phonopy's returned eigenvectors don't tell you which one) leaves both invariants unchanged -- the representative's computed values apply exactly to every other partner in its group. stb-ramanAnalysis reuses them automatically. Needs a PRIMITIVE cell (same as --use-symmetry/--reduce-components; degrades to running every mode, with a warning, if that's not available).
  --optical-mesh OPTICAL_MESH OPTICAL_MESH OPTICAL_MESH
                        Optical.Mesh k-grid for the dielectric-function calculation (default: 10 10 10).
  --optical-nbands OPTICAL_NBANDS
                        Optical.NumberOfBands (default: SIESTA's own default -- all bands within the basis).
  --optical-broaden OPTICAL_BROADEN
                        Optical.Broaden in eV (default: 0.2).
  --export-animations   Write a looping animation of each selected mode's eigendisplacement (a smooth 0/+A/0/-A/0 sweep) as optical_disp/mode_XX_animation.axsf -- open in XCrySDen/VESTA to see which atoms move before interpreting the spectrum. Same amplitude as --displacement.
  --animation-frames ANIMATION_FRAMES
                        Frames per mode animation, with --export-animations (default: 20).
  --view-animation      After everything else is written, open each selected mode's eigendisplacement animation in an interactive ASE viewer window (ase-gui), one mode at a time -- close a window to advance to the next. Needs a display (X11/Wayland); off by default. Independent of --export-animations -- works whether or not the .axsf files are also written to disk, and vice versa.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage example:
  stb-ramanModes --directory raman_study --calc calc_optical.fdf
  stb-ramanModes --directory raman_study --calc calc_optical.fdf --modes 1 2 3

stb-slab.help:
usage: stb-slab [-h] -f FILENAME --hkl H K L [--min-slab-size MIN_SLAB_SIZE]
                [--min-vacuum-size MIN_VACUUM_SIZE] [--lll-reduce] [--center-slab]
                [--primitive] [--symmetrize] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                [-i | --termination TERMINATION] [--all] [--passivate]
                [--passivant PASSIVANT] [--cutoff CUTOFF] [--bond-length BOND_LENGTH]
                [--ml-relax] [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report] [--view]
                [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Cuts a Miller-index slab from a bulk SIESTA FDF structure.
Adds vacuum along the surface normal; the vacuum axis lands on c.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input bulk structure file (.fdf).
  --hkl H K L           Miller index of the surface to cut, e.g. --hkl 1 0 0
  --min-slab-size MIN_SLAB_SIZE
                        Minimum slab thickness in Angstrom (default: 10.0).
  --min-vacuum-size MIN_VACUUM_SIZE
                        Minimum vacuum thickness in Angstrom (default: 15.0).
  --lll-reduce          LLL-reduce the slab lattice (pymatgen SlabGenerator option).
  --center-slab         Center the slab in the middle of the vacuum (pymatgen SlabGenerator option).
  --primitive           Reduce the bulk to its primitive cell before cutting the slab. Off by default so the input cell is used as given.
  --symmetrize          Ask pymatgen to symmetrize polar/asymmetric terminations.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry tolerance, Ang, used for the polar/symmetric diagnostics AND the before/after symmetry table (default: 0.1).
  -i, --interactive     Show all terminations found and prompt for one to keep.
  --termination TERMINATION
                        Directly select a termination index (0-based). Default: index 0 after sorting non-polar/symmetric terminations first.
  --all                 Write every termination found, instead of just one.
  --passivate           Cap dangling bonds on each written termination with a passivating atom (same logic as stb-passivate). Only single-missing-bond sites are auto-passivated; sites missing 2+ bonds are reported instead of guessed.
  --passivant PASSIVANT
                        Element to cap dangling bonds with, only with --passivate (default: H).
  --cutoff CUTOFF       Neighbor-search radius in Angstrom for --passivate. Default: auto-detected (see stb-passivate --help).
  --bond-length BOND_LENGTH
                        Passivant bond length in Angstrom for --passivate. Default: auto per species pair (see stb-passivate --help).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax each written slab with a MACE potential before writing it out (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the in-plane cell -- the vacuum axis always stays exactly fixed. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_slab_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) of the bulk structure and every written slab (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file(s). Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: slab.fdf). When more than one termination is written, it is suffixed '_term0', '_term1', ...
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-slab -f bulk.fdf --hkl 1 0 0
  stb-slab -f bulk.fdf --hkl 1 1 1 -i
  stb-slab -f bulk.fdf --hkl 1 1 1 --all -o surface.fdf
  stb-slab -f bulk.fdf --hkl 1 1 1 --passivate
  stb-slab -f bulk.fdf --hkl 1 1 1 --ml-relax --save-report --view

stb-spintexture.help:
usage: stb-spintexture [-h] [--label LABEL] [--wfsx WFSX] [--hsx-file HSX_FILE]
                       [--geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE]
                       [--shift {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual,none}]
                       [--manual-value MANUAL_VALUE] [--fermi FERMI]
                       [--bands-file BANDS_FILE] [--fermi-file FERMI_FILE]
                       [--gap-tol GAP_TOL] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report]
                       [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Spin texture (<Sx>,<Sy>,<Sz>) scattered onto a band structure, from a non-collinear/SOC SIESTA .WFSX.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Auto-detects <label>.WFSX, falling back to <label>.selected.WFSX then <label>.bands.WFSX, and, unless --hsx-file/--geometry-file override it, <label>.HSX (optional, upgrades accuracy) then <label>.fdf. Mutually exclusive with --wfsx (not --hsx-file/--geometry-file -- see their own help).
  --wfsx WFSX           Explicit path to the .WFSX file (alternative to --label).
  --hsx-file HSX_FILE   Optional explicit .HSX path for physically correct overlap-weighted spin moments. Falls back to --geometry-file / auto-detected .fdf with an accuracy warning if omitted. Optional (and common) together WITH --label too, since the real file is often not literally named <label>.HSX.
  --geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE
                        Optional explicit .fdf geometry path, used as the fallback parent when no .HSX is available.
  --shift {vbm,cbm,fermi,manual,none}
                        Energy reference (default: none, i.e. raw eigenvalues as stored in the .WFSX).
  --manual-value MANUAL_VALUE
                        Custom shift value (eV), required if --shift manual.
  --fermi FERMI         Fermi energy (eV) for --shift fermi/vbm/cbm. Highest-priority source if given.
  --bands-file BANDS_FILE
                        Companion .bands file to read the Fermi energy from, for --shift fermi/vbm/cbm.
  --fermi-file FERMI_FILE
                        Explicit SIESTA .out log to read the Fermi energy from, for --shift fermi/vbm/cbm -- an alternative to --bands-file for a run with no saved .bands file. Not assumed to be named after --label.
  --gap-tol GAP_TOL     Energy tolerance in eV for VBM/CBM classification when --shift is vbm/cbm (default: 0.01).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write spintexture_S{x,y,z}.dat/.gplot (with --save-gnuplot) and stb_spintexture_report.txt/references.bib into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_spintexture_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write spintexture_S{x,y,z}.dat + spintexture.gplot. Off by default -- this tool used to write both unconditionally on every run.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview before finishing. Off by default -- this tool previously always showed it, with no way to skip.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-spintexture --label siesta --shift fermi --fermi -4.2
  stb-spintexture --label siesta --shift fermi --fermi-file calc.out \
      --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-sqs.help:
usage: stb-sqs [-h] -f FILENAME --sublattice SUBLATTICE --composition COMPOSITION
               [--scaling SCALING] [--method {monte_carlo,enumeration}]
               [--instances INSTANCES] [--temperature TEMPERATURE]
               [--mc-steps MC_STEPS] [--cluster-cutoffs CLUSTER_CUTOFFS] [-sp SYMPREC]
               [--ml-relax] [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
               [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report] [--view]
               [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Generates a Special Quasirandom Structure (SQS) for a substitutional alloy.
Picks one sublattice (--sublattice) and disorders it with a target
composition, then searches for the atomic arrangement that best mimics an
ideal random alloy (via icet's Monte Carlo or enumeration SQS search).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input structure file (.fdf).
  --sublattice SUBLATTICE
                        Existing species whose sites become the disordered alloy sublattice.
  --composition COMPOSITION
                        Target composition on that sublattice, e.g. 'Fe:0.5,Ni:0.5' (must sum to 1.0). Practically limited to 2 species: pymatgen's own SQSTransformation/IcetSQS wrapper (pymatgen/io/icet.py) builds its internal reference structure the same way this tool's minimal_scaling() used to (a replace_species() call that leaves a site's occupancy dict merged rather than collapsed for 3+ species), and raises 'ASE Atoms only supports ordered structures' during the search itself for a 3+ -species composition -- verified upstream in the installed pymatgen, not something this tool can work around without bypassing SQSTransformation entirely.
  --scaling SCALING     icet supercell-size control (positive integer). Multiplies icet's own internally-detected primitive unit, not necessarily the literal input atom count -- read the actual resulting atom count from the output. Default: auto-detect the smallest scaling that gives every species in --composition an exact atom count (a --scaling that doesn't divide evenly is rejected, since icet would otherwise fail to find any candidate structure at that size).
  --method {monte_carlo,enumeration}
                        SQS search method (default: monte_carlo).
  --instances INSTANCES
                        Number of parallel search instances/processes (default: 1, serial). For --method enumeration, icet's own enumeration of candidate structures is single -threaded regardless of this value -- only the (comparatively cheap) scoring of already-generated candidates is split across instances, so raising it rarely helps. For monte_carlo, each instance runs an independent full search and the best is kept, which can help on a machine with real spare cores -- but every instance re-pays icet/pymatgen's startup cost (imports, primitive-cell detection via spglib), so on a loaded or virtualized machine more instances can end up *slower* in wall time despite using more CPU overall. Benchmark before raising this; don't assume it helps.
  --temperature TEMPERATURE
                        Monte Carlo starting temperature (default: 1.0).
  --mc-steps MC_STEPS   Caps the number of Monte Carlo steps (--method monte_carlo only). Default: icet's own default.
  --cluster-cutoffs CLUSTER_CUTOFFS
                        Cluster size:shell pairs, e.g. '2:3,3:2' (default: icet's own {2:3, 3:2, 4:1}).
  -sp SYMPREC, --symprec SYMPREC
                        Symmetry tolerance in Angstroms for the before/after symmetry analysis (default: 0.01).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax the SQS structure found with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) before writing it out -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the cell -- any vacuum-padded axis always stays exactly fixed. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_sqs_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the input structure and the final SQS structure (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: sqs.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-sqs -f ni.fdf --sublattice Ni --composition Ni:0.5,Fe:0.5
  stb-sqs -f ni.fdf --sublattice Ni --composition Ni:0.75,Fe:0.25 --scaling 8 --method enumeration
  stb-sqs -f ni.fdf --sublattice Ni --composition Ni:0.5,Fe:0.5 --ml-relax --save-report --view

stb-stackingfault.help:
usage: stb-stackingfault [-h] -l1 LAYER1 -l2 LAYER2 -c CALC [-p PSEUDO_DIR]
                         [-a MAX_AREA] [-s MAX_STRAIN] [-id MATCH_ID] [-g GAP]
                         [--vacuum VACUUM] [-sm {top,bottom,sym}] [-t TWIST] [--d3]
                         [--no-d3] [--mode {1,2,3}] [--relax-z-steps RELAX_Z_STEPS]
                         [--scan {surface,x,y,xy}] [-n SCAN_POINTS] [-nx GRID_NX]
                         [-ny GRID_NY] [--ml-prerelax-layers] [--ml-preview]
                         [--ml-model {small,medium,large}] [--ml-custom-model PATH]
                         [--ml-device {cpu,cuda}] [--ml-fmax ML_FMAX] [-O OUTPUT_DIR]
                         [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Prepares SIESTA folders for a 2D stacking-fault (generalized stacking fault energy / gamma-surface) study: rigidly slides one layer of a bilayer across a 2D grid of lateral offsets and writes one SIESTA folder per grid point -- a plain single-point by default, or a real/ML-assisted z-only relaxation, see --mode.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l1 LAYER1, --layer1 LAYER1
                        Bottom monolayer .fdf (stays fixed).
  -l2 LAYER2, --layer2 LAYER2
                        Top monolayer .fdf (rigidly slid across the grid). Pass the same file as --layer1 for a material sliding against itself.
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template (kgrid, basis, XC, %include structure.fdf, etc.) -- copied into every shift_II_JJ/ folder; single-point SCF enforcement (and the optional --d3 dispersion correction) is added via a config_extra.fdf %include, not embedded inline.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank or a folder path.
  -a MAX_AREA, --max_area MAX_AREA
                        Maximum ZSL commensurate-supercell area, Ang^2 (default: 150.0, same as stb-2Dstacking).
  -s MAX_STRAIN, --max_strain MAX_STRAIN
                        Maximum allowed ZSL match strain fraction (default: 0.05).
  -id MATCH_ID, --match_id MATCH_ID
                        Which ZSL match to use, 0-based, best (lowest strain) first (default: 0).
  -g GAP, --gap GAP     Interlayer gap in Ang (default: 3.2, same as stb-2Dstacking). Under --mode 3 (default) this is the FIXED value used across the whole grid -- a rigid-shift protocol, standard in the literature (see the [INFO] closest-contact line in the report for how close high-energy registries got at this fixed distance). Under --mode 1/2 this is only the STARTING guess -- SIESTA (mode 1) or MACE-MP-0 (mode 2) relaxes it per grid point from here.
  --vacuum VACUUM       Target vacuum space in Ang. Inherits --layer1's by default.
  -sm {top,bottom,sym}, --strain_mode {top,bottom,sym}
                        Strain distribution mode for the ZSL match (default: top).
  -t TWIST, --twist TWIST
                        Twist angle of layer 2 in degrees (default: 0.0), FIXED for the whole grid -- a different twist is a different physical system, not swept here.
  --d3                  Force the Grimme DFT-D3 dispersion correction (via config_extra.fdf) in every generated calc.fdf -- physically relevant here since the interlayer binding swept across the grid is a van-der-Waals-dominated interaction that plain GGA misses (same correction stb-adsorb/stb-neb force by default elsewhere in the suite). ON by default. Applies in every --mode.
  --no-d3               Disable the DFT-D3 dispersion correction (not recommended for this workflow -- see --d3).
  --mode {1,2,3}        Interlayer-gap strategy, per grid point (default: 1):
                          1 = SIESTA relaxes z for real: writes one restricted CG relaxation per grid point (x,y frozen for every atom, only z free -- see build_z_relax_block/--relax-z-steps). Most accurate (same level of theory as the reported energy), most expensive (a real relaxation, not one SCF, per point).
                          2 = MACE-MP-0 relaxes z first (same x,y-frozen/z-free definition as mode 1, cheap ML engine), THEN writes a plain single-point SIESTA folder at the resulting geometry -- middle ground between cost and accuracy. Needs the optional 'ml' extra.
                          3 = fixed --gap, plain single-point SIESTA, no relaxation of any kind (today's behavior, the cheapest of the three).
  --relax-z-steps RELAX_Z_STEPS
                        With --mode 1: MD.Steps for the restricted SIESTA z-relaxation (default: 200). Ignored in modes 2/3.
  --scan {surface,x,y,xy}
                        Sweep shape (default: surface):
                          surface = full 2D grid (-nx x -ny points), the gamma-surface -- output is the pm3d map/heatmap already documented above.
                          x       = 1D sweep along shift_x only (shift_y fixed at 0) -- -n points, output is a line plot (E vs. distance along x).
                          y       = 1D sweep along shift_y only (shift_x fixed at 0) -- -n points, output is a line plot (E vs. distance along y).
                          xy      = 1D sweep along the diagonal shift_x == shift_y -- -n points, output is a line plot (E vs. distance along the diagonal).
                        -nx/-ny only apply to 'surface'; -n/--scan-points only applies to 'x'/'y'/'xy'.
  -n SCAN_POINTS, --scan-points SCAN_POINTS
                        With --scan x/y/xy: number of points along the 1D sweep (default: 15). Ignored under --scan surface (see -nx/-ny instead).
  -nx GRID_NX, --grid-nx GRID_NX
                        With --scan surface: grid resolution along shift_x, this many lateral shifts covering [0, 1) (default: 7). Independent of --grid-ny -- an anisotropic lattice (a != b, e.g. a rectangular or low-symmetry 2D cell) often warrants a different sampling density per axis rather than forcing a square grid. Ignored under --scan x/y/xy (see -n/--scan-points instead).
  -ny GRID_NY, --grid-ny GRID_NY
                        With --scan surface: grid resolution along shift_y (default: 7). See --grid-nx. Ignored under --scan x/y/xy.
  --ml-prerelax-layers  Relax each monolayer's positions (cell fixed) with MACE-MP-0 before stacking -- a cheap safety net when you're not fully certain --layer1/--layer2 are already at equilibrium. Needs the optional 'ml' extra.
  --ml-preview          Evaluate the whole grid's single-point energy on MACE-MP-0 (fast, no SIESTA) and write stackingfault_ml_preview.png -- a quick sanity check of the gamma-surface's shape before committing to the full Nx x Ny DFT single-points. Written alongside the normal SIESTA folders, not instead of them. Needs the optional 'ml' extra.
  --ml-model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size (default: medium). Ignored if --ml-custom-model is given.
  --ml-custom-model PATH
                        Use a custom MACE model file instead of the MACE-MP-0 foundation potential -- e.g. one fine-tuned on your own SIESTA data via stb-mlffAnalysis. Overrides --ml-model.
  --ml-device {cpu,cuda}
  --ml-fmax ML_FMAX     Force convergence for --ml-prerelax-layers and --mode 2's z-only MACE relaxation (default: 0.05).
  -O OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Root directory (default: current directory) -- everything lives under its 'sf_run/' subfolder (see --save-report): every 'shift_II_JJ/' grid folder under 'sf_run/positions/', the manifest, and the optional report directly under 'sf_run/' -- same self-contained-run-folder convention as stb-adsorb's 'sites/' and stb-neb's 'neb_run/'.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run narrative to <output-dir>/sf_run/stackingfault_setup.txt. Off by default -- the machine-readable sf_manifest.json that stb-stackingfaultAnalysis actually reads is always written regardless of this flag.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-stackingfault -l1 graphene.fdf -l2 graphene.fdf -c calc.fdf -nx 7 -ny 7
  stb-stackingfault -l1 graphene.fdf -l2 hbn.fdf -c calc.fdf -nx 9 -ny 5 -g 3.4
  stb-stackingfault -l1 graphene.fdf -l2 graphene.fdf -c calc.fdf --scan x -n 15

Pass the SAME file for -l1/-l2 for the canonical use case (a material sliding against itself, e.g. graphite ABA vs. ABC stacking) -- already the precedented 'identical layers' case for stb-2Dstacking's own ZSL match. Different files study an interlayer/heterostructure sliding energy landscape instead.

-nx/-ny may differ (an asymmetric grid) -- useful for an anisotropic 2D lattice where one in-plane direction needs finer sampling than the other (--scan surface only).

--scan x/y/xy trade the full 2D gamma-surface for a cheaper 1D line through it (along shift_x, shift_y, or the shift_x=shift_y diagonal) -- useful for a quick high-symmetry-line profile before committing to the full surface.

stb-stackingfaultAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-stackingfaultAnalysis [-h] [--dir DIR] [--file FILE] [-o OUTPUT]
                                 [--apply STRUCTURE_FDF]
                                 [--force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE] [--save-report]
                                 [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [--view-animation] [-v]
                                 [--no-intro]

Computes a stacking-fault (gamma-surface) energy landscape from an stb-stackingfault grid: reads each positions/shift_II_JJ/'s SIESTA energy and reports the equilibrium stacking, the highest-energy registry, and the corrugation energy.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --dir DIR             Root directory containing 'positions/shift_II_JJ/' (default: 'sf_run', the self-contained run folder stb-stackingfault Stage 1 always writes its output into -- auto-detected as '.' instead when the current directory already has its own sf_manifest.json).
  --file FILE           SIESTA output filename inside each folder (default: calc.out).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Base filename for the gnuplot data file (default: stackingfault_surface.dat), written under '<dir>/plot/' -- only relevant with --save-gnuplot.
  --apply STRUCTURE_FDF
                        Copy the equilibrium (lowest-energy) grid point's structure.fdf to this path.
  --force-tolerance FORCE_TOLERANCE
                        Residual atomic force in eV/Ang (default: 0.05, same as stb-adsorbAnalysis/stb-nebAnalysis) above which a grid point's calc.out is flagged as possibly not single-point-converged. Advisory only, never blocks the result.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <dir>/stackingfault_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also save the gamma-surface (or line-scan) data as gnuplot .dat + .gplot scripts, under '<dir>/plot/'. Off by default.
  --view                View the gamma-surface heatmap (or 1D line, for --scan x/y/xy) interactively via matplotlib now. Off by default. Needs a display. Independent of --save-gnuplot -- matplotlib here is only an on-screen preview, never written to disk.
  --view-animation      Open every analyzed grid point's structure (same order as the always-saved animation XYZ) in ASE's interactive multi-frame 3D viewer. Off by default. Needs a display. Independent of --view (which shows the energy plot, not structures).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-stackingfaultAnalysis --dir . --file calc.out
  stb-stackingfaultAnalysis --dir . --apply equilibrium.fdf
  stb-stackingfaultAnalysis --save-gnuplot --view
  stb-stackingfaultAnalysis --view-animation

stb-status.help:
usage: stb-status [-h] [--path PATH] [-l LABEL] [--save-report] [--no-intro] [-v]

SCF convergence, max force, final energy, and which key output files (.XV, .bands,

at once (e.g. 'strain_*').

                        matching several directories (default: current directory).
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        SystemLabel override, applied to every matched directory.
                        Auto-detected per directory from its .fdf file(s) if not

                        default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
