stb-stm.help:
usage: stb-stm [-h] [--label LABEL] [--file LDOS_FILE] [--geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE]
               [--axis {0,1,2}] [--mode {height,current}] [--z Z] [--iso ISO]
               [--z-max Z_MAX] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot]
               [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Simulate an STM image (Tersoff-Hamann approximation) from a SIESTA energy-integrated LDOS grid (<label>.LDOS).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Auto-detects <label>.LDOS (falling back to <label>.STM.LDOS with a note) and <label>.XV/<label>.fdf for the topmost-atom reference. Mutually exclusive with --file/--geometry-file.
  --file LDOS_FILE      Explicit path to the .LDOS/.STM.LDOS file (alternative to --label).
  --geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE
                        Explicit .XV/.fdf geometry path (alternative/override to --label's auto-detect). Required if --file is used instead of --label.
  --axis {0,1,2}        Surface-normal axis (0=X, 1=Y, 2=Z). Auto-detected from the geometry's vacuum padding if omitted and exactly one vacuum axis is found.
  --mode {height,current}
                        'current' (default): classic constant-current STM image -- the topography a tip follows to hold the LDOS at --iso. 'height': constant-height LDOS map at --z above the surface.
  --z Z                 Height (Ang) above the topmost surface atom for --mode height (default: 3.0, a commonly used representative constant-height tip-sample separation).
  --iso ISO             LDOS threshold (same units as the .LDOS file, e/Bohr^3) defining the constant-current contour for --mode current (default: 0.001 -- a relative threshold, not a calibrated absolute current; tune it for your own system's LDOS magnitude if the default leaves too many/few points reaching it, see [3] in the report).
  --z-max Z_MAX         Upper bound (Ang above the topmost atom) of the search/plot window along --axis. Default: distance to the cell boundary.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write stm_<mode>.dat/.gplot into (with --save-gnuplot) and stb_stm_report.txt/references.bib (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_stm_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write stm_<mode>.dat + stm_<mode>.gplot together. Off by default -- this tool used to write both unconditionally on every run.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the STM image before finishing. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-stm --label siesta --mode current --iso 0.001
  stb-stm --label siesta --mode height --z 3.0
  stb-stm --label siesta --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-strain.help:
usage: stb-strain [-h] -s STRUCTURE -c CALC --relax-mode
                  {cell-fixed,stress-constrained} [-p PSEUDO_DIR] --stdir STDIR
                  [--stmin STMIN] [--stmax STMAX] [--step STEP] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                  [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--symprec SYMPREC]
                  [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE] [--save-report] [-v]
                  [--no-intro]

Stage 1 of 2: applies strain in Cartesian coordinates to a SIESTA structure and writes one ready-to-run folder (structure + calc.fdf + config_extra.fdf + pseudopotentials) per scanned strain value. Type (uniaxial/biaxial) is inferred from direction; --relax-mode selects how the cell is allowed to respond (see its own help). Doesn't run SIESTA -- run each folder yourself, then use stb-strainAnalysis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -s STRUCTURE, --structure STRUCTURE
                        Input structure.fdf -- lattice + atomic coordinates. Only this file's %block LatticeVectors is rewritten per strain step; everything else is preserved verbatim. Atomic coordinates MUST be fractional (checked in [1] of the report -- Cartesian positions would not scale with the strained cell).
  -c CALC, --calc CALC  calc.fdf template -- SCF/basis/MD settings, normally %including the structure file above by name. Copied into every generated folder with one line added: '%include config_extra.fdf' (the Geometry.Constraints block --relax-mode builds, see [4] of the report) -- no other directive in this file is modified.
  --relax-mode {cell-fixed,stress-constrained}
                        How the cell responds to the imposed strain, via a %block Geometry.Constraints written to config_extra.fdf: 'cell-fixed' fixes all 6 Voigt stress components (cell stays exactly at the imposed strain; atomic positions still relax, via whatever MD.TypeOfRun/MD.Steps is already in --calc). 'stress-constrained' fixes only the imposed strain direction's own component(s) (plus anything touching a vacuum axis); every other periodic direction relaxes freely to zero stress. Either way, MD.VariableCell must be enabled in your own --calc for Geometry.Constraints to have any effect -- checked (not forced) in [4] of the report.
  -p PSEUDO_DIR, --pseudo-dir PSEUDO_DIR
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path. If given, the required pseudopotential for every species in the structure is copied into every generated folder, so it's immediately ready for SIESTA.
  --stdir STDIR         Direction of strain: x, y, z for uniaxial; xy, xz, yz, etc. for biaxial.
  --stmin STMIN         Minimum strain percentage (default: 0). Can be negative for compression.
  --stmax STMAX         Maximum strain percentage (default: 25).
  --step STEP           Strain step percentage (default: 1).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Top-level directory (default: strain_runs). The run folders go into its own '<output-dir>/<direction>/strain_<direction>_<val>/' subfolder -- so 2 different --stdir runs into the same --output-dir never mix their folders, and stb-strainAnalysis can point --dir at one direction's subfolder alone, or at <output-dir> itself with --compare to analyze every direction found under it.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum gap threshold in Ang used to detect which lattice axes are periodic vs. vacuum-padded (default: 10.0), same convention as stb-kgrid/stb-kpath. Straining a vacuum-padded axis is physically meaningless and is refused.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default), used only for the informational note about symmetry-equivalent directions (uniaxial only) -- never blocks the run. Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance -- a tighter value than the relaxation's own residual numerical noise can misdetect the true space group.
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry angle tolerance in degrees (default: 5.0, pymatgen's own default), same use as --symprec.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/strain_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-strain -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf -p dojo --relax-mode cell-fixed --stdir x --stmin -2 --stmax 2 --step 1
  stb-strain -s structure.fdf -c calc.fdf --relax-mode stress-constrained --stdir xy --stmax 5 --save-report

stb-strainAnalysis.help:
usage: stb-strainAnalysis [-h] -f FILE [--dir DIR] [--dimensionality {auto,3d,2d,1d}]
                          [--vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP] [--thickness THICKNESS]
                          [--cross-section CROSS_SECTION] [--yield] [-o OUTPUT_DIR]
                          [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Mechanical Properties from Stress-Strain Data (Stage 2 of stb-strain).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILE, --file FILE  Siesta output file (e.g., calc.out).
  --dir DIR             Directory to scan for 'strain_*' run folders (default: strain_runs). Accepts either stb-strain's own output layout -- point this at a single direction's own subfolder (e.g. strain_runs/x) for that direction alone, or at the top-level output directory itself to automatically compare every direction found under it -- or a flat directory of 'strain_*' folders.
  --dimensionality {auto,3d,2d,1d}
                        Physical dimensionality, controlling report units (GPa/N/m/nN) and how the cross-section for 1D Force mode is computed. 'auto' (default) tries to read a real, parseable .fdf structure file from the first strain folder found and classify it via vacuum-axis detection (same convention as stb-strain/stb-mlelastic); if none is found (the common, expected case for hand-built/legacy folders holding only a bare SIESTA .out), falls back to 3d.
  --vacuum-gap VACUUM_GAP
                        Vacuum-gap threshold in Ang, used only when --dimensionality auto finds a real .fdf structure file to classify (default: 10.0, matching stb-strain/stb-mlelastic).
  --thickness THICKNESS
                        Vacuum height (Z) for 2D conversion (Angstrom).
  --cross-section CROSS_SECTION
                        Physical cross-section area (Ang^2) of the wire/tube wall, only used when the run is 1D (--dimensionality 1d, or auto resolving to 1d), to additionally report a conventional Stress (GPa) -- there is no way to auto-derive this (unlike the 2D vacuum height), since a wire/tube wall thickness is a physical convention, not a cell property.
  --yield               Also report the 0.2% offset Yield -- a macroscopic-plasticity concept borrowed from metallurgy; off by default since a defect-free periodic crystal under affine DFT strain has no dislocation-nucleation mechanism to actually yield through.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write <direction>_curve.dat/.gplot (single direction) or comparison_curve.dat/.gplot (multiple directions) into with --save-gnuplot, and stb_strainAnalysis_report.txt into with --save-report (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_strainAnalysis_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write the curve data + a companion .gplot script (single direction: <direction>_curve.dat/.gplot; multiple directions: comparison_curve.dat/.gplot). Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview (the stress/force-strain curve, fit line, and peak) before finishing. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-strainAnalysis --file calc.out
  stb-strainAnalysis --file calc.out --dir strain_runs --save-report --save-gnuplot --view
  stb-strainAnalysis --file calc.out --dimensionality 1d --cross-section 45.2

stb-structural.help:
usage: stb-structural [-h] --file FILE --format {fdf,struct_out} --mode {list,mean}
                      [--list LIST] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--no-rdf] [--rdf-rmax RDF_RMAX]
                      [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Compute ECN and structural properties from a SIESTA structure file.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Path to structure file.
  --format {fdf,struct_out}
                        Input file format:
                          fdf:        SIESTA structure input (%block LatticeVectors etc.)
                          struct_out: SIESTA post-relaxation output (.STRUCT_OUT)
  --mode {list,mean}    Calculation mode: list or mean
  --list LIST           List of atom indices (comma-separated, 1-based). Example: 1,4,5,7 - Required for 'list' mode
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write rdf.dat and references.bib into (and stb_structural_report.txt, with --save-report) (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --no-rdf              Skip the radial distribution function g(r) (rdf.dat is not written).
  --rdf-rmax RDF_RMAX   Cutoff radius for g(r), in Å (default: 10.0). Larger values capture more coordination shells but take longer for large structures.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_structural_report.txt. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-structural --file structure.fdf --format fdf --mode mean
  stb-structural --file siesta.STRUCT_OUT --format struct_out --mode list --list 1,4,5
  stb-structural --file structure.fdf --format fdf --mode mean --save-report

stb-sts.help:
usage: stb-sts [-h] [--label LABEL] [--wfsx WFSX] [--geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE]
               (--point X Y Z | --xy X Y) [--height HEIGHT] [--axis {0,1,2}] --erange
               EMIN EMAX [--npoints NPOINTS] [--shift {none,fermi,manual}]
               [--fermi FERMI] [--bands-file BANDS_FILE] [--fermi-file FERMI_FILE]
               [--manual-value MANUAL_VALUE] (--sigma SIGMA | --fwhm FWHM)
               [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v]
               [--no-intro]

Simulated STS dI/dV(E) spectroscopy curve at a fixed tip point, from a full-BZ SIESTA .WFSX.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Auto-detects <label>.WFSX, falling back to <label>.selected.WFSX then <label>.bands.WFSX, and, unless --geometry-file overrides it, <label>.fdf (with its .ion/.ion.xml files alongside it). Mutually exclusive with --wfsx (not --geometry-file -- see its own help: the real fdf is very often NOT named <label>.fdf).
  --wfsx WFSX           Explicit path to the .WFSX file (alternative to --label).
  --geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE
                        Explicit .fdf geometry path (must have the basis's .ion/.ion.xml files alongside it). Required if --wfsx is used instead of --label; optional (and common) together WITH --label too, since the real fdf is often not literally named <label>.fdf (e.g. SystemLabel 'siesta' with the actual input file called calc.fdf) -- --label still auto-detects the .WFSX in that case, only the geometry source changes.
  --point X Y Z         Absolute Cartesian tip position (Ang).
  --xy X Y              In-plane Cartesian position (Ang); needs --height too. stb-stm-style: the tip sits --height Ang above the topmost surface atom along the vacuum axis.
  --height HEIGHT       Height (Ang) above the topmost surface atom, for --xy mode.
  --axis {0,1,2}        Surface-normal axis for --xy mode. Auto-detected from the geometry's vacuum padding if omitted and exactly one vacuum axis is found.
  --erange EMIN EMAX    Energy window (eV), relative to --shift's reference.
  --npoints NPOINTS     Number of energy samples (default: 400).
  --shift {none,fermi,manual}
                        Energy reference (default: none, i.e. raw eigenvalues as stored in the .WFSX). No vbm/cbm option here -- see the module docstring.
  --fermi FERMI         Fermi energy (eV) for --shift fermi. Highest-priority source if given.
  --bands-file BANDS_FILE
                        Companion .bands file to read the Fermi energy from, for --shift fermi.
  --fermi-file FERMI_FILE
                        Explicit SIESTA .out log to read the Fermi energy from, for --shift fermi -- an alternative to --bands-file for a run with no saved .bands file. Not assumed to be named after --label.
  --manual-value MANUAL_VALUE
                        Custom shift value (eV), required if --shift manual.
  --sigma SIGMA         Gaussian broadening standard deviation, in meV.
  --fwhm FWHM           Gaussian broadening full width at half maximum, in meV.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write sts.dat (and, with --save-gnuplot/--save-report, the .gplot script/report/references.bib) into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_sts_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a real .gplot script alongside sts.dat. Off by default -- this tool used to write the .dat file unconditionally but never wrote a .gplot script at all.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview before finishing. Off by default (replaces the old --no-plot, which was on by default).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-sts --label siesta --xy 0 0 --height 3.0 --erange -3 3 --sigma 50
  stb-sts --label siesta --point 1.2 0.7 12.0 --erange -5 5 --fwhm 100
  stb-sts --label siesta --xy 0 0 --height 3.0 --erange -5 5 --sigma 50 --shift fermi --fermi-file calc.out --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-supercell.help:
usage: stb-supercell [-h] -f FILENAME -d DIM [DIM ...] [-o OUTPUT] [-sp SYMPREC]
                     [--ml-relax] [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                     [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report]
                     [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Builds a supercell from a SIESTA FDF structure file.
Give -d 3 numbers for a diagonal supercell, or 9 for a full row-major matrix.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input structure file (.fdf).
  -d DIM [DIM ...], --dim DIM [DIM ...]
                        Supercell dimensions: 3 numbers for a diagonal supercell (e.g. 2 2 2),
                        or 9 numbers for a full row-major 3x3 matrix (e.g. 2 0 0 0 2 0 0 0 1).
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: supercell.fdf).
  -sp SYMPREC, --symprec SYMPREC
                        Symmetry tolerance in Angstroms for the before/after symmetry analysis (default: 0.01).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax the built supercell with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) before writing it out -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the cell -- any vacuum-padded axis always stays exactly fixed. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_supercell_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the input structure and the final supercell (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-supercell -f structure.fdf -d 2 2 2
  stb-supercell -f structure.fdf -d 2 0 0 0 2 0 0 0 1 -o big_cell.fdf
  stb-supercell -f structure.fdf -d 2 2 2 --ml-relax --save-report --view

stb-symmetry.help:
usage: stb-symmetry [-h] --file FILE --format {fdf,struct_out} [--symprec SYMPREC]
                    [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE] [--no-operations]
                    [--scan-symprec] [--compare-to PATH]
                    [--compare-format {fdf,struct_out}] [--write-refined FILENAME]
                    [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Analyze crystal symmetry (space group, Wyckoff positions, symmetry operations) from a SIESTA structure file.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Path to structure file.
  --format {fdf,struct_out}
                        Input file format:
                          fdf:        SIESTA structure input (%block LatticeVectors etc.)
                          struct_out: SIESTA post-relaxation output (.STRUCT_OUT)
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry-detection tolerance in Å (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default). Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance -- a tighter value than the relaxation's own residual numerical noise can misdetect the true space group; use --scan-symprec to check where a given structure's symmetry call is sensitive.
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry-detection angle tolerance in degrees (default: 5.0).
  --no-operations       Skip the full symmetry-operations list in the report -- keeps just the count in the SPACE GROUP section. Useful for high-symmetry structures where the full list is long.
  --scan-symprec        Also detect symmetry at a range of tolerances (1e-05, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1) and report where the space group changes -- reveals symmetry that's present but hidden by small numerical noise (e.g. from a DFT relaxation) at the --symprec you asked for. For a structure with exactly one vacuum axis, also scans the layer group; for one with all 3 axes vacuum-padded (an isolated molecule), scans the point group's own tolerance instead (both physically meaningful there, in their own report sections).
  --compare-to PATH     Also analyze a second structure file and report whether it shares the same space group -- e.g. compare a pre-relaxation .fdf against its post-relaxation .STRUCT_OUT to check whether symmetry survived. Analyzed with the same --symprec/--angle-tolerance as --file. If both structures have a detected layer group (e.g. comparing a 2D slab) or point group (e.g. comparing an isolated molecule), that's compared too.
  --compare-format {fdf,struct_out}
                        File format of --compare-to (required if --compare-to is given).
  --write-refined FILENAME
                        Also write the symmetry-refined structure (conventional cell, positions snapped to the detected symmetry) as this .fdf file inside --output-dir, with a header documenting the source file, tolerances, and which group it was refined against -- the same reduction stb-unitcell --mode refined uses. For a structure with exactly one vacuum axis, refines against the layer group instead; for one with all 3 axes vacuum-padded (an isolated molecule), symmetrizes it as a molecule instead (both physically meaningful there, unlike the 3D space group) -- skipped with an error for a wire (2 vacuum axes, no rod-group equivalent exists) or if the applicable detection failed.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write references.bib into (and stb_symmetry_report.txt, with --save-report) (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_symmetry_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) of the analyzed structure -- or, if --write-refined/--compare-to is also given, both structures side by side (page through frames in ase-gui) -- after the report is written. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-symmetry --file structure.fdf --format fdf
  stb-symmetry --file siesta.STRUCT_OUT --format struct_out --symprec 1e-4

stb-translate.help:
usage: stb-translate [-h] [-if {fdf,xsf,poscar,fhi,siesta,xyz,dftb,cif}] -i IN_FILE
                     [-of {fdf,xsf,poscar,fhi,xyz,dftb,cif,lammps}] [-o OUT_FILE]
                     [--out-dir OUT_DIR] [--dry-run] [--save-report]
                     [-cf {direct,cartesian}]
                     [--lattice-vectors AX AY AZ BX BY BZ CX CY CZ] [--view]
                     [--view-image PATH] [-v] [--no-intro]

File format converter using stb-translate.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -if {fdf,xsf,poscar,fhi,siesta,xyz,dftb,cif}, --in-format {fdf,xsf,poscar,fhi,siesta,xyz,dftb,cif}
                        Input file format (options: poscar, cif, siesta [SIESTA
                        STRUCT_OUT-style output], xyz, fhi, dftb, xsf, fdf [SIESTA
                        .fdf input file]). If omitted, inferred from --in-file's
                        name/extension.
  -i IN_FILE, --in-file IN_FILE
                        Path to the input file, or a glob pattern (e.g. '*.poscar')
                        matching several files for batch conversion.
  -of {fdf,xsf,poscar,fhi,xyz,dftb,cif,lammps}, --out-format {fdf,xsf,poscar,fhi,xyz,dftb,cif,lammps}
                        Output file format (options: cif, xyz, poscar, fdf, dftb, xsf,
                        fhi, lammps [LAMMPS data file, atom_style atomic, metal units
                        -- for handing a relaxed structure off to classical MD/force-
                        field runs]). Required unless --dry-run.
  -o OUT_FILE, --out-file OUT_FILE
                        Path to the output file. Required unless --dry-run, or in
                        batch mode (use --out-dir instead).
  --out-dir OUT_DIR     Output directory for batch conversion, used when --in-file is
                        a glob pattern matching more than one file. Each output is
                        named after its input's basename with the output format's
                        extension. Required in batch mode unless --dry-run; ignored
                        otherwise.
  --dry-run             Parse --in-file and print a summary (formula, atom count,
                        coordinate type, lattice vectors, cell volume, symmetry)
                        without writing any output file. --out-format/--out-file are
                        not needed.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to stb_translate_report.txt (next to
                        --out-file, or in --out-dir in batch mode), not just print it.
                        Off by default; ignored with --dry-run (no disk side effects
                        there regardless).
  -cf {direct,cartesian}, --coord-format {direct,cartesian}
                        Specify the output coordinate format (direct/fractional or
                        cartesian). If not specified, uses the input format or the
                        output format's default.
  --lattice-vectors AX AY AZ BX BY BZ CX CY CZ
                        The 3 lattice vectors in Cartesian Angstrom, required only for
                        XYZ input, e.g. --lattice-vectors 5.43 0 0 0 5.43 0 0 0 5.43.
                        Applied to every matched file in batch mode.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D viewer (ASE GUI) for the parsed
                        structure. Needs a display (local X11, or ssh -X/-Y). Runs as
                        the very last step, once every file has been read, written and
                        verified.
  --view-image PATH     Save a static 3D snapshot of the parsed structure to PATH
                        (e.g. structure.png). In batch mode, PATH is a directory
                        instead, and each file's snapshot is named after its stem.
                        Works without a display; can be used together with, or instead
                        of, --view. Runs as the very last step.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

stb-unitcell.help:
usage: stb-unitcell [-h] -f FILENAME [--mode {primitive,conventional,refined}]
                    [--symprec SYMPREC] [--angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE]
                    [--ml-relax] [--ml-relax-cell] [--model {small,medium,large}]
                    [--custom-model PATH] [--device {cpu,cuda}] [--save-report]
                    [--view] [-o OUTPUT] [-v] [--no-intro]

Finds the primitive/conventional unit cell of a structure, or refines it.
Uses pymatgen's symmetry analyzer (spglib) to detect the crystal's true
unit cell, which may be much smaller than the literal input cell (e.g. a
4-atom conventional FCC cell reduces to a 1-atom primitive cell).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f FILENAME, --file FILENAME
                        Path to the input structure file (.fdf).
  --mode {primitive,conventional,refined}
                        primitive: smallest possible cell (default).
                        conventional: standardized, usually larger, cell.
                        refined: conventional cell with atomic positions snapped to the
                        detected symmetry -- cleans up numerical noise from relaxations or
                        hand-built/CIF structures without changing which atoms are present.
  --symprec SYMPREC     Symmetry precision (default: 0.01, pymatgen's own default, matches stb-symmetry). Also used as the tolerance for the before/after symmetry analysis below. Loosen further (e.g. 0.02-0.05) for a structure relaxed with a looser force tolerance -- a tighter value than the relaxation's own residual numerical noise can misdetect the true space group.
  --angle-tolerance ANGLE_TOLERANCE
                        Symmetry angle tolerance in degrees (default: 5.0, pymatgen's own default).
  --ml-relax            Pre-relax the reduced unit cell with a MACE potential (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) before writing it out -- positions only by default. Off by default.
  --ml-relax-cell       With --ml-relax, also relax the cell -- any vacuum-padded axis always stays exactly fixed. Only valid together with --ml-relax.
  --model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 foundation model size for --ml-relax (default: medium).
  --custom-model PATH   Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --ml-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size.
  --device {cpu,cuda}   Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu).
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report (including the symmetry analysis) to stb_unitcell_report.txt. Off by default.
  --view                Open an interactive 3D view (via ASE) comparing the input structure and the final reduced cell (page through frames in ase-gui) after writing the output file. Needs a display. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output .fdf file name (default: unitcell.fdf).
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-unitcell -f structure.fdf
  stb-unitcell -f structure.fdf --mode conventional -o conventional.fdf
  stb-unitcell -f structure.fdf --mode refined -o clean.fdf
  stb-unitcell -f structure.fdf --ml-relax --save-report --view

Notes:
  - This operates on the literal 3D periodic cell as given. For slabs/2D materials/nanotubes with a vacuum direction, spot-check that the vacuum axis wasn't reoriented before using the output.
  - The output's atom order and coordinate origin are NOT guaranteed to match the input, in any mode -- spglib rebuilds the cell from the detected symmetry operations from scratch, free to pick any symmetry-equivalent origin/ordering. For highly symmetric structures (e.g. a monoatomic FCC lattice) even tiny input noise can flip which equivalent origin it picks. This is expected: the crystal is the same, just relabeled.

stb-wfdensity.help:
usage: stb-wfdensity [-h] [--label LABEL] [--wfsx WFSX]
                     [--geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE]
                     [--k-index K_INDEX | --k-point KX KY KZ] [--spin {0,1}] --band
                     BAND [--fermi FERMI] [--bands-file BANDS_FILE]
                     [--fermi-file FERMI_FILE] [--gap-tol GAP_TOL]
                     [--spacing SPACING | --shape NX NY NZ] [--axis {0,1,2}]
                     [--profile] [-p POS] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report]
                     [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Real-space |psi|^2 of one chosen (k, band) eigenstate from a SIESTA .WFSX file -> Gaussian .cube.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --label LABEL         SIESTA output label. Auto-detects <label>.WFSX, falling back to <label>.selected.WFSX (written by WriteWaveFunctions T + %block WaveFuncKPoints) then <label>.bands.WFSX, with a note -- and, unless --geometry-file overrides it, <label>.fdf (with its .ion/.ion.xml files alongside it -- NOT <label>.XV/.HSX, neither of which carries real orbital shapes). Mutually exclusive with --wfsx (not --geometry-file -- see its own help: the real fdf is very often NOT named <label>.fdf).
  --wfsx WFSX           Explicit path to the .WFSX file (alternative to --label).
  --geometry-file GEOMETRY_FILE
                        Explicit .fdf geometry path (must have the basis's .ion/.ion.xml files alongside it). Required if --wfsx is used instead of --label; optional (and common) together WITH --label too, since the real fdf is often not literally named <label>.fdf (e.g. SystemLabel 'siesta' with the actual input file called calc.fdf) -- --label still auto-detects the .WFSX in that case, only the geometry source changes.
  --k-index K_INDEX     0-based index into the .WFSX's own k-point order (default: 0 if neither --k-index nor --k-point is given).
  --k-point KX KY KZ    Match by k-point vector instead of index (same units as the .WFSX's own k, matched via sisl's read_eigenstate).
  --spin {0,1}          Spin channel (default: 0; must be 0 for a non-polarized calculation).
  --band BAND           Which band at the chosen k: an integer N (1-based), or 'vbm'/'cbm' (requires --fermi, --bands-file, --fermi-file, or an auto-detected .out log -- see below).
  --fermi FERMI         Fermi energy (eV) for --band vbm/cbm. Highest-priority source if given.
  --bands-file BANDS_FILE
                        Companion .bands file to read the Fermi energy from, for --band vbm/cbm. No correspondence guard against --wfsx like stb-fatbands has.
  --fermi-file FERMI_FILE
                        Explicit SIESTA .out log to read the Fermi energy from, for --band vbm/cbm -- an alternative to --bands-file for a run with no saved .bands file. Not assumed to be named after --label (see below).
  --gap-tol GAP_TOL     Energy tolerance in eV for VBM/CBM classification (default: 0.01). Same meaning as stb-bands/stb-fatbands.
  --spacing SPACING     Grid spacing in Angstrom (default: 0.3). Mutually exclusive with --shape.
  --shape NX NY NZ      Explicit grid shape (voxel counts), alternative to --spacing.
  --axis {0,1,2}        Axis for the optional --save-gnuplot slice/profile (default: 2).
  --profile             Write a planar-averaged 1D profile instead of a 2D slice, for the optional --save-gnuplot output.
  -p POS, --pos POS     Position (Angstrom) along --axis of the 2D slice (ignored in --profile mode). Default: auto-detected at the plane where the planar-averaged |psi|^2 is largest -- NOT the geometric center of the cell, which can land in empty vacuum for a structure whose atoms aren't centered along --axis (verified live: a real structure with atoms clustered near the cell boundary and vacuum in the middle had its default slice land on a point with ~1000x less density than the real peak, right at the atoms).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write the .cube (and, with --save-gnuplot, the slice/profile data + report/references.bib) into (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_wfdensity_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write a 2D-slice or (with --profile) 1D-profile .dat + .gplot pair of the |psi|^2 density. Off by default -- this tool used to write the .dat file (but never a .gplot script) unconditionally, opted out of via the old --cube-only flag (now removed).
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview (2D slice or 1D profile, matching --profile) before finishing. Off by default -- this tool previously had no matplotlib option at all.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Example usage:
  stb-wfdensity --label siesta --k-index 0 --band 1
  stb-wfdensity --label siesta --band vbm --fermi -4.2
  stb-wfdensity --label siesta --band cbm --save-report --save-gnuplot --view

stb-workfunction.help:
usage: stb-workfunction [-h] -l LABEL [-f FILE] [-g GRID] [-z {0,1,2}] [--fermi FERMI]
                        [--asymmetric-tol EV] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report]
                        [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [--no-intro] [-v]

Calculates the work function from a SIESTA electrostatic potential grid.
Reads <label>.VT (total potential, planar-averaged along --axis) plus the
Fermi energy from <label>.out (or --fermi to override), and locates the
vacuum plateau(s) in the averaged potential to compute Phi = E_vac - E_F.
If <label>.XV or <label>.fdf is present (and its cell matches <label>.VT's),
--axis is auto-detected from the structure's actual vacuum-padded direction
(core.kspace.detect_vacuum_axes, same mechanism as stb-kgrid/stb-mlrelax);
otherwise it defaults to z (2). An asymmetric slab (different terminations
on each side) genuinely has two different vacuum levels -- this is detected
automatically and reported as two separate work functions rather than one
physically meaningless average, along with the vacuum-level difference
(proportional to the surface dipole moment). Also reports the slab
thickness/vacuum size along the axis (when geometry is available), and
warns if a "vacuum" plateau has a systematic slope (a common symptom of a
missing dipole correction) rather than being genuinely flat.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -l LABEL, --label LABEL
                        System Label (required).
  -f FILE, --file FILE  Output file (.out). Default: label.out
  -g GRID, --grid GRID  Potential grid file (.VT recommended). Default: label.VT
  -z {0,1,2}, --axis {0,1,2}
                        Axis normal to surface (0=x, 1=y, 2=z). Default: auto-detected from label.XV/label.fdf if available and matching label.VT's cell, else z (2)
  --fermi FERMI         Manually force Fermi Energy (eV).
  --asymmetric-tol EV   Vacuum levels within this many eV of each other are treated as the same physical plateau rather than a genuinely asymmetric slab (default: 0.05)
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write references.bib into (and the report/data+gnuplot files, with --save-report/--save-gnuplot) (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_workfunction_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write workfunction_data.dat and workfunction.gplot (the planar-averaged potential profile, annotated with the detected vacuum level(s)/work function(s)). Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the potential profile before exiting. Off by default.
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit

Example usage:
  stb-workfunction -l graphene
  stb-workfunction -l slab --axis 2
  stb-workfunction -l slab --fermi -4.5 --save-report --save-gnuplot

stb-xrd.help:
usage: stb-xrd [-h] --file FILE --format {fdf,struct_out} [--wavelength WAVELENGTH]
               [--two-theta-range MIN MAX] [--top TOP] [--compare-to PATH]
               [--raw-experimental] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [--save-report] [--save-gnuplot]
               [--view] [-v] [--no-intro]

Simulates a powder XRD pattern from a structure.
Uses pyxtal's own diffraction engine (not pymatgen's) so the same dependency
already needed by stb-crystalcast covers this too.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --file FILE           Path to structure file.
  --format {fdf,struct_out}
                        Input file format:
                          fdf:        SIESTA structure input (%block LatticeVectors etc.)
                          struct_out: SIESTA post-relaxation output (.STRUCT_OUT)
  --wavelength WAVELENGTH
                        X-ray source: a known name (CuKa, CuKa1, MoKa, CrKa, FeKa, CoKa, AgKa, ...) or a wavelength in Ang as a plain number (default: CuKa, 1.54184 Ang).
  --two-theta-range MIN MAX
                        2-theta range in degrees to compute (default: 0 90).
  --top TOP             Only include the N strongest peaks in the saved data file (--save-gnuplot); default: include all of them. No effect without --save-gnuplot -- there's no console/report peak table anymore, see [2] DIFFRACTION PATTERN for a summary instead.
  --compare-to PATH     Compare the simulated pattern against an experimental one: a text file with 2-theta in the first column and intensity in the LAST column (any columns in between, e.g. d/h/k/l, are ignored -- so stb-xrd's own --save-gnuplot xrd_pattern.dat is a valid input too), whitespace- or comma-separated, '#' comments and blank lines allowed. If the file looks like a sparse list of discrete peaks rather than a continuous scan (e.g. a literature peak table, or this tool's own stick-pattern output), it is automatically Gaussian-broadened before comparing -- pass --raw-experimental to disable this and compare it unbroadened instead. Prints a similarity score (pyxtal's cosine-weighted metric, 0-1, higher is more similar); combine with --view for a visual overlay.
  --raw-experimental    With --compare-to, never auto-broaden a peak-list-looking experimental file -- compare it exactly as read. Off by default (auto-detection normally handles this correctly).
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write references.bib into (and the report/data+gnuplot files, with --save-report/--save-gnuplot) (default: current directory). Created if it doesn't exist.
  --save-report         Also persist the full run report to stb_xrd_report.txt. Off by default.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write xrd_pattern.dat (all peaks, pyxtal's own format) and xrd_pattern.gplot (a stick-pattern plot script) together. Off by default -- this tool used to write the data file unconditionally on every run; that's no longer the case.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview of the pattern (or, with --compare-to, an overlay of both patterns) before finishing. Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-xrd --file structure.fdf --format fdf
  stb-xrd --file structure.fdf --format fdf --wavelength MoKa --top 10
  stb-xrd --file relaxed.STRUCT_OUT --format struct_out \
      --two-theta-range 10 80 --view
  stb-xrd --file structure.fdf --format fdf \
      --compare-to experimental.dat --view --save-report --save-gnuplot

stb-xrdrank.help:
usage: stb-xrdrank [-h] [--input-dir INPUT_DIR] --experimental PATH
                   [--raw-experimental] [--wavelength WAVELENGTH]
                   [--two-theta-range MIN MAX] [--top TOP] [-o OUTPUT]
                   [--save-gnuplot] [--view] [--save-report] [-v] [--no-intro]

Ranks candidate structures by similarity to an experimental XRD pattern (Stage 2 - Analysis).
Part of the Structure Solution (XRD) workflow: reads every candidate structure
in --input-dir (default 'xrd_search', stb-xrdsearch's own default output
folder -- one candidate per subfolder, picking up a relaxed '*.STRUCT_OUT'
over the raw 'structure.fdf' if you've already run SIESTA there), simulates
each one's powder XRD pattern, and ranks them by similarity to an
experimental pattern -- a fast pre-screen for which candidate space group/
arrangement is most likely correct. Run it once on the raw candidates to
prioritize which to relax with real DFT, then again on the relaxed results
to confirm. Each comparison takes 10s of seconds (pyxtal's Similarity() has
no faster mode), so this can take a while for a large --input-dir.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --input-dir INPUT_DIR
                        Folder of candidate structures, one per subfolder (e.g. written by stb-xrdsearch as '<subfolder>/structure.fdf') -- defaults to 'xrd_search', stb-xrdsearch's own default --output-dir, so Stage 2 runs against Stage 1's output with no extra flag in the common case. If a subfolder also has a '*.STRUCT_OUT' file (from running SIESTA there), the relaxed structure is used instead of the raw one. Flat .fdf files directly in --input-dir are also accepted.
  --experimental PATH   Experimental XRD pattern: a plain text file with two columns (2theta intensity), whitespace- or comma-separated, '#' comments and blank lines allowed. If the file looks like a sparse list of discrete peaks (e.g. a literature peak table, or stb-xrd's own stick-pattern output) rather than a continuous scan, it is automatically Gaussian-broadened before comparing -- see --raw-experimental.
  --raw-experimental    Never auto-broaden a peak-list-looking --experimental file -- compare it exactly as read. Off by default (auto-detection normally handles this correctly; matches stb-xrd's own --compare-to flag of the same name).
  --wavelength WAVELENGTH
                        X-ray source: a known name (CuKa, CuKa1, MoKa, CrKa, FeKa, CoKa, AgKa, ...) or a wavelength in Ang as a plain number (default: CuKa, 1.54184 Ang).
  --two-theta-range MIN MAX
                        2-theta range in degrees to compute (default: 0 90).
  --top TOP             Only show/plot the N best-matching candidates (default: show all). The full ranking is always written to --output regardless.
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        Output ranking table file name (default: xrd_rank.txt). Always lists every candidate, regardless of --top. Gnuplot/report files (--save-gnuplot/--save-report) are written alongside it, in the same directory.
  --save-gnuplot        Also write the ranking as a gnuplot bar chart (xrd_rank.dat + xrd_rank.gplot) and the best candidate's simulated-vs-experimental pattern overlay (xrd_rank_top_sim.dat/xrd_rank_top_exp.dat + xrd_rank_overlay.gplot), all under a 'plot/' subfolder alongside --output. Off by default.
  --view                Show an interactive matplotlib preview (ranking bar chart + best candidate's simulated-vs-experimental overlay, one figure) before finishing. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the full numbered run report to xrd_rank_report.txt (written alongside --output). Off by default.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-xrdrank --experimental measured.dat
  stb-xrdrank --input-dir candidates --experimental measured.dat \
      --wavelength MoKa --top 5
  stb-xrdrank --experimental measured.dat --save-gnuplot --view --save-report

stb-xrdsearch.help:
usage: stb-xrdsearch [-h] --species SPECIES [SPECIES ...] --num-ions NUM_IONS
                     [NUM_IONS ...] --groups GROUPS
                     [--count-per-group COUNT_PER_GROUP] [--molecular]
                     [--volume-factor VOLUME_FACTOR] [--max-attempts MAX_ATTEMPTS]
                     [--seed SEED] [--ml-rank] [--keep-top-per-group N] [--mace-relax]
                     [--mace-model {small,medium,large}] [--mace-custom-model PATH]
                     [--mace-device {cpu,cuda}] [--mace-fmax MACE_FMAX]
                     [--mace-max-steps MACE_MAX_STEPS] [-c PATH] [--d3] [-s]
                     [-p PATH_OR_BANK] [--view] [--save-report] [-o OUTPUT_DIR] [-v]
                     [--no-intro]

Casts candidate structures across a set of space groups (Stage 1 - Prep).
Part of the Structure Solution (XRD) workflow: given a composition and a
list of space groups to try, casts --count-per-group random candidates in
each (by driving stb-crystalcast once per group), and puts each candidate
in its own folder as '<folder>/structure.fdf'. Optionally pre-relaxes every
final candidate with a MACE potential (--mace-relax, positions + cell) --
a fast cleanup of pyxtal's raw random placement, not a substitute for a
real SIESTA relaxation. By default, also generates the standard relaxation
calc.fdf (same as stb-inputfile -t relax) in every folder -- use --calc to
supply your own template instead -- and links pseudopotentials if
--pseudo-dir is given, so every folder is ready for a real SIESTA
relaxation as-is. Follow up with stb-xrdrank to score every candidate
against an experimental XRD pattern (either now, on these raw candidates,
or later, on your relaxed .STRUCT_OUT results).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --species SPECIES [SPECIES ...]
                        Element symbols in the structure, e.g. --species Ni O.
  --num-ions NUM_IONS [NUM_IONS ...]
                        Number of atoms of each --species, same order and count, e.g. --num-ions 4 8.
  --groups GROUPS       Comma- or space-separated space group numbers to try, e.g. '225,227,229' or '225 227 229'.
  --count-per-group COUNT_PER_GROUP
                        Random candidates to generate per space group (default: 1).
  --molecular           Passed through to stb-crystalcast: treat --species as whole rigid molecules instead of bare elements.
  --volume-factor VOLUME_FACTOR
                        Passed through to stb-crystalcast (default: 1.1).
  --max-attempts MAX_ATTEMPTS
                        Passed through to stb-crystalcast (default: 10).
  --seed SEED           Base random seed; each space group's batch uses seed+group so groups don't share identical draws (default: not seeded).
  --ml-rank             Passed through to stb-crystalcast: quickly relax each candidate with MACE-MP-0 and rank by energy (needs the optional 'ml' extra: pip install stb_suite[ml]) -- a fast, local pre-screen, not a substitute for the real SIESTA relaxation. Folders are then named '<group>_rank<N>' (most stable first) instead of by attempt order.
  --keep-top-per-group N
                        Only keep the N most stable candidates per group (requires --ml-rank; default: keep all --count-per-group candidates).
  --mace-relax          Pre-relax every FINAL candidate structure (positions + cell) with a MACE potential before generating calc.fdf -- a fast heuristic cleanup of pyxtal's raw random placement, not a substitute for the real SIESTA relaxation. The relaxed geometry overwrites each candidate's structure.fdf. Distinct from --ml-rank, which only relaxes (positions-only, transiently) to RANK/select candidates during casting -- the geometry it uses for that is discarded, not kept. Needs the optional 'ml' extra (pip install stb_suite[ml]).
  --mace-model {small,medium,large}
                        MACE-MP-0 model size for --mace-relax (default: medium). Ignored if --mace-custom-model is given. Only valid together with --mace-relax.
  --mace-custom-model PATH
                        Path to a custom fine-tuned .model file for --mace-relax, instead of a MACE-MP-0 foundation size. Only valid together with --mace-relax.
  --mace-device {cpu,cuda}
                        Device to run the MACE model on (default: cpu) -- used for both --mace-relax (here) and --ml-rank (passed through to the stb-crystalcast subprocess).
  --mace-fmax MACE_FMAX
                        Force convergence threshold for --mace-relax, eV/Ang (default: 0.05).
  --mace-max-steps MACE_MAX_STEPS
                        Maximum optimizer steps for --mace-relax (default: 200).
  -c PATH, --calc PATH  Custom calc.fdf template, copied (as 'calc.fdf') into every candidate folder -- should %include 'structure.fdf' by name. If omitted (default), the standard relaxation calc.fdf -- the same default stb-inputfile -t relax produces -- is auto-generated for every candidate instead (see --d3/--spin-polarized).
  --d3                  Auto-generate mode only (--calc not given): enable the DFT-D3 (Grimme) van der Waals correction in the generated calc.fdf. Rejected together with --calc.
  -s, --spin-polarized  Auto-generate mode only (--calc not given): enable spin polarization in the generated calc.fdf. Rejected together with --calc.
  -p PATH_OR_BANK, --pseudo-dir PATH_OR_BANK
                        Pseudopotentials source (optional): a bundled bank (dojo, virtual_vault) or a folder path. If given, the required pseudopotential for every species actually present in the cast candidates is copied into every candidate folder.
  --view                After generating, open one interactive 3D view (via ASE) paging through every candidate structure. Needs a display. Off by default.
  --save-report         Also persist the report to <output-dir>/xrdsearch_stage1.txt. Off by default.
  -o OUTPUT_DIR, --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Folder to write candidate structures into (default: xrd_search); each candidate gets its own '<output-dir>/<name>/'. Created if it doesn't exist; refuses to run if it already has any content, to avoid mixing batches.
  -v, --version         show program's version number and exit
  --no-intro            Do not show the introduction

Usage examples:
  stb-xrdsearch --species Ni O --num-ions 4 8 --groups 225,227,229
  stb-xrdsearch --species Na Cl --num-ions 4 4 --groups 225,221,62 \
      --count-per-group 3 -o candidates --pseudo-dir dojo
  stb-xrdsearch --species Na Cl --num-ions 4 4 --groups 225,221,62 \
      --count-per-group 5 --ml-rank --keep-top-per-group 1
  stb-xrdsearch --species Ni O --num-ions 4 8 --groups 225,227 \
      --calc my_calc_template.fdf --pseudo-dir /path/to/pps --view
  stb-xrdsearch --species Ni O --num-ions 4 8 --groups 225,227 \
      --mace-relax --mace-model medium --pseudo-dir dojo
